10// Suppress the spurious GCC/Eigen -Warray-bounds false positives emitted when
11// Eigen's vectorized reductions inline TMB's multi-dimensional array indexing
12// (e.g. the 5-D suitability(...) access in predation.hpp). The index math is
13// correct -- this is a well-known GCC/Eigen false positive, not a bug here. We
14// do this as a source pragma rather than a -Wno-array-bounds compiler flag so
15// CRAN's "checking compilation flags used" stays clean; real diagnostics (e.g.
16// -Wmaybe-uninitialized) still surface.
17#if defined(__GNUC__)
18# pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Warray-bounds"
19#endif

33/**
34 * @file ceattle.cpp
35 * @brief The CEATTLE objective function: configuration, population dynamics,
36 * predation, likelihood and report. The numbered section index is in the
37 * banner below; the process equations live in the headers this file includes.

40// List-of-matrices data structure: reads an R list() of numeric matrices into a
41// vector<matrix<Type>>. Used for the per-fleet survey-index covariance matrices
42// (Sigma) supplied when Index_loglike == "MVN"/"MVNORM" (the AMAK/ebswp DoCovBTS
43// covariance survey likelihood; see sections 8.2 and 13.1). Non-covariance fleets
44// pass a 1x1 inert dummy so the list is always length n_flt and can be indexed by
45// fleet code.
46template<class Type>
47struct LOM_t : vector<matrix<Type> > {
48 LOM_t(SEXP x) { // x = R list of matrices
49 (*this).resize(LENGTH(x));
50 for(int i = 0; i < LENGTH(x); i++){
51 SEXP m = VECTOR_ELT(x, i);
52 (*this)(i) = asMatrix<Type>(m);
53 }
54 }
55};

102 DATA_INTEGER(msmMode);
103 // 0 = single species mode (no predation mortality)
104 // 1 = Type II MSVPA based (sensu Holsman et al 2015)
105 // 2 = Type III MSVPA based
106 // 3-9 = NOT YET IMPLEMENTED (Holling Type I/II/III, predator interference,
107 // predator preemption, Hassell-Varley, Ecosim)
108 // DATA_INTEGER(est_diet); // Include diet data in the likelihood
109 DATA_IVECTOR(suitMode); // Estimate suitability
110 // DATA_INTEGER(avgnMode); // N used for predation function
111 // 0 = avgN_at_age
112 // 1 = N*exp(-Z / 2))
113 // 2 = N

118 // 1.2. Temporal dimensions
119 DATA_INTEGER( styr ); // Start year
120 DATA_INTEGER( endyr ); // End of estimation years
121 DATA_INTEGER( projyr ); // End year of projection
122
123 DATA_INTEGER( srr_mse_switchyr ); // The last year used to calculate average recruitment. Used for MSE runs.
124 DATA_IVECTOR( suit_styr ); // The first year (per predator species) used to calculate suitability averages.
125 DATA_IVECTOR( suit_endyr ); // The last year (per predator species) used to calculate suitability averages.
126 DATA_INTEGER( srr_hat_styr ); // The first year used to calculate stock-recuitment penalties or env-rec relationship.
127 DATA_INTEGER( srr_hat_endyr ); // The last year used to calculate stock-recuitment penalties or env-rec relationship.
128
129 int nyrs = projyr - styr + 1;
130 int nyrs_hind = endyr - styr + 1;
131
132 // suit_styr / suit_endyr are per-predator (offset to model-year indices below,
133 // once `nspp` is available).
134 int nyrs_srrmean = srr_mse_switchyr - styr + 1;
135
136 srr_hat_styr = srr_hat_styr - styr;
137 srr_hat_endyr = srr_hat_endyr - styr;
138 if(nyrs_srrmean > nyrs_hind){nyrs_srrmean = nyrs_hind;}
139 if(srr_hat_styr == 0){srr_hat_styr = 1;} // R_hat starts at year 1.
140
141 // 1.3. Number of species
142 DATA_INTEGER( nspp ); // Number of species (prey)
143
144 // Offset per-predator suitability reference years to model-year indices and
145 // count the averaging window length for each predator species.
146 vector<int> nyrs_suit(nspp);
147 for(int sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
148 suit_endyr(sp) = suit_endyr(sp) - styr;
149 suit_styr(sp) = suit_styr(sp) - styr;
150 nyrs_suit(sp) = suit_endyr(sp) - suit_styr(sp) + 1;
151 }

218 int max_nlengths = imax(nlengths); // Integer of maximum nlengths to make the arrays

220 // bins, which are the data bins whenever no pop_lengths is supplied.
221 int max_nlengths_pop = imax(nlengths_pop);

223 // -- 2.3c. First and last population bin in each data bin, per species. SS3
224 // forms sel(L) * P(L|age) at population resolution and bins the result, so
225 // pred_CAAL and the length compositions sum each data bin's run rather than
226 // applying one bin-average selectivity across it. The map is monotone, so the
227 // runs are contiguous; with one grid every run is a single bin.
228 matrix<int> pop_bin_lo(nspp, max_nlengths); pop_bin_lo.setZero();
229 matrix<int> pop_bin_hi(nspp, max_nlengths); pop_bin_hi.setZero();
230 for(int sp_i = 0; sp_i < nspp; sp_i++){
231 for(int d = 0; d < nlengths(sp_i); d++){ pop_bin_lo(sp_i, d) = -1; pop_bin_hi(sp_i, d) = -2; }
232 for(int lp = 0; lp < nlengths_pop(sp_i); lp++){
233 int d = pop_to_data_bin(sp_i, lp);
234 if(pop_bin_lo(sp_i, d) < 0) pop_bin_lo(sp_i, d) = lp;
235 pop_bin_hi(sp_i, d) = lp;
236 }
237 }

240 // nlengths_pop, so a finer grid would otherwise write past non_par_sel.
241 int max_bin = (max_age > max_nlengths_pop) ? max_age : max_nlengths_pop;

352 // -- 2.4.2b One-step-ahead (OSA) residual support
353 // `obsvec` is a flat vector holding every observation that enters the
354 // likelihood: log catch and log index (aggregate series), the bin counts of
355 // each comp / caal composition, and each stomach's diet composition. `keep`
356 // is the companion indicator used by TMB::oneStepPredict(): during normal
357 // model fitting it defaults to all ones, so the likelihood is numerically
358 // unchanged; oneStepPredict() toggles individual elements to compute
359 // one-step-ahead residuals. The `*_obsvec_idx` vectors give, for each row of
360 // the corresponding `*_obs` matrix, that observation's 0-based position in
361 // `obsvec` (for compositions, the start position of the row's bins), or -1
362 // when the row is excluded from the likelihood (e.g. projection years or
363 // non-positive observations).
364 // `osa_mode` (0 = normal fitting, the default) switches the composition /
365 // caal / diet branches to a proper, unweighted, keep-gated density suitable
366 // for OSA residuals; it does not alter the aggregate (catch/index) likelihood,
367 // which reads from `obsvec` identically in both modes.
368 // `osa_mode == 2` is mode 1 plus the conditional CDF terms
369 // oneStepPredict(method = "cdf") reads -- log F(x) gated by keep.cdf_lower and
370 // log(1 - F(x)) gated by keep.cdf_upper, alongside each keep-gated density.
371 // Both gates are zero except inside such a call, so the objective is
372 // unchanged; they are computed only in mode 2 so no other path pays for the
373 // `pbeta` / `pnorm` they cost. The Dirichlet-multinomial composition families
374 // have no CDF term (see comp_osa.hpp) and osa_residuals() keeps those fleets
375 // off this method.
376 DATA_VECTOR( obsvec ); // Flat observations for OSA residuals
377 DATA_VECTOR_INDICATOR( keep, obsvec ); // oneStepPredict keep indicator (defaults to 1 when fitting)
378 DATA_IVECTOR( catch_obsvec_idx ); // obsvec position for each catch_obs row (-1 = excluded)
379 DATA_IVECTOR( index_obsvec_idx ); // obsvec position for each index_obs row (-1 = excluded)
380 DATA_IVECTOR( comp_obsvec_idx ); // obsvec start position for each comp_obs row's bins (-1 = excluded)
381 DATA_IVECTOR( caal_obsvec_idx ); // obsvec start position for each caal_obs row's bins (-1 = excluded)
382 DATA_IVECTOR( diet_obsvec_idx ); // obsvec start position for each stomach's prey bins (incl. "other prey"); length n_stomach_obs (-1 = excluded)
383 DATA_INTEGER( osa_mode ); // 0 = normal fitting (default); 1 = OSA build (unweighted keep-gated comp/caal/diet densities); 2 = OSA build + conditional CDF terms for method = "cdf"
384 DATA_INTEGER( adreport_sel ); // 0 = no selectivity standard errors (default); 1 = ADREPORT log_sel_at_age; set via fit_control(selectivity_se =)
385 DATA_SCALAR( comp_offset ); // proportion offset added to comp/caal obs & pred before the multinomial; set via rearrange_data()/fit_control()
386
387 // -- 2.4.2c. Simulation switches (sim_mod(simulate = TRUE))
388 // Observations are always drawn; process error is a choice, so it is switched.
389 //
390 // simulate_state: which process. Slots 0 recruitment, 1 M, 2 growth,
391 // 3 catchability, 4 selectivity -- the same codes linkage_process uses, so a
392 // random linkage is gated by simulate_state(linkage_process(i)) with no
393 // translation. Default off: redrawing a process changes what self_test()
394 // measures, from recovering parameters to recovering a process. Recruitment
395 // covers init_dev too -- the initial age structure is recruitment from before
396 // styr, sharing R_sd and its bias correction.
397 //
398 // simulate_period: slot 0 the fitted window (0 < Year <= endyr), slot 1
399 // outside it. Only slot 0 is read, and only by the PROCESS draws, whose
400 // densities cover the hindcast alone. Observations are drawn in every period
401 // deliberately, because run_mse() splices the negative-Year rows back in as
402 // the next assessment's data. Slot 1 is reserved for a projection-period
403 // process draw and is inert today; sim_mod() exposes neither slot.
404 DATA_IVECTOR( simulate_state );
405 DATA_IVECTOR( simulate_period );
406

665 vector<Type> SPRFinit(nspp); SPRFinit.setZero(); // Estimated spawning biomass per recruit at Finit

667 matrix<Type> SBF(nspp, nyrs); SBF.setZero(); // Estimated spawning stock biomass at F = target (Accounts for S_at_age-R)
668 matrix<Type> B0(nspp, nyrs); B0.setZero(); // Estimated biomass at F = 0 (Accounts for S_at_age-R)
669 vector<Type> Flimit = exp(log_Flimit); // Limit F (FOFL proxy, e.g. F35%) on natural scale
670 vector<Type> Ftarget = exp(log_Ftarget); // Target F (max FABC proxy, e.g. F40%) on natural scale
671 vector<Type> Finit = exp(log_Finit); // Initial F for non-equilibrium age-structure
672 vector<Type> index_q_mult(index_q_beta.cols()); index_q_mult.setZero(); // Environmental design matrix for q
673 vector<Type> M1_mult(M1_beta.dim(2)); M1_mult.setZero(); // Environmental design matrix for M1
674 vector<Type> beta_q_tmp(index_q_beta.cols()); beta_q_tmp.setZero(); // Temporary vector to store Q beta parameters by species for matrix mult
675 vector<Type> env_q_tmp(index_q_beta.cols()); env_q_tmp.setZero(); // Temporary vector to store Q env data by year for matrix mult
676 vector<Type> beta_M1_tmp(M1_beta.dim(2)); beta_M1_tmp.setZero(); // Temporary vector to store beta parameters by species for matrix mult
677 vector<Type> env_M1_tmp(M1_beta.dim(2)); env_M1_tmp.setZero(); // Temporary vector to store env data by year for matrix mult

680 // -- 4.7. Survey components
681 vector<Type> index_q_sd(n_flt); index_q_sd.setZero(); // Vector of standard deviation of survey catchability prior
682 vector<Type> index_q_dev_sd(n_flt); index_q_dev_sd.setZero(); // Vector of standard deviation of time-varying survey catchability deviation
683 vector<Type> index_hat(index_obs.rows()); index_hat.setZero(); // Estimated survey index; mt or thousands of fish per the fleet's Observation_units
684 // Rejection bookkeeping for the natural-scale survey draws (sim_mod only).
685 // Counted per index_obs row, so a non-zero tries count marks the rows a
686 // rejection-capable branch drew: the untruncated "Normal" family and
687 // MVN/MVNORM, both of which have to redraw a non-positive index.
688 // "TruncatedNormal" draws by inverse CDF and never enters here. sim_mod()
689 // sizes the draw/density gap analytically from index_hat and index_sd
690 // rather than from these counts, which carry one draw per row per call.
691 vector<Type> index_trunc_tries_sim(index_obs.rows()); index_trunc_tries_sim.setZero();
692 vector<Type> index_trunc_rejects_sim(index_obs.rows()); index_trunc_rejects_sim.setZero();
693 // The marginal sd the draw itself used, per row, so sim_mod() can size the
694 // truncated mass as Phi(-index_hat/sd). Reported separately from index_sd
695 // because a covariance fleet draws from index_cov_mat and its index_sd
696 // holds whatever the (unused) Index_sd column happens to carry.
697 vector<Type> index_trunc_sd_sim(index_obs.rows()); index_trunc_sd_sim.setZero();
698 // The budget ACTUALLY applied to each row: the base constant on the univariate
699 // branch, and that scaled by the fleet's row count on the correlated one,
700 // which rejects the whole vector at once. Reported per row rather than as the
701 // bare constant, because the constant is not the number the correlated draw
702 // uses and quoting it would misstate the very thing the warning is about.
703 vector<Type> index_trunc_budget_sim(index_obs.rows()); index_trunc_budget_sim.setZero();
704 // Redraw budget, per row. Flat per row on the univariate branch; the
705 // correlated branch scales it by the fleet's row count, because a vector is
706 // rejected whenever any single row is non-positive and the joint rejection
707 // probability climbs with the number of rows. REPORTed below (under the _sim
708 // name every SIMULATE report takes, see section 5.12b) so sim_mod() quotes
709 // this value in its warning rather than carrying a second copy of it.
710 const int index_trunc_max_tries = 100;
711 // The observation sd the index likelihood actually used for each row, whichever
712 // of the three est_sigma_index routes supplied it. It is NOT a log: it is the
713 // sd itself, on the scale that fleet's Index_distribution works on -- a
714 // log-scale sd (unitless) for Lognormal, an ABSOLUTE sd in the units of the
715 // index for the natural-scale families. Named log_index_sd until 5.9.0, which
716 // was wrong on both counts.
717 vector<Type> index_sd(index_obs.rows()); index_sd.setZero();
718 vector<Type> index_analytical_sd(n_flt); index_analytical_sd.setZero(); // Concentrated (analytical) index sd used when Estimate_index_sd = 2; a log-scale sd, not a log
719 vector<Type> index_q_analytical(n_flt); index_q_analytical.setZero(); // Analytical catchability (not an sd) used when Catchability = 3; "AnalyticalArith" (7) has its own block at 8.2b
720 matrix<Type> index_q(n_flt, nyrs_hind); index_q.setZero(); // Estimated survey catchability //FIXME: extend out to full time-series
721 vector<Type> index_n_obs(n_flt); index_n_obs.setZero(); // Vector to save the number of observations for each survey time series
722
723 // -- 4.8. Composition data
724 // age_hat / age_obs_hat are indexed by AGE, whatever dimension the fleet's
725 // composition data are on: a length-composition fleet is built at age first
726 // and converted through the age-length transition. comp_obs is only as wide as
727 // the workbook's Comp_ columns, which for a length-only model is nlengths -- so
728 // sizing these from it wrote past the matrix whenever nlengths < nages. Eigen
729 // does not bounds-check in a release build, so that was a silent write into
730 // adjacent memory, not a crash. Width is the widest age index any composition
731 // row actually writes -- nages(sp), or nages(sp) * 2 for a joint-sex row
732 // (comp_ctl column 2 == 3) -- and never narrower than comp_obs, so no REPORTed
733 // object shrinks and none gains all-zero columns it never had.
734 // The species index is range-checked because this runs at allocation time:
735 // nothing between rearrange_data() and MakeADFun validates comp_data$Species,
736 // and a non-numeric one arrives here as NA_integer_. Reading nages() at that
737 // index would size the two matrices below from garbage.
738 int max_age_cols = static_cast<int>(comp_obs.cols());
739 for(int comp_row = 0; comp_row < comp_ctl.rows(); comp_row++){
740 int comp_row_sp = comp_ctl(comp_row, 1) - 1;
741 if((comp_row_sp < 0) | (comp_row_sp >= nspp)){
742 error("comp_data Species on row %d is not in 1..nspp", comp_row + 1);
743 }
744 int comp_row_cols = (comp_ctl(comp_row, 2) == 3) ? nages(comp_row_sp) * 2 : nages(comp_row_sp);
745 if(comp_row_cols > max_age_cols){ max_age_cols = comp_row_cols; }
746 }
747 vector<Type> n_hat(comp_obs.rows()) ; n_hat.setZero() ; // Estimated catch (numbers)
748 matrix<Type> age_hat(comp_obs.rows(), max_age_cols); age_hat.setZero(); // Estimated catch at true age
749 matrix<Type> age_obs_hat(comp_obs.rows(), max_age_cols); age_obs_hat.setZero(); // Estimated catch at observed age (accounts for ageing error)
750 matrix<Type> comp_hat = comp_obs; comp_hat.setZero(); // Estimated comp
751 matrix<Type> caal_hat = caal_obs; caal_hat.setZero(); // Estimated CAAL
752 array<Type> pred_CAAL(n_flt, max_sex, max_age, max_nlengths, nyrs); pred_CAAL.setZero(); // Predicted CAAL for each fleet

811 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
812 * 5. INITIAL CALCULATIONS //
813 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
814
815 // 5.1. DATA VARIANCE TERMS
816 R_sd = exp(R_log_sd); // Convert log sd to natural scale
817 sel_dev_sd = exp(sel_dev_log_sd) ;
818 index_q_sd = exp(index_q_log_sd) ;
819 index_q_dev_sd = exp(index_q_dev_log_sd) ;
820 Cindex -=1; // Subtract 1 from Cindex to deal with indexing start at 0
821
822
823 // -- 5.12b. SIMULATE LINKAGE RANDOM EFFECTS (sim_mod(simulate = TRUE))
824 // Time-varying recruitment, M, growth, q and selectivity are all written the
825 // same way -- a random linkage -- so all five draw here, before the deviations
826 // are gathered below and the processes read them.
827 //
828 // Each structure draws from the density that scores it in section 14.6:
829 // IID N(0, sigma) per slot;
830 // rw N(0, sigma) on first differences; slot 0 is left alone, being a level
831 // the density never sees and the map pins;
832 // ar1 stationary, sigma the MARGINAL SD (draw standardized, then scale).
833 // Slots are in ascending time order, so "next slot" is "next year".
834 //
835 // beta_linkage_re_drawn_sim marks which slots this call actually wrote. The
836 // reported deviation vector spans EVERY random linkage, drawn or not, so
837 // without the mask a caller cannot tell a simulated slot from one left at its
838 // fitted value and would score recovery on both.
839 SIMULATE {
840 vector<Type> beta_linkage_re_drawn_sim(linkage_re_sigma.size());
841 beta_linkage_re_drawn_sim.setZero();
842 if (log_sigma_linkage.size() > 0 && simulate_period(0) == 1) {
843 int n_slot = linkage_re_sigma.size();
844 int n_grp = log_sigma_linkage.size();
845
846 // Drawn only if EVERY row using the group names a process the caller asked
847 // for. Groups are per (process, param) in practice, so this matters only
848 // for a sigma shared across processes, where redrawing for one would
849 // quietly move the other.
850 vector<int> grp_used(n_grp), grp_draw(n_grp);
851 grp_used.setZero();
852 grp_draw.fill(1);
853 for (int i = 0; i < linkage_re_index.size(); ++i) {
854 if (linkage_re_index(i) < 0) continue;
855 int grp = linkage_re_sigma(linkage_re_index(i));
856 grp_used(grp) = 1;
857 // linkage_process also codes composition (5), which simulate_state does
858 // not cover because composition linkages carry priors, not random
859 // effects. Treat anything outside the five as "not asked for" rather
860 // than reading past the end of simulate_state.
861 int proc = linkage_process(i);
862 if (proc < 0 || proc >= simulate_state.size() || simulate_state(proc) != 1) {
863 grp_draw(grp) = 0;
864 }
865 }
866
867 for (int grp = 0; grp < n_grp; ++grp) {
868 if (grp_used(grp) == 0 || grp_draw(grp) == 0) continue;
869
870 // Rogers QAR1: the latent is measured by an observed covariate series, so
871 // redrawing it alone would leave the two describing different histories.
872 // Left as fitted; sim_mod() warns that it was.
873 if (linkage_re_obs(grp) >= 0) continue;
874
875 int len = 0;
876 for (int s = 0; s < n_slot; ++s) if (linkage_re_sigma(s) == grp) len++;
877 if (len == 0) continue;
878
879 vector<int> slot_of(len);
880 int j = 0;
881 for (int s = 0; s < n_slot; ++s) if (linkage_re_sigma(s) == grp) slot_of(j++) = s;
882
883 Type sigma = exp(log_sigma_linkage(grp));
884 vector<Type> re(len);
885 int st = linkage_re_struct(grp);
886
887 if (st == 1) { // rw / RandomWalk
888 re(0) = linkage_re_integrate(slot_of(0))
889 ? beta_linkage_re(linkage_re_slot(slot_of(0)))
890 : beta_linkage_re_pen(linkage_re_slot(slot_of(0)));
891 for (int t = 1; t < len; ++t) re(t) = re(t - 1) + rnorm(Type(0), sigma);
892 } else if (st == 2) { // ar1
893 Type rho = rho_trans(trans_rho_linkage(linkage_re_rho(grp)));
894 AR1(rho).simulate(re);
895 re *= sigma;
896 } else { // us / IID
897 for (int t = 0; t < len; ++t) re(t) = rnorm(Type(0), sigma);
898 }
899
900 for (int t = 0; t < len; ++t) {
901 if (linkage_re_integrate(slot_of(t))) {
902 beta_linkage_re(linkage_re_slot(slot_of(t))) = re(t);
903 } else {
904 beta_linkage_re_pen(linkage_re_slot(slot_of(t))) = re(t);
905 }
906 // A `rw` group keeps slot 0 at its fitted level -- the density never
907 // sees it -- so that slot is written but not drawn.
908 if (!(st == 1 && t == 0)) beta_linkage_re_drawn_sim(slot_of(t)) = 1;
909 }
910 }
911 }
912 REPORT(beta_linkage_re_drawn_sim);
913 }
914
915 // Every deviation in one vector, indexed by RE slot: integrated deviations live
916 // in beta_linkage_re, penalized ones in beta_linkage_re_pen, and
917 // linkage_re_slot gives the position within whichever holds it. With no
918 // penalized group this is an element-wise copy of beta_linkage_re, so those
919 // fits stay bit-identical.
920 vector<Type> beta_linkage_re_all(linkage_re_sigma.size());
921 for (int s = 0; s < beta_linkage_re_all.size(); ++s) {
922 beta_linkage_re_all(s) = linkage_re_integrate(s)
923 ? beta_linkage_re(linkage_re_slot(s))
924 : beta_linkage_re_pen(linkage_re_slot(s));
925 }
926
927 // THE _sim NAMING RULE, stated once here and referred to below.
928 // TMB never clears the report environment, so anything REPORTed inside a
929 // SIMULATE block stays visible in obj$report() for the rest of this object's
930 // life. Under the observed object's own name that would leave a random
931 // replicate readable as the data. Every draw is therefore reported under a
932 // name ending _sim, and the composition, CAAL and diet draws are written into
933 // separate copies (comp_sim, caal_sim, diet_sim) for the same reason.
934 SIMULATE {
935 vector<Type> beta_linkage_re_sim = beta_linkage_re_all;
936 REPORT(beta_linkage_re_sim);
937 }
938
939 // Effective linkage coefficient per table row. Fixed rows use their
940 // beta_linkage(i); random-effect rows (linkage_re_index >= 0) instead draw
941 // their deviation from the slot-space vector, which carries the density in
942 // row 20. The accumulators below are agnostic to the split -- they see one
943 // beta vector. With no RE rows every linkage_re_index is -1, so
944 // beta_linkage_eff is an element-wise copy of beta_linkage and the fit is
945 // bit-identical.
946 vector<Type> beta_linkage_eff = beta_linkage;
947 for (int i = 0; i < beta_linkage_eff.size(); ++i) {
948 if (linkage_re_index(i) >= 0) {
949 Type z = beta_linkage_re_all(linkage_re_index(i));
950 // Rogers QAR1: an observed ar1 latent enters the target scaled by an
951 // estimated effect size beta. Unobserved groups (the common case) keep
952 // the deviate as-is, so those fits stay bit-identical.
953 int grp = linkage_re_sigma(linkage_re_index(i));
954 if (linkage_re_obs(grp) >= 0) z *= beta_linkage_obs(linkage_re_obs(grp));
955 beta_linkage_eff(i) = z;
956 }
957 }
958
959
960 // 5.3. CATCHABILITY
961 // Environmental linkage offsets, one pass per link scale. Zero unless a
962 // q linkage was supplied, so models without one are unaffected.
963 matrix<Type> q_linkage_offset(n_flt, nyrs_hind); q_linkage_offset.setZero();
964 matrix<Type> q_linkage_offset_nat(n_flt, nyrs_hind); q_linkage_offset_nat.setZero();
965 matrix<Type> q_linkage_log_mult(n_flt, nyrs_hind); q_linkage_log_mult.setZero();
966
967 rceattle_apply_q_linkages(
968 q_linkage_offset,
969 /*link_code=*/ 1, // log-link rows -> log-scale tensor
970 linkage_process, linkage_param, linkage_species, linkage_sex,
971 linkage_age_bin, linkage_fleet, linkage_X_col, linkage_link,
972 linkage_X, beta_linkage_eff, n_flt, nyrs_hind);
973
974 rceattle_apply_q_linkages(
975 q_linkage_offset_nat,
976 /*link_code=*/ 0, // identity-link rows -> natural-scale tensor
977 linkage_process, linkage_param, linkage_species, linkage_sex,
978 linkage_age_bin, linkage_fleet, linkage_X_col, linkage_link,
979 linkage_X, beta_linkage_eff, n_flt, nyrs_hind);
980
981 rceattle_apply_q_linkages(
982 q_linkage_log_mult,
983 /*link_code=*/ 3, // exponential rows -> log-scale multiplier tensor
984 linkage_process, linkage_param, linkage_species, linkage_sex,
985 linkage_age_bin, linkage_fleet, linkage_X_col, linkage_link,
986 linkage_X, beta_linkage_eff, n_flt, nyrs_hind);
987
988 REPORT(q_linkage_offset);
989 REPORT(q_linkage_offset_nat);
990 REPORT(q_linkage_log_mult);
991
992 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
993 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
994 // Order follows SS3: an `exponential` row multiplies log q, and the
995 // index_q_dev deviate is added after that product, as SS3 applies its dev
996 // blocks after the env link. Inside it the deviate's effective sd would be
997 // sd * exp(beta * x), year-varying, against a constant index_q_dev_sd.
998 index_q(flt, yr) = exp((index_log_q(flt) + q_linkage_offset(flt, yr))
999 * exp(q_linkage_log_mult(flt, yr))
1000 + index_q_dev(flt, yr))
1001 + q_linkage_offset_nat(flt, yr); // Exponentiate
1002
1003 // Q as a function of environmental index
1004 if(est_index_q(flt) == 5){
1005 beta_q_tmp = index_q_beta.row(flt);
1006 env_q_tmp = env_index.row(yr) ;
1007 index_q_mult = env_q_tmp * beta_q_tmp;
1008 index_q(flt, yr) = exp(index_log_q(flt) + (index_q_mult).sum());
1009 }
1010 }
1011 }
1012
1013 matrix<int> r_sexes(diet_obs.rows(), 2); r_sexes.setZero();
1014 matrix<int> k_sexes(diet_obs.rows(), 2); k_sexes.setZero();
1015
1016
1017 // 5.4. MATURITY, Finit, AND SEX RATIO
1018 // -- for SSB derivation, not SPR
1019 matrix<Type> mature_females = maturity;
1020 for( sp = 0; sp < nspp ; sp++) {
1021
1022 if(initMode < 3 || initMode == 5){
1023 Finit(sp) = 0; // If population starts out at equilibrium set Finit to 0 (R_init and R0 will be the same). initMode 5 (OffsetEquilibrium) is an F = 0 equilibrium seeded by first-year recruitment.
1024 }
1025
1026 // Sex ratio for SSB derivation
1027 for( age = 0 ; age < nages(sp); age++ ) {
1028 if(nsex(sp) == 1){
1029 mature_females( sp, age ) = maturity( sp, age ) * sex_ratio(sp, age); // Multiply sex_ratio and maturity for 1 sex models
1030 }
1031 }
1032 }
1033
1034 // 5.5. OFFSETS
1035 // Each process gets two parallel offset tensors:
1036 // - `*_linkage_offset` log-scale additive contribution from
1037 // log-link rows (linkfn == 1, default).
1038 // Added to log_<param> before exp.
1039 // - `*_linkage_offset_nat` natural-scale additive contribution from
1040 // identity-link rows (linkfn == 0). Added
1041 // to the natural-scale parameter after exp.
1042 // Combine at the consume site as:
1043 // param_nat_yr = exp(log_base + log_offset) + nat_offset.
1044 // Catchability has a third tensor, `q_linkage_log_mult`, from
1045 // exponential-link rows (linkfn == 3), which MULTIPLIES the log
1046 // rather than shifting it; see 5.3 for the q form.
1047 // With no linkages, the tensors stay at zero so the result is
1048 // identical to the pre-linkage formula.
1049 //
1050 // - RECRUITMENT OFFSETS
1051 array<Type> recruitment_linkage_offset(nspp,
1052 int(RCEATTLE_N_REC_PARAMS),
1053 nyrs);

1056 nyrs);

1061 /*link_code=*/ 1, // log-link rows -> log-scale tensor

1066 linkage_age_bin,
1067 linkage_X_col,
1068 linkage_link,
1069 linkage_X,

1072 nyrs
1073 );

1176 // 5.6. RECRUITMENT PARAMETERS
1177 // Linkage offsets combine log-link (multiplicative) and identity-link
1178 // (natural-scale additive) contributions:
1179 // R0(yr) = exp(rec_pars(sp,0) + log_offset) + nat_offset.
1180 // TODO: a negative nat_offset can make R0, alpha or Beta non-positive; only hindcast R, R_hat and the penalty curve are floored (inst/dev/TODO-srr-multispecies.md, item 14).
1181 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1182 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1183 R0(sp, yr) = exp(rec_pars(sp, 0) + recruitment_linkage_offset(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_R0, yr))
1184 + recruitment_linkage_offset_nat(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_R0, yr);
1185 alpha(sp, yr) = exp(rec_pars(sp, 1) + recruitment_linkage_offset(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_ALPHA, yr))
1186 + recruitment_linkage_offset_nat(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_ALPHA, yr);
1187 Beta(sp, yr) = exp(rec_pars(sp, 2) + recruitment_linkage_offset(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_BETA, yr))
1188 + recruitment_linkage_offset_nat(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_BETA, yr);
1189 }
1190 }
1191
1192
1193 // 5.7. GROWTH
1194 // -- Rearange growth parameters. Log-link offset enters additively
1195 // on the log scale (multiplicative on natural K/L1/Linf/m);
1196 // identity-link offset enters additively on the natural scale.
1197 array<Type> growth_parameters(nspp, max_sex, nyrs, RCEATTLE_N_GROWTH_PARAMS); growth_parameters.setZero(); // K, L1, Linf, m
1198 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1199 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
1200 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1201 for(int par = 0; par < 4; par++){
1202 growth_parameters(sp, sex, yr, par) = exp(
1203 log_growth_pars(sp, sex, par)
1204 + growth_linkage_offset(sp, sex, yr, par)
1205 ) + growth_linkage_offset_nat(sp, sex, yr, par);
1206 }
1207 }
1208 }
1209 }
1210 REPORT(growth_parameters);

1306 // "sel_at_age" and "sel_at_length" modified via pass-by-reference
1307 // when "sel_at_length" is used, it is converted to "sel_at_age" using the growth matrix
1308 calculate_selectivity(
1309 nspp, // Number of species
1310 n_flt, // Number of fleets
1311 nyrs, // Total years
1312 nyrs_hind, // Hindcast years
1313 styr, // Start year
1314 nsex, // Vector of sexes per species
1315 nages, // Vector of max ages per species
1316 nlengths, // Vector of max lengths per species
1317 lengths, // Length bin boundaries matrix
1318 nlengths_pop, // Population length bins per species (= nlengths when no pop grid)
1319 lengths_pop, // Population length bin lower edges
1320 flt_spp, // Fleet to species mapping
1321 flt_sel_type, // Selectivity model type per fleet
1322 flt_varying_sel, // Time_varying_sel per fleet (picks NonParametricIntegrable's construction)
1323 flt_sel_dim, // Age or length based
1324 bin_first_selected, // Min bin selected per fleet
1325 flt_n_sel_bins, // Max estimated bins per fleet
1326 flt_sel_cap_bin, // Bin (0-based) at/after which realized non-par sel is capped flat (NonParametricPM)
1327 sel_norm_bin1, // Normalization control/bin 1
1328 sel_norm_bin2, // Normalization control/bin 2
1329 sel_norm_scope, // Normalization reference pooled across sexes?
1330 flt_sel_start_yr, // Per-fleet selectivity start year (0-based)
1331 emp_sel_obs, // Empirical observations matrix
1332 emp_sel_ctl, // Empirical control matrix
1333 log_sel_slp, // Logistic slope parameters
1334 log_sel_slp_dev, // Slope deviations
1335 sel_inf, // Inflection parameters
1336 sel_inf_dev, // Inflection deviations
1337 sel_coff, // Non-parametric coefficients
1338 sel_coff_dev, // Coefficient deviations
1339 avg_sel, // [Modified] Average selectivity
1340 non_par_sel, // [Modified] Unnormalized non-parametric selectivity
1341 log_non_par_sel, // [Modified] The same curve on the log scale, for the penalties
1342 sel_at_length, // [Modified] Final length-based selectivity
1343 sel_at_age, // [Modified] Final age-based selectivity
1344 growth_matrix, // Length to age transition matrix
1345 sel_slp_off, sel_slp_off_nat, // selectivity linkage offsets (log / natural)
1346 sel_inf_off, sel_inf_off_nat,
1347 sel_coff_off, sel_coff_off_nat,
1348 sel_apical_on, log_sel_apical, // per-sex apical height, only when a linkage names it
1349 sel_apical_off, sel_apical_off_nat,
1350 sel_dn6, sel_dn6_off, sel_dn6_off_nat, sel_dn6_ends // DoubleNormalSS3
1351 );
1352
1353 // -- Selected body weight (kg): sum_l P(l|a) s(l) w(l) / sum_l P(l|a) s(l),
1354 // SS3's "bodywt". A length-selective fleet takes the larger or smaller fish
1355 // of an age class, so its catch and survey biomass weigh that class by the
1356 // fish it selects, not by the class mean. Estimated growth only.
1357 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
1358 sp = flt_spp(flt);
1359 if(growth_model(sp) == 0 || flt_sel_dim(flt) != 1 || flt_sel_type(flt) == 0) continue;
1360 int wt_idx_sel = nspp * 2 + flt;
1361 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
1362 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1363 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1364 Type num = 0, den = 0;
1365 // Integrated over POPULATION bins: both the key and the curve live
1366 // there, so the selectivity weighting is applied at the resolution
1367 // the curve is defined on rather than to a bin average.
1368 for(int ln = 0; ln < nlengths_pop(sp); ln++){
1369 // The last bin takes the previous bin's width; a single-bin grid has
1370 // no neighbour to take one from, so it keeps the edge itself.
1371 Type lenmid = (ln < nlengths_pop(sp) - 1)
1372 ? (lengths_pop(sp, ln) + lengths_pop(sp, ln + 1)) / Type(2.0)
1373 : (nlengths_pop(sp) < 2
1374 ? lengths_pop(sp, ln)
1375 : lengths_pop(sp, ln) + (lengths_pop(sp, ln) - lengths_pop(sp, ln - 1)) / Type(2.0));
1376 Type p_sel = growth_matrix(wt_idx_sel, sex, age, ln, yr) * sel_at_length(flt, sex, ln, yr);
1377 num += p_sel * weight_length_pars(sp, 0) * pow(lenmid, weight_length_pars(sp, 1));
1378 den += p_sel;
1379 }
1380 // An age class the fleet does not select contributes nothing either way.
1381 weight_hat(wt_idx_sel, sex, age, yr) = num / (den + Type(1e-30));
1382 }
1383 }
1384 }
1385 }
