1414 // 5.12. FISHING MORTALITY and FSPRs
1415 // Outside the multi-species iteration loop: hindcast F needs no M. The
1416 // forecast arm below is provisional -- section 6.7 recomputes it once the
1417 // HCR has its reference points.
1418 F_spp.setZero();
1419 F_flt_age.setZero();
1420 F_at_age.setZero();
1421 Ftarget_at_age.setZero();
1422 Flimit_at_age.setZero();
1423 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++) {
1424
1425 sp = flt_spp(flt); // Temporary index of fishery survey
1426
1427 if(flt_type(flt) == 1){
1428 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
1429 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
1430 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
1431
1432 // Hindcast
1433 if( yr < nyrs_hind){
1434 F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) = sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * exp(log_F(flt, yr));
1435 }
1436
1437
1438 // Forecast
1439 if( yr >= nyrs_hind){
1440 // -- Apply HCRs
1441 switch(HCR){
1442 case 0: // No fishing
1443 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0;
1444 break;
1445
1446 case 1: // CMSY
1447 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp);
1448 break;
1449
1450 case 2: // Constant F
1451 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp);
1452 break;
1453
1454 case 3: // Constant F that acheives X% of SSB0
1455 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp);
1456 break;
1457
1458 case 4: // Constant Fspr
1459 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp) * Fmult(sp);
1460 break;
1461
1462 case 5: // NPFMC Tier 3 HCR
1463 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp); // Used Fabc of Ftarget_age%
1464 break;
1465
1466 case 6: // PFMC Category 1 HCR
1467 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp) = Flimit(sp) + QnormHCR(sp);
1468 break;
1469
1470 case 7: // SESSF Tier 1 HCR
1471 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp); // Used Fabc of Ftarget_age%
1472 break;
1473 }
1474
1475 // No projected F when the forecast is off or numbers-at-age are input (estDynamics > 0).
1476 if((forecast(sp) == 0) | (estDynamics(sp) > 0)){
1477 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0;
1478 }
1479 F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) = sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
1480 }
1481
1482 // -- Sum F across fleets
1483 F_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) += F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr);
1484
1485 // -- Calculate F target by age and sex for reference points
1486 Flimit_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) += sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * proj_F_prop(flt) * Flimit(sp); // account for time-varying sel
1487 Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) += sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * proj_F_prop(flt) * Ftarget(sp); // account for time-varying sel
1488 }
1489 }
1490 }
1491
1492 // F across fleets or species
1493 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
1494 // Hindcast
1495 if( yr < nyrs_hind){
1496 F_flt(flt, yr) = exp(log_F(flt, yr));
1497 F_spp(sp, yr) += exp(log_F(flt, yr)); // Fully selected fishing mortality
1498 }
1499
1500 // Forecast
1501 if( yr >= nyrs_hind){
1502 F_flt(flt, yr) = proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
1503 F_spp(sp, yr) += proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
1504 }
1505 }
1506 }
1507 }
1508
1509
1510 // 5.12.1. FISHERY SELECTIVITY AT AGE FOR THE INITIAL STATE (initMode 6 only)
1511 //
1512 // SS3's InitF convention: the initial equilibrium decays at Finit weighted by
1513 // fishery selectivity, so a size-selective fishery barely touches the young
1514 // ages. Mean over the species' fishery fleets in year 1; every other mode
1515 // leaves it at 1. Filled before the SPR reference points build Z_init, and so
1516 // SPRFinit, from it.
1517 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1518 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
1519 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1520 sel_init(sp, sex, age) = 1.0;
1521 }
1522 }
1523 }
1524 if(initMode == 6){
1525 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1526 int n_fsh = 0;
1527 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
1528 if((flt_type(flt) == 1) && (flt_spp(flt) == sp)) n_fsh++;
1529 }
1530 if(n_fsh > 0){
1531 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
1532 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1533 Type acc = 0.0;
1534 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
1535 if((flt_type(flt) == 1) && (flt_spp(flt) == sp)){
1536 acc += sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, 0);
1537 }
1538 }
1539 sel_init(sp, sex, age) = acc / Type(n_fsh);
1540 }
1541 }
1542 }
1543 }
1544 }
1545
1546
1547 // 5.13. SIMULATE PROCESS ERROR (sim_mod(simulate = TRUE), simulate_state)
1548 // Drawn before the dynamics consume the deviations, so the dynamics and every
1549 // observation draw downstream are automatically consistent with the simulated
1550 // process. WHAM keeps a second copy of its population dynamics (sim_pop) to
1551 // re-derive after the fact; that is unnecessary here, because these deviations
1552 // and their SDs are all parameters. rec_dev and init_dev are first read in the
1553 // initial-numbers block below, so this is the last point both are untouched.
1554 //
1555 // Each draw uses the density that scores it in section 13, bias correction
1556 // included, which is what makes simulated recruitment mean-unbiased.
1557 //
1558 // True when exactly one density scores rec_dev. False for the AMAK/Ianelli
1559 // configuration (srr_fun == 0 with srr_pred_fun > 0), where the stock-recruit
1560 // curve is fitted as a second penalty on the same deviation -- see the
1561 // recruitment draw below. REPORTed so sim_mod() can warn without re-deriving it.
1562 int rec_srr_single_density = !((srr_fun == 0) && (srr_pred_fun > 0));
1563 REPORT(rec_srr_single_density);
1564
1565 SIMULATE {
1566 // Masks marking which cells this call actually drew. Every deviation array
1567 // is REPORTed whole -- hindcast and projection alike -- so without these a
1568 // caller cannot tell a simulated cell from one left at its fitted value, and
1569 // a recovery statistic taken over the whole array scores both.
1570 matrix<Type> rec_dev_drawn_sim(rec_dev.rows(), rec_dev.cols());
1571 matrix<Type> init_dev_drawn_sim(init_dev.rows(), init_dev.cols());
1572 array<Type> log_M1_dev_drawn_sim(log_M1_dev.dim);
1573 rec_dev_drawn_sim.setZero();
1574 init_dev_drawn_sim.setZero();
1575 log_M1_dev_drawn_sim.setZero();
1576
1577 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1578
1579 // The density covers the hindcast only -- projection recruitment comes
1580 // from the harvest control rule or sample_rec() -- so the fitted window is
1581 // the only period this can honestly redraw.
1582 //
1583 // srr_fun == 0 with srr_pred_fun > 0 is excluded (rec_srr_single_density,
1584 // set above). That is the AMAK/Ianelli configuration, where section 13
1585 // scores rec_dev once through JNLL_REC_DEV and again through
1586 // JNLL_SRR_PENALTY over srr_hat_styr..srr_hat_endyr, so there is no single
1587 // distribution to draw from. Nothing is drawn and sim_mod() says why; the
1588 // full argument is in vignette("model-diagnostics").
1589 if(simulate_state(0) == 1 && simulate_period(0) == 1 && rec_srr_single_density){
1590 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
1591 rec_dev(sp, yr) = rnorm(-bias_adjust_proc*square(R_sd(sp))/2.0, R_sd(sp));
1592 rec_dev_drawn_sim(sp, yr) = 1;
1593 }
1594 }
1595
1596 // Initial abundance-at-age: the same process, for years before styr. The
1597 // gate is the density's own -- the equilibrium modes and
1598 // OffsetEquilibrium (5) fix init_dev and carry no penalty, so there is
1599 // nothing to draw. It also carries the rec_srr_single_density gate: a
1600 // fresh initial age structure sitting on top of the FITTED hindcast
1601 // deviations is not a history the model generated, so recruitment is
1602 // redrawn whole or not at all.
1603 if(simulate_state(0) == 1 && simulate_period(0) == 1 && rec_srr_single_density &&
1604 (initMode > 1) && (initMode != 5)){
1605 for(age = 1; age < nages(sp); age++){
1606 init_dev(sp, age - 1) = rnorm(-bias_adjust_proc*square(R_sd(sp))/2.0, R_sd(sp));
1607 init_dev_drawn_sim(sp, age - 1) = 1;
1608 }
1609 }
1610 }
1611
1612 // Natural mortality random effects. The IID modes are the AR1 code with
1613 // rho = 0, so one construction covers all six: draw a standardized AR1 and
1614 // scale by the marginal SD afterwards (SCALE()'s own simulate() is not
1615 // used). Note M1_dev_log_sd is the INNOVATION sd; Sigma_M is the marginal.
1616 //
1617 // The draw is BROADCAST along whichever dimension the mode holds constant --
1618 // modes 1/4 over years, modes 2/5 over ages. The map enforces that on the
1619 // parameter vector, but this block writes the expanded array, so writing
1620 // only the element the density reads would leave the rest at fitted values
1621 // and the deviation would not be constant as the model assumes.
1622 //
1623 // Sex is the same story. build_map() gives the sexes separate deviations
1624 // only at M1_model = 2; otherwise it maps male onto female, so they are one
1625 // parameter. num_re_sexes is therefore the number of INDEPENDENT draws, and
1626 // each is written to every sex sharing it -- write the female slice alone
1627 // and the two sexes would carry different M, which the estimation model has
1628 // no way to represent.
1629 if(simulate_state(1) == 1 && simulate_period(0) == 1){
1630 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
1631 int num_re_sexes = (M1_model(sp) == 2 && nsex(sp) > 1) ? 2 : 1;
1632
1633 if((M1_re(sp) == 1) || (M1_re(sp) == 4)){ // by age, constant over years
1634 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
1635 Type rho_M_a = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 0));
1636 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / (1.0 - pow(rho_M_a, 2)), 0.5);
1637 for(int s = 0; s < num_re_sexes; s++){
1638 vector<Type> M_re_age(nages(sp));
1639 AR1(rho_M_a).simulate(M_re_age);
1640 M_re_age *= Sigma_M;
1641 int sex_end = (num_re_sexes == 1) ? nsex(sp) : s + 1;
1642 for(int sex = s; sex < sex_end; sex++){
1643 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1644 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1645 log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, yr) = M_re_age(age);
1646 log_M1_dev_drawn_sim(sp, sex, age, yr) = 1;
1647 }
1648 }
1649 }
1650 }
1651 }
1652
1653 if((M1_re(sp) == 2) || (M1_re(sp) == 5)){ // by year, constant over ages
1654 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
1655 Type rho_M_y = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 1));
1656 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / (1.0 - pow(rho_M_y, 2)), 0.5);
1657 for(int s = 0; s < num_re_sexes; s++){
1658 vector<Type> M_re_yr(nyrs_hind);
1659 AR1(rho_M_y).simulate(M_re_yr);
1660 M_re_yr *= Sigma_M;
1661 int sex_end = (num_re_sexes == 1) ? nsex(sp) : s + 1;
1662 for(int sex = s; sex < sex_end; sex++){
1663 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
1664 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1665 log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, yr) = M_re_yr(yr);
1666 log_M1_dev_drawn_sim(sp, sex, age, yr) = 1;
1667 }
1668 }
1669 }
1670 }
1671 }
1672
1673 if((M1_re(sp) == 3) || (M1_re(sp) == 6)){ // by age and year
1674 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
1675 Type rho_M_a = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 0));
1676 Type rho_M_y = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 1));
1677 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / ((1.0 - pow(rho_M_y, 2)) * (1.0 - pow(rho_M_a, 2))), 0.5);
1678 for(int s = 0; s < num_re_sexes; s++){
1679 array<Type> M_re_a_yr(nages(sp), nyrs_hind);
1680 // Same argument order as the density in section 14 -- year on the
1681 // outermost dimension, age on the fastest-running one.
1682 SEPARABLE(AR1(rho_M_y), AR1(rho_M_a)).simulate(M_re_a_yr);
1683 int sex_end = (num_re_sexes == 1) ? nsex(sp) : s + 1;
1684 for(int sex = s; sex < sex_end; sex++){
1685 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1686 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
1687 log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, yr) = Sigma_M * M_re_a_yr(age, yr);
1688 log_M1_dev_drawn_sim(sp, sex, age, yr) = 1;
1689 }
1690 }
1691 }
1692 }
1693 }
1694 }
1695 }
1696
1697 // Reported so the draw can be checked directly. Inferring it from the data
1698 // it produces cannot tell "drew correctly" from "drew nothing, and the
1699 // observation error moved". Each goes out with its drawn-cell mask.
1700 matrix<Type> rec_dev_sim = rec_dev;
1701 matrix<Type> init_dev_sim = init_dev;
1702 array<Type> log_M1_dev_sim = log_M1_dev;
1703 REPORT(rec_dev_sim);
1704 REPORT(init_dev_sim);
1705 REPORT(log_M1_dev_sim);
1706 REPORT(rec_dev_drawn_sim);
1707 REPORT(init_dev_drawn_sim);
1708 REPORT(log_M1_dev_drawn_sim);
1709 }
1710
1711 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
1712 * 6. POPULATION DYNAMICS EQUATIONS //
1713 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
1714 // Start iterations for multi-species convergence (anything dependent on M)
1715 for(int iter = 0; iter < niter; iter++) {
1716
1717 // 6.1. TOTAL MORTALITY-AT-AGE
1718 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
1719 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
1720 // Element-wise: assigning a scalar to a vector would broadcast.
1721 for(int i = 0; i < M1_beta.dim(2); i++){
1722 beta_M1_tmp(i) = M1_beta(sp, sex, i);
1723 }
1724 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
1725 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
1726 // Matrix multiplication from sliced arrays doesn't work
1727 env_M1_tmp = env_index.row(yr);
1728 M1_mult = env_M1_tmp * beta_M1_tmp;
1729
1730 // M1_mult.sum() is LEGACY (scheduled removal: v4.5.0).
1731 // Carries the env effect from the soft-deprecated
1732 // M1_indices path. See "Scheduled removal" in NEWS.md
1733 // (4.1.0 section) for the full cleanup checklist.
1734 M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = exp(
1735 log_M1(sp, sex, age)
1736 + log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, yr)
1737 + M1_mult.sum()
1738 + M_linkage_offset(sp, sex, age, yr)
1739 ) + M_linkage_offset_nat(sp, sex, age, yr);
1740 M_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
1741 M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr);
1742 M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr);
1743 Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + F_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
1744 // S_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
1745 }
1746 }
1747 }
1748 }
1749
1750
1751 // 6.2. SPR BASED REFERENCE POINTS
1752 //FIXME - make time-varying?
1753 SPR0.setZero();
1754 SPRFinit.setZero();
1755 SPRlimit.setZero();
1756 SPRtarget.setZero();
1757 // Not defined under predation: M carries M2, which scales with predator
1758 // abundance, so spawning output per recruit would not be a property of the
1759 // prey stock alone. data_check() refuses the switch combinations that read
1760 // these downstream.
1761 if(msmMode == 0){
1762 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
1763
1764 int na = nages(sp);
1765 int term_yr = nyrs_hind - 1; // rates for a reference point are the terminal hindcast year's
1766 wt_idx_ssb = 2 * sp + 1;
1767
1768 // The four schedules. Flimit and Ftarget are selectivity-scaled and
1769 // read the terminal hindcast year; Finit is the flat F that generated
1770 // the initial age structure, so it is constant across ages and reads
1771 // year 0, weight included.
1772 // FIXME: time-vary sel in the forecast
1773 vector<Type> Z_unfished(na), Z_limit(na), Z_target(na), Z_init(na);
1774 vector<Type> wt_term(na), wt_first(na), mature_at_age(na);
1775 Type female_split = (nsex(sp) == 1) ? Type(1.0) : sex_ratio(sp, 0);
1776
1777 for(age = 0; age < na; age++){
1778 Z_unfished(age) = M_at_age(sp, 0, age, term_yr);
1779 Z_limit(age) = M_at_age(sp, 0, age, term_yr) + Flimit_at_age(sp, 0, age, term_yr);
1780 Z_target(age) = M_at_age(sp, 0, age, term_yr) + Ftarget_at_age(sp, 0, age, term_yr);
1781 Z_init(age) = M_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) + Finit(sp) * sel_init(sp, 0, age);
1782
1783 // Spawning output per TOTAL recruit, so the female fraction enters once:
1784 // spawn_output (5.7) carries maturity and the age-varying ratio for a
1785 // one-sex species, female_split the recruitment split (6.6) for a two-sex one.
1786 wt_term(age) = spawn_output(sp, age, term_yr);
1787 wt_first(age) = spawn_output(sp, age, 0);
1788 mature_at_age(age) = female_split;
1789 }
1790
1791 vector<Type> n_unfished = per_recruit_survivors(Z_unfished);
1792 vector<Type> n_limit = per_recruit_survivors(Z_limit);
1793 vector<Type> n_target = per_recruit_survivors(Z_target);
1794 vector<Type> n_init = per_recruit_survivors(Z_init);
1795
1796 SPR0(sp) = spawning_biomass_per_recruit(n_unfished, Z_unfished, wt_term, mature_at_age, spawn_month(sp));
1797 SPRlimit(sp) = spawning_biomass_per_recruit(n_limit, Z_limit, wt_term, mature_at_age, spawn_month(sp));
1798 SPRtarget(sp) = spawning_biomass_per_recruit(n_target, Z_target, wt_term, mature_at_age, spawn_month(sp));
1799 SPRFinit(sp) = spawning_biomass_per_recruit(n_init, Z_init, wt_first, mature_at_age, spawn_month(sp));
1800
1801 // Reported for inspection; slot order matches the four calls above.
1802 for(age = 0; age < na; age++){
1803 NbyageSPR(0, sp, age) = n_unfished(age);
1804 NbyageSPR(1, sp, age) = n_limit(age);
1805 NbyageSPR(2, sp, age) = n_target(age);
1806 NbyageSPR(3, sp, age) = n_init(age);
1807 }
1808 }
1809 }
1810
1811
1812 // 6.3. INITIAL RECRUITMENT
1813 // -- For beverton-holt, steepness and R0 are derived from SPR0
1814 penalty = 0.0;
1815 zero_N_pen.setZero();
1816 for( sp = 0; sp < nspp ; sp++) {
1817 // Under predation SPR is undefined: a hindcast curve takes R_init from the
1818 // free level R0(sp, 0) and reports steepness 0, skipping the cases below.
1819 if((msmMode > 0) & (srr_fun > 1)){
1820 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){ steepness(sp, yr) = 0; }
1821 R_init(sp) = R0(sp, 0);
1822 } else switch(srr_fun){
1823 case 0: // Random about mean (e.g. Alaska)
1824 // No compensation, so steepness is constant across years.
1825 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){ steepness(sp, yr) = 0.99; }
1826 {
1827 R_init(sp) = R0(sp, 0);
1828 }
1829 break;
1830
1831 case 1: // Random about mean with environmental linkage
1832 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){ steepness(sp, yr) = 0.99; }
1833 {
1834 R_init(sp) = R0(sp, 0);
1835 }
1836 break;
1837
1838 case 2: // Beverton-Holt
1839 {
1840 // Steepness for every year -- alpha may be time-varying through a
1841 // recruitment linkage.
1842 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1843 steepness(sp, yr) = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp)/(4.0 + alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp));
1844 }
1845 // Unfished recruitment implied by the curve, first year only. Filling
1846 // it for every year makes R0 an AD function of alpha and Beta across
1847 // the whole series, which feeds the reference-point and projection
1848 // recruitment calls and costs ~6x in fit time for a value that is
1849 // reported rather than used: Beverton-Holt recruitment is a function
1850 // of alpha, Beta and SSB, not of R0.
1851 R0(sp, 0) = (alpha(sp, 0) - 1.0/SPR0(sp)) / Beta(sp, 0); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
1852 R_init(sp) = (alpha(sp, 0) - 1.0/SPRFinit(sp)) / Beta(sp, 0); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
1853 // Same floor as R in 6.6.1: an identity-link alpha offset can make both negative.
1854 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R0(sp, 0) = posfun(R0(sp, 0), Type(1e-3), pen_R); R_init(sp) = posfun(R_init(sp), Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
1855 }
1856 break;
1857
1858 case 3: // Beverton-Holt with environmental impacts on alpha
1859 {
1860 // Steepness for every year -- alpha may be time-varying through a
1861 // recruitment linkage.
1862 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1863 steepness(sp, yr) = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp)/(4.0 + alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp));
1864 }
1865 // Unfished recruitment implied by the curve, first year only. Filling
1866 // it for every year makes R0 an AD function of alpha and Beta across
1867 // the whole series, which feeds the reference-point and projection
1868 // recruitment calls and costs ~6x in fit time for a value that is
1869 // reported rather than used: Beverton-Holt recruitment is a function
1870 // of alpha, Beta and SSB, not of R0.
1871 R0(sp, 0) = (alpha(sp, 0) - 1.0/SPR0(sp)) / Beta(sp, 0); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
1872 R_init(sp) = (alpha(sp, 0) - 1.0/SPRFinit(sp)) / Beta(sp, 0); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
1873 // Same floor as R in 6.6.1: an identity-link alpha offset can make both negative.
1874 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R0(sp, 0) = posfun(R0(sp, 0), Type(1e-3), pen_R); R_init(sp) = posfun(R_init(sp), Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
1875 }
1876 break;
1877
1878 case 4: // Ricker
1879 {
1880 // Steepness for every year -- alpha may be time-varying through a
1881 // recruitment linkage.
1882 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1883 { Type aS = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp); // kept positive under an identity-link alpha offset
1884 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_d = 0; aS = posfun(aS, Type(1e-3), pen_d); }
1885 steepness(sp, yr) = 0.2 * exp(0.8*log(aS)); }
1886 }
1887
1888 // - R at F0
1889 Type pen_rk = 0; // this species' floor penalties alone
1890 ricker_intercept = alpha(sp, 0) * SPR0(sp) - 1.0;
1891 ricker_intercept = posfun(ricker_intercept, Type(0.001), pen_rk) + 1.0;
1892 // will NOT overwrite when doing Ianelli penalty, srr_fun vs srr_pred_fun
1893 // Year 0 only: the Ricker intercept is kept positive by posfun(), which
1894 // accumulates a penalty into the objective, so it is evaluated once.
1895 R0(sp, 0) = log(ricker_intercept)/(Beta(sp, 0) * SPR0(sp)/1000000.0);
1896
1897 // R at equilibrium F
1898 ricker_intercept = alpha(sp, 0) * SPRFinit(sp) - 1.0;
1899 ricker_intercept = posfun(ricker_intercept, Type(0.001), pen_rk) + 1.0;
1900 R_init(sp) = log(ricker_intercept)/(Beta(sp, 0) * SPRFinit(sp)/1000000.0);
1901 zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_rk;
1902 }
1903 break;
1904
1905 case 5: // Ricker with environmental impacts on alpha
1906 {
1907 // Steepness for every year -- alpha may be time-varying through a
1908 // recruitment linkage.
1909 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1910 { Type aS = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp); // kept positive under an identity-link alpha offset
1911 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_d = 0; aS = posfun(aS, Type(1e-3), pen_d); }
1912 steepness(sp, yr) = 0.2 * exp(0.8*log(aS)); }
1913 }
1914
1915 // - R at F0
1916 Type pen_rk = 0; // this species' floor penalties alone
1917 ricker_intercept = alpha(sp, 0) * SPR0(sp) - 1.0;
1918 ricker_intercept = posfun(ricker_intercept, Type(0.001), pen_rk) + 1.0;
1919 // will NOT overwrite when doing Ianelli penalty, srr_fun vs srr_pred_fun
1920 // Year 0 only: the Ricker intercept is kept positive by posfun(), which
1921 // accumulates a penalty into the objective, so it is evaluated once.
1922 R0(sp, 0) = log(ricker_intercept)/(Beta(sp, 0) * SPR0(sp)/1000000.0);
1923
1924 // R at equilibrium F
1925 ricker_intercept = alpha(sp, 0) * SPRFinit(sp) - 1.0;
1926 ricker_intercept = posfun(ricker_intercept, Type(0.001), pen_rk) + 1.0;
1927 R_init(sp) = log(ricker_intercept)/(Beta(sp, 0) * SPRFinit(sp)/1000000.0);
1928 zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_rk;
1929 }
1930 break;
1931
1932 default:
1933 error("Invalid 'srr_fun'");
1934 }
1935
1936 // Steepness belongs to the stock-recruit curve, which under the Ianelli
1937 // configuration (srr_fun = 0 or 1, srr_pred_fun > 1) is estimated as a
1938 // recruitment penalty rather than driving the hindcast. The switch above
1939 // keys on srr_fun and so leaves steepness at the mean-recruitment
1940 // constant; derive it from the penalty curve's alpha instead. The
1941 // stock-recruit prior (slot JNLL_SRR_PRIOR) is evaluated on this, so
1942 // without it a prior on steepness has no parameter to act on.
1943 //
1944 // R0 is deliberately NOT re-derived here: recruitment in this
1945 // configuration is R0 * exp(rec_dev), so R0 keeps its estimated value.
1946 if((srr_fun < 2) & (srr_pred_fun > 1) & (msmMode == 0)){
1947 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
1948 if((srr_pred_fun == 2) | (srr_pred_fun == 3)){
1949 steepness(sp, yr) = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp)/(4.0 + alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp));
1950 }
1951 if((srr_pred_fun == 4) | (srr_pred_fun == 5)){
1952 { Type aS = alpha(sp, yr) * SPR0(sp); // kept positive under an identity-link alpha offset
1953 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_d = 0; aS = posfun(aS, Type(1e-3), pen_d); }
1954 steepness(sp, yr) = 0.2 * exp(0.8*log(aS)); }
1955 }
1956 }
1957 }
1958 // SPR0 is undefined under predation, so steepness is reported as 0;
1959 // data_check() refuses a steepness prior there.
1960 if((srr_fun < 2) & (srr_pred_fun > 1) & (msmMode > 0)){
1961 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){ steepness(sp, yr) = 0; }
1962 }
1963 }
1964
1965
1966 // 6.4. INITIAL ABUNDANCE AT AGE, BIOMASS, AND SSB (YEAR 1)
1967 //
1968 biomass.setZero();
1969 ssb.setZero();
1970 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
1971
1972 // Sex ratio at recruitment (1-sex model gets all R)
1973 if(nsex(sp) == 1){
1974 sex_ratio(sp, 0) = 1.0;
1975 }
1976
1977 // A free initial recruitment level, log scale (0 without an R_init
1978 // linkage, which leaves every expression below unchanged). Read at year 0
1979 // because the initial state is one year, and per species because that is
1980 // the stratum it is estimated on. Only the estimated branch below reads
1981 // it; a species with input numbers-at-age has no initial state to scale.
1982 Type init_level = recruitment_linkage_offset(sp, RCEATTLE_REC_R_INIT, 0);
1983
1984 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
1985 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
1986
1987 switch(estDynamics(sp)){
1988 case 0: // Estimated
1989
1990 // - Amin (i.e. recruitment).
1991 if(age == 0){
1992 // Year-1 recruitment is a recruitment year with its own deviate,
1993 // not part of the pre-hindcast level, so it stays at R_init.
1994 R(sp, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp(rec_dev(sp, 0));
1995 N_at_age(sp, 0, 0, 0) = R(sp, 0) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
1996 // The male slot only exists where some species is two-sex; a
1997 // one-sex species has sex_ratio 1 (set above), so this is 0 either
1998 // way, but the index itself is out of range when max_sex is 1.
1999 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2000 N_at_age(sp, 1, 0, 0) = R(sp, 0) * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2001 }
2002 // The equilibrium carries no recruitment deviation: it is the mean
2003 // level the deviates depart from. It DOES carry the initial level,
2004 // on every age including this one, so the equilibrium that
2005 // equil_catch_hat integrates sits at one recruitment level.
2006 N_eq(sp, 0, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp(init_level) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2007 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2008 N_eq(sp, 1, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp(init_level) * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2009 }
2010 }
2011
2012 // - Estimate as free parameters
2013 if(initMode == 0){
2014 if(age > 0){
2015 N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) = exp(init_dev(sp, age-1)) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2016 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2017 N_at_age(sp, 1, age, 0) = exp(init_dev(sp, age-1)) * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2018 }
2019 // No equilibrium underlies free initial numbers; Finit is 0 here
2020 // and an equilibrium catch is refused, so this is never fitted.
2021 N_eq(sp, 0, age) = N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0);
2022 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2023 N_eq(sp, 1, age) = N_at_age(sp, 1, age, 0);
2024 }
2025 }
2026 }
2027
2028 // - Equilibrium or non-equilibrium estimated as function of Rinit, Finit, mortality, and init devs
2029 // Finit is 0 for initMode 0, 1, 2 and 5; it is estimated for the
2030 // fished non-equilibrium modes 3, 4 and 6 (see section 6.1).
2031 if(initMode > 0){
2032
2033 // How far the initial age-structure sits off the mean-recruitment
2034 // equilibrium R0, on the log scale. Two sources, never both: the
2035 // free R_init level (SS3's SR_regime block on the year before the
2036 // hindcast, which SS3 shrinks at sigmaR/ave_age and Rceattle
2037 // leaves free -- put a prior on the coefficient to match SS3), or,
2038 // under OffsetEquilibrium (5), the first-year recruitment
2039 // deviation, which seeds the structure off
2040 // exp(rec_pars + rec_dev(sp, 0)) with init devs off (Cole
2041 // Monnahan / AFSC GOA pollock convention). An R_init linkage is
2042 // refused under mode 5. 0 under neither, i.e. no change.
2043 Type init_log_scalar = init_level;
2044 if(initMode == 5){
2045 init_log_scalar += rec_dev(sp, 0);
2046 }
2047
2048 // Sum M1 until age - 1. OffsetEquilibrium (5) uses the same
2049 // standard departing-age cumulative-M decay as the equilibrium
2050 // modes (Finit is 0 for mode 5).
2051 if((initMode == 1) | (initMode == 2) | (initMode == 3) | (initMode == 5)){
2052 mort_sum(sp, age) = 0;
2053 for(int age_tmp = 0; age_tmp < age; age_tmp++){
2054 mort_sum(sp, age) += M1_at_age(sp, sex, age_tmp, 0) + Finit(sp);
2055 }
2056 }
2057
2058 // SS3's InitF convention: the initial F is spread over ages by
2059 // the fishery's selectivity before it accumulates, so an
2060 // unselected young age carries almost none of it.
2061 if(initMode == 6){
2062 mort_sum(sp, age) = 0;
2063 for(int age_tmp = 0; age_tmp < age; age_tmp++){
2064 mort_sum(sp, age) += M1_at_age(sp, sex, age_tmp, 0)
2065 + Finit(sp) * sel_init(sp, sex, age_tmp);
2066 }
2067 }
2068
2069 if(initMode == 4){
2070 mort_sum(sp, age) = 0;
2071 for(int age_tmp = 0; age_tmp < age; age_tmp++){
2072 mort_sum(sp, age) += M1_at_age(sp, sex, age_tmp, 0);
2073 }
2074 mort_sum(sp, age) += Finit(sp);
2075 }
2076
2077 // -- 6.5.2. Age Amin+1:Amax-1 (initial abundance)
2078 if((age > 0) & (age < nages(sp) - 1)) {
2079
2080 if(sex == 0){
2081 N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_dev(sp, age - 1) + init_log_scalar) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2082 N_eq(sp, 0, age) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_log_scalar) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2083 }
2084 if(sex == 1){
2085 N_at_age(sp, 1, age, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_dev(sp, age - 1) + init_log_scalar) * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2086 N_eq(sp, 1, age) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_log_scalar) * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2087 }
2088 }
2089
2090 // -- 6.5.3. Amax
2091 if(age == (nages(sp) - 1)) {
2092
2093 // The plus group accumulates at its own total mortality. Under
2094 // initMode 6 the initial F reaches an age through that age's
2095 // selectivity, so the oldest age decays at M1 + Finit * sel --
2096 // SS3's equilibrium convention. Every other mode charges the
2097 // full Finit here, as it does in mort_sum above.
2098 Type Z_plus = M1_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp) - 1, 0) + Finit(sp) *
2099 ((initMode == 6) ? sel_init(sp, sex, nages(sp) - 1) : Type(1.0));
2100 Type plus_grp = 1 - exp(-Z_plus);
2101
2102 if(sex == 0){// NOTE: This solves for the geometric series
2103 N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_dev(sp, age - 1) + init_log_scalar) / plus_grp * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2104 N_eq(sp, 0, age) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_log_scalar) / plus_grp * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2105 }
2106
2107 if(sex == 1){
2108 N_at_age(sp, 1, age, 0) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_dev(sp, age - 1) + init_log_scalar) / plus_grp * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2109 N_eq(sp, 1, age) = R_init(sp) * exp( - mort_sum(sp, age) + init_log_scalar) / plus_grp * (1-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2110 }
2111 }
2112 }
2113 break;
2114
2115 case 1: // Numbers-at-age fixed exactly to NByageFixed (pop_scalar mapped to
2116 // NA in build_map so log_pop_scalar = 0 -> pop_scalar = 1.0)
2117 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, 0);
2118 break;
2119
2120 case 2: // Numbers-at-age scaled by a single estimated age-independent scalar
2121 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, 0);
2122 break;
2123
2124 default:
2125 error("Invalid 'estDynamics'");
2126 }
2127
2128 // -- 6.5.3. Estimate total biomass in year 1
2129 wt_idx_pop = 2 * sp;
2130 biomass_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, 0);
2131 biomass(sp, 0) += N_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, 0);
2132 }
2133
2134 // -- 6.5.4. Estimated initial female SSB
2135 wt_idx_ssb = 2 * sp + 1;
2136 // ssb_at_age(sp, age, 0) = N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) * pow(S(sp, 0, age, 0), spawn_month(sp)/12) * spawn_output(sp, age, 0); // 6.6.
2137 ssb(sp, 0) += N_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, 0, age, 0) * spawn_month(sp)/12) * spawn_output(sp, age, 0); // 6.6. ssb_at_age(sp, age, 0);
2138 }
2139 }
2140
2141
2142 // 6.5. HINDCAST NUMBERS AT AGE, BIOMASS-AT-AGE (kg), and ssb-AT-AGE (kg)
2143 penalty = 0.0;
2144 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2145 for(yr = 1; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
2146
2147 // Switch for srr (for MSEs if using Ianelli SRR method)
2148 int srr_switch = srr_fun;
2149 if(yr >= nyrs_srrmean){
2150 srr_switch = srr_pred_fun;
2151 }
2152
2153 // -- 6.6.1. Recruitment
2154
2155 // - Calculate recruitment.
2156 // Recruits arriving at age minage in year yr were spawned in yr - minage,
2157 // before styr while yr < minage. With no modelled SSB those years take
2158 // R_init * exp(rec_dev) -- equilibrium recruitment at F = Finit, exactly
2159 // what year 0 gets, so ages seeded from the same equilibrium agree.
2160 // Stock Synthesis treats the pre-start period the same way; WHAM avoids
2161 // it by fixing the lag at one year. Cannot fire at minage = 1.
2162 int spawn_yr = yr - minage(sp);
2163 int srr_use = (spawn_yr < 0) ? 0 : srr_switch;
2164 Type ssb_tmp = (spawn_yr < 0) ? Type(0.0) : ssb(sp, spawn_yr);
2165 // Pre-styr years take R_init, not R0(sp, yr): under a hindcast curve R0 is
2166 // set only at year 0 (derived, or the free level under predation).
2167 Type rec_mean = (spawn_yr < 0) ? R_init(sp) : R0(sp, yr);
2168
2169 R(sp, yr) = calculate_recruitment(srr_use, rec_mean, ssb_tmp, alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), rec_dev(sp, yr), SPR0(sp));
2170 // Under an identity-link recruitment offset the curve can go non-positive: keep R
2171 // positive (posfun, 0.001 barrier), charging the excursion to the zero-N row.
2172 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R(sp, yr) = posfun(R(sp, yr), Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
2173
2174 N_at_age(sp, 0, 0, yr) = R(sp, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2175 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2176 N_at_age(sp, 1, 0, yr) = R(sp, yr) * (1.0-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2177 }
2178
2179
2180 // -- 6.6.2. Ages beyond recruitment
2181 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
2182 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2183
2184 switch(estDynamics(sp)){
2185 case 0: // Estimated numbers-at-age
2186
2187 // -- Where Amin < age < Amax
2188 if(age < (nages(sp) - 1)) {
2189 N_at_age(sp, sex, age + 1, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr-1));// S_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1);
2190 }
2191
2192 // -- Plus group where age = Amax.
2193 if(age == (nages(sp) - 1)) {
2194 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age - 1, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1)) + N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr-1)); // S_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1);
2195 }
2196 break;
2197
2198 case 1: // Numbers-at-age fixed exactly to NByageFixed (pop_scalar = 1.0 via map)
2199 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, yr);
2200 break;
2201
2202 case 2: // Numbers-at-age scaled by a single estimated age-independent scalar
2203 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, yr);
2204 break;
2205
2206 default:
2207 error("Invalid 'estDynamics'");
2208 }
2209
2210 // A fresh accumulator per cell: the penalty is this cell's excursion alone.
2211 { Type pen_N = 0; N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = posfun(N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr), Type(0.001), pen_N); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_N; }
2212
2213 // -- 6.6.3. Estimate total biomass
2214 wt_idx_pop = 2 * sp ;
2215 biomass_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, yr );
2216 biomass(sp, yr) += biomass_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2217 }
2218
2219 // -- 6.6.4. Estimated female ssb
2220 wt_idx_ssb = 2 * sp + 1;
2221 /*
2222 ssb_at_age(sp, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * pow(S_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr), spawn_month(sp)/12.0) * spawn_output(sp, age, yr); // 6.6.
2223 ssb(sp, yr) += ssb_at_age(sp, age, yr);
2224 */
2225 ssb(sp, yr) += N_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0) * spawn_output(sp, age, yr); // 6.6.
2226 }
2227 }
2228 }
2229
2230
2231 // 6.6. DEPLETION BASED BIOMASS REFERENCE POINTS (i.e. SB0 and dynamic SB0)
2232 // -- calculate mean recruitment
2233 // FIXME: may want specified year ranges
2234 avg_R.setZero();
2235 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2236 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_srrmean; yr++) {
2237 avg_R(sp) += R(sp, yr)/Type(nyrs_srrmean); // Update mean rec
2238 }
2239 }
2240
2241 // -- Calc biomass_depletion based BRPs
2242 NByage0.setZero();
2243 NByageF.setZero();
2244 N_at_age_dBF.setZero();
2245 N_at_age_dB0.setZero();
2246 B0.setZero();
2247 SB0.setZero();
2248 SBF.setZero();
2249 DynamicB0.setZero();
2250 DynamicSB0.setZero();
2251 DynamicSBF.setZero();
2252 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2253 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
2254
2255 // - Year 1
2256 // -- Initial abundance-at-age is the same as the hindcast
2257 if(yr == 0){
2258 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2259 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
2260 NByage0(sp, sex, age , 0) = NByageF(sp, sex, age , 0) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, 0) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, 0) = N_at_age(sp,sex,age,0);
2261 }
2262 }
2263 }
2264
2265 // - Recruitment Year > 1
2266 if(yr > 0){
2267 // - Option 1a: Use mean rec
2268 if((proj_mean_rec == 1) & (srr_pred_fun < 2)){
2269 // Equilibrium RPs used mean rec across all years
2270 NByage0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = avg_R(sp);
2271 NByageF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = avg_R(sp);
2272
2273 // Dynamic RPs use mean rec for forecast and observed rec for hindcast
2274 // LEGACY (scheduled removal: v4.5.0). Use relationship below
2275 if(yr < nyrs_hind){
2276 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = R(sp, yr); // Hindcast use observed R
2277 }
2278 if(yr >= nyrs_hind){
2279 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = exp(log(avg_R(sp)) + rec_dev(sp, yr)); // Projections use mean R given bias in R0
2280 }
2281 }
2282
2283
2284 // - Option 2: Use SRR
2285 // Reached whenever a curve exists, not only when the projection runs
2286 // on it. proj_mean_rec = 1 (the build_srr() default) with an estimated
2287 // curve otherwise matched NEITHER arm -- Option 1a excludes
2288 // srr_pred_fun >= 2 -- and reference-point recruitment stayed 0 for
2289 // every year after the first, so SB0 decayed towards zero and
2290 // SB0(sp, nyrs-1) is what HCR 5 and 6 read as the depletion reference.
2291 // Projection recruitment itself is unaffected: that switch is read
2292 // separately in 6.8, so mean-recruitment projections stay mean.
2293 if((proj_mean_rec == 0) | (srr_pred_fun >= 2)){
2294
2295 // - Equilibrium reference points (No recruitment deviation: pass Type(0.0))
2296 // Equilibrium spawning biomass exists every year; yr < minage reads the
2297 // first year's value so the lag stays in bounds.
2298 int rp_yr = yr - minage(sp);
2299 if(rp_yr < 0){ rp_yr = 0; }
2300
2301 // TODO: not floored under an identity-link recruitment offset, so SB0, SBF and B0 can go negative (inst/dev/TODO-srr-multispecies.md, item 14).
2302 NByage0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = calculate_recruitment(srr_pred_fun, R0(sp, yr), SB0(sp, rp_yr), alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), Type(0.0), SPR0(sp));
2303 NByageF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = calculate_recruitment(srr_pred_fun, R0(sp, yr), SBF(sp, rp_yr), alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), Type(0.0), SPR0(sp));
2304
2305 // - Dynamic reference points (Includes annual recruitment deviation: pass rdev)
2306 // Cohorts spawned before the first year take the hindcast's realized R
2307 // (R_init with its deviation), so both runs start from the same cohorts.
2308 Type rdev = rec_dev(sp, yr);
2309 if(yr < minage(sp)){
2310 Type R_early = (yr < nyrs_hind) ? R(sp, yr) : R_init(sp) * exp(rdev);
2311 N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = R_early;
2312 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = R_early;
2313 } else {
2314 // Under the Ianelli form the hindcast is on mean recruitment until srr_mse_switchyr, so rec_dev
2315 // there is measured from R0; the curve takes the realized deviation from it, log R - log R_hat.
2316 if((srr_fun != srr_pred_fun) & (yr < nyrs_srrmean)){
2317 Type R_curve = calculate_recruitment(srr_pred_fun, R0(sp, yr), ssb(sp, rp_yr), alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), Type(0.0), SPR0(sp));
2318 // Same floor as R in 6.6.1, for an identity-link offset that makes the curve non-positive.
2319 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R_curve = posfun(R_curve, Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
2320 rdev = log(R(sp, yr)) - log(R_curve);
2321 }
2322 // TODO: dynamic-B0 recruitment is not floored under an identity-link offset (inst/dev/TODO-srr-multispecies.md, item 14).
2323 N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = calculate_recruitment(srr_pred_fun, R0(sp, yr), DynamicSB0(sp, rp_yr), alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), rdev, SPR0(sp));
2324 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = calculate_recruitment(srr_pred_fun, R0(sp, yr), DynamicSBF(sp, rp_yr), alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), rdev, SPR0(sp));
2325 }
2326
2327 } // End recruitment switch
2328
2329 // Account for sex ratio. The male slot only exists where some species
2330 // is two-sex; a one-sex species has sex_ratio 1 (set in 6.4), so the
2331 // male value is 0 either way, but the index is out of range when
2332 // max_sex is 1.
2333 NByage0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = NByage0(sp, 0, 0, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0); // Females
2334 NByageF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = NByageF(sp, 0, 0, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0); // Females
2335 N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0); // Females
2336 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0); // Females
2337
2338 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2339 // Males (divide by sex_ratio because we multiplied in the lines above)
2340 NByage0(sp, 1, 0, yr) = NByage0(sp, 0, 0, yr) / sex_ratio(sp, 0) * (1.0-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2341 NByageF(sp, 1, 0, yr) = NByageF(sp, 0, 0, yr) / sex_ratio(sp, 0) * (1.0-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2342 N_at_age_dB0(sp, 1, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, 0, yr) / sex_ratio(sp, 0) * (1.0-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2343 N_at_age_dBF(sp, 1, 0, yr) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, 0, yr) / sex_ratio(sp, 0) * (1.0-sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2344 }
2345
2346
2347 // N-at-age year > 1
2348 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2349 for(age = 1; age < nages(sp)-1; age++) {
2350 NByage0(sp, sex, age, yr) = NByage0(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1)); // F = 0
2351
2352 NByageF(sp, sex, age, yr) = NByageF(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1)); // F = target
2353
2354 // No 0.001 floor here: the hindcast's is a numerical guard, and dynamic B0 must not
2355 // assume a stock that fell to it would not have crashed without fishing.
2356 N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1) * exp(-M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age-1, yr - 1)); // F = 0
2357
2358 N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1) * exp(-M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age-1, yr - 1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1)); // F = Ftarget
2359 }
2360
2361 // Plus group -- No fishing
2362 NByage0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr) = NByage0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1)) + NByage0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1));
2363
2364 NByageF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr) = NByageF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr-1)) + NByageF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr-1));
2365
2366 N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1)) + N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1));
2367
2368 N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr - 1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-2, yr-1)) + N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) * exp(-M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr - 1) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, nages(sp)-1, yr-1));
2369
2370 }
2371 }
2372
2373 // A species with input numbers-at-age (estDynamics > 0) keeps them in the
2374 // dynamic runs; projection years are read directly, as 6.8 fills N later.
2375 if(estDynamics(sp) > 0){
2376 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2377 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
2378 Type n_fixed = (yr < nyrs_hind) ? N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) :
2379 pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, yr);
2380 N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr) = n_fixed;
2381 N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) = n_fixed;
2382 }
2383 }
2384 }
2385
2386
2387 // Calculate Dynamic SB0 and SB at F target
2388 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2389
2390 wt_idx_ssb = 2 * sp + 1;
2391 // Multispecies: M_at_age carries the projection's realized M2. The one rule
2392 // that reads SBF, NPFMC (HCR 5), is refused there; SB0 is replaced by MSSB0 below.
2393 SB0(sp, yr) += NByage0(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_output(sp, age, nyrs_hind - 1) * exp(-M_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0);
2394 SBF(sp, yr) += NByageF(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_output(sp, age, nyrs_hind - 1) * exp(-(M_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) + Ftarget_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr)) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0);
2395 DynamicSB0(sp, yr) += N_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_output(sp, age, yr) * exp(-M_at_age_dB0(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0);
2396 DynamicSBF(sp, yr) += N_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_output(sp, age, yr) * exp(-(M_at_age_dBF(sp, 0, age, yr) + Ftarget_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr)) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0);
2397
2398 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2399
2400 wt_idx_pop = 2 * sp;
2401 B0(sp, yr) += NByage0(sp, sex, age, yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, nyrs_hind - 1 );
2402 DynamicB0(sp, yr) += N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex,age, yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, yr );
2403 }
2404 }
2405
2406
2407 // Input SB0 (if running in multi-species mode)
2408 if(msmMode > 0){
2409 SB0(sp, yr) = MSSB0(sp);
2410 B0(sp, yr) = MSB0(sp);
2411 }
2412 }
2413 }
2414
2415 // 6.7-6.9. FORECAST NUMBERS AT AGE, BIOMASS-AT-AGE (kg), and ssb-AT-AGE (kg)
2416 // Includes Harvest Control Rules
2417 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2418 for(yr = nyrs_hind; yr < nyrs; yr++){
2419
2420 // 6.7. HARVEST CONTROL RULES FOR PROJECTION
2421 // Equilibrium or dynamic reference points (i.e. SB0 or dynamic SB0)
2422 Type ref_SB0 = (DynamicHCR == 1) ? DynamicSB0(sp, yr-1) : SB0(sp, nyrs-1);
2423 Type ref_SBF = (DynamicHCR == 1) ? DynamicSBF(sp, yr-1) : SBF(sp, nyrs-1);
2424
2425 switch(HCR){
2426 case 0: // No fishing
2427 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0.0;
2428 break;
2429
2430 case 1: // CMSY
2431 // proj_F(sp, yr) retains its incoming value
2432 break;
2433
2434 case 2: // Constant F
2435 // proj_F(sp, yr) retains its incoming value
2436 break;
2437
2438 case 3: // Constant F to acheive X% of SB0
2439 // proj_F(sp, yr) retains its incoming value
2440 break;
2441
2442 case 4: // Constant Fspr with multiplier
2443 // proj_F(sp, yr) retains its incoming value
2444 break;
2445
2446 case 5: // NPFMC Tier 3 HCR
2447 if(ssb(sp, yr-1) < ref_SBF){
2448 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp) * (((ssb(sp, yr-1)/ref_SBF)-Alpha(sp))/(1-Alpha(sp))); // Used Fabc of FtargetSPR%
2449 }
2450 if((ssb(sp, nyrs_hind-1) < ref_SB0 * Plimit(sp)) || (ssb(sp, yr-1) / ref_SBF < Alpha(sp))){ // If overfished
2451 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0.0;
2452 }
2453 break;
2454
2455 case 6: // PFMC Category 1 HCR
2456 if(ssb(sp, yr-1) < ref_SB0 * Ptarget(sp)){
2457 proj_F(sp, yr) = (Flimit(sp) + QnormHCR(sp)) * (ref_SB0 * Ptarget(sp) * (ssb(sp, yr-1) - ref_SB0 * Plimit(sp))) / (ssb(sp, yr-1) * (ref_SB0 * (Ptarget(sp) - Plimit(sp))));
2458 }
2459 if(ssb(sp, yr-1) < ref_SB0 * Plimit(sp)){ // If overfished
2460 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0.0;
2461 }
2462 break;
2463
2464 case 7: // SESSF Tier 1 HCR
2465 if(ssb(sp, yr-1) < ref_SB0 * Ptarget(sp)){
2466 proj_F(sp, yr) = Ftarget(sp) * ((ssb(sp, yr-1)/(ref_SB0 * Plimit(sp)))-1); // Used Fabc of FtargetSPR%
2467 }
2468 if(ssb(sp, yr-1) < ref_SB0 * Plimit(sp)){ // If overfished
2469 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0.0;
2470 }
2471 break;
2472 }
2473
2474
2475 // No projected F when the forecast is off or numbers-at-age are input (estDynamics > 0).
2476 if((forecast(sp) == 0) | (estDynamics(sp) > 0)){
2477 proj_F(sp, yr) = 0.0;
2478 }
2479
2480 // Adjust F*selex
2481 // -- Update F for the projection (account for selectivity and fleets)
2482 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2483 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2484 F_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = 0.0;
2485 }
2486 }
2487
2488 // -- Multiply F from HCR by selectivity and fleet proportion
2489 F_spp(sp, yr) = proj_F(sp, yr);
2490 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++) {
2491 if((sp == flt_spp(flt)) & (flt_type(flt) == 1)){ // Fisheries only, as in 5.12
2492 F_flt(flt, yr) = proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
2493 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2494 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2495 F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) = sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, nyrs_hind - 1) * proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr); // FIXME using last year of selectivity
2496 if(flt_type(flt) == 1){
2497 F_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) += F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr);
2498 }
2499 }
2500 }
2501 }
2502 }
2503
2504
2505 // -- Update mortality for forecast with new F
2506 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2507 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2508 M_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2509 Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + F_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) + M2_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2510 }
2511 }
2512

2514 // 6.8. FORECAST NUMBERS AT AGE, BIOMASS-AT-AGE (kg), and ssb-AT-AGE (kg)
2515 // -- 6.8.1. Forecasted recruitment
2516 // - Option 1: Use mean rec
2517 if(proj_mean_rec == 1){
2518 R(sp, yr) = avg_R(sp); // // Projections use mean R given bias in R0
2519 }
2520
2521 // - Option 2: Use SRR and rec devs
2522 if(proj_mean_rec == 0){
2523
2524 // - Calculate recruitment (with linkage offsets pre-added).
2525 // Pre-styr spawning year takes R_init, as in the hindcast block;
2526 // reachable only if the hindcast is shorter than minage.
2527 int proj_spawn_yr = yr - minage(sp);
2528 int proj_srr_use = (proj_spawn_yr < 0) ? 0 : srr_pred_fun;
2529 Type ssb_tmp = (proj_spawn_yr < 0) ? Type(0.0) : ssb(sp, proj_spawn_yr);
2530 Type proj_rec_mean = (proj_spawn_yr < 0) ? R_init(sp) : R0(sp, yr);
2531 // TODO: projected recruitment is not floored under an identity-link offset (inst/dev/TODO-srr-multispecies.md, item 14).
2532 R(sp, yr) = calculate_recruitment(proj_srr_use, proj_rec_mean, ssb_tmp, alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), rec_dev(sp, yr), SPR0(sp));
2533 }
2534
2535 N_at_age(sp, 0, 0 , yr) = R(sp, yr) * sex_ratio(sp, 0);
2536 if(nsex(sp) > 1){
2537 N_at_age(sp, 1, 0 , yr) = R(sp, yr) * (1 - sex_ratio(sp, 0));
2538 }
2539
2540
2541 // -- 6.8.2. Ages > recruitment
2542 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2543 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2544 switch(estDynamics(sp)){
2545 case 0: // Estimated numbers-at-age
2546
2547 // -- 6.8.2. Where minage + 1 <= age < Ai
2548 if(age < (nages(sp) - 1)) {
2549 N_at_age(sp, sex, age + 1, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr-1));
2550 }
2551
2552 // -- 6.8.3. Plus group where age > Ai.
2553 if(age == (nages(sp) - 1)) {
2554 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age - 1, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age-1, yr-1)) + N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr - 1) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr-1));
2555 }
2556 break;
2557
2558 case 1: // Fixed numbers-at-age - fixed scalar
2559 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, yr);
2560 break;
2561
2562 case 2: // Fixed numbers-at-age age-independent scalar
2563 N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = pop_scalar(sp) * NByageFixed(sp, sex, age, yr);
2564 break;
2565
2566 default: // Wrong estDynamics
2567 error("Invalid 'estDynamics'");
2568 }
2569
2570 // -- 6.8.4. FORECAST BIOMASS
2571 wt_idx_pop = 2 * sp;
2572 biomass_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_pop, sex, age, nyrs_hind-1 ); // 6.5.
2573 biomass(sp, yr) += biomass_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2574 } // End sex loop
2575
2576 // -- 6.8.5. FORECAST SSB (SUM ACROSS AGES)
2577 wt_idx_ssb = 2 * sp + 1;
2578 /*
2579 ssb_at_age(sp, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * pow(S_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr), spawn_month(sp)/12.0) * spawn_output(sp, age, nyrs_hind-1); // 6.6.
2580 ssb(sp, yr) += ssb_at_age(sp, age, yr);
2581 */
2582 ssb(sp, yr) += N_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * exp(-Z_at_age(sp, 0, age, yr) * spawn_month(sp)/12.0) * spawn_output(sp, age, nyrs_hind-1); // 6.6.
2583 }
2584 }
2585 }
2586
2587
2588 // 6.9. EXPECTED RECRUITMENT
2589 // Defensive: the function-scope `yr` is left at `nyrs` after the
2590 // forecast loop above, so the year-0 block must NOT use it -- doing
2591 // so reads `R0/alpha/Beta` one column past the end and segfaults
2592 // inside MakeADFun. Use the explicit `first_yr` constant and assert
2593 // that the expected-recruitment matrices match the year horizon.
2594 const int first_yr = 0;
2595 if (R0.cols() != nyrs || alpha.cols() != nyrs || Beta.cols() != nyrs) {
2596 error("Section 6.9: R0/alpha/Beta column count does not equal nyrs; "
2597 "recruitment-parameter matrices were sized inconsistently.");
2598 }
2599 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2600
2601 // Year 1 (arent fit in likelihood)
2602 // Under predation there is no SPRFinit (6.2) to place the first year on
2603 // the curve, so it takes R_init, the anchor its realised recruitment uses.
2604 if((msmMode > 0) & (srr_pred_fun > 1)){
2605 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = R_init(sp);
2606 } else {
2607 switch(srr_pred_fun){
2608 case 0: // Random about mean (e.g. Alaska)
2609 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = R0(sp, first_yr);
2610 break;
2611
2612 case 1: // Random about mean with environmental effects
2613 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = R0(sp, first_yr);
2614 break;
2615
2616 case 2: // Beverton-Holt
2617 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = (alpha(sp, first_yr) - 1/SPRFinit(sp)) / Beta(sp, first_yr); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
2618 break;
2619
2620 case 3: // Beverton-Holt with environmental impacts on alpha
2621 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = (alpha(sp, first_yr) - 1/SPRFinit(sp)) / Beta(sp, first_yr); // (Alpha-1/SPR0)/beta
2622 break;
2623
2624 case 4: // Ricker
2625 { Type aS = alpha(sp, first_yr) * SPRFinit(sp); // kept positive so the log is finite; R_hat itself is floored below
2626 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_d = 0; aS = posfun(aS, Type(1e-3), pen_d); }
2627 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = log(aS) / (Beta(sp, first_yr) * SPRFinit(sp)/1000000.0); }
2628 break;
2629
2630 case 5: // Ricker with environmental impacts on alpha
2631 { Type aS = alpha(sp, first_yr) * SPRFinit(sp); // kept positive so the log is finite; R_hat itself is floored below
2632 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_d = 0; aS = posfun(aS, Type(1e-3), pen_d); }
2633 R_hat(sp, first_yr) = log(aS) / (Beta(sp, first_yr) * SPRFinit(sp)/1000000.0); }
2634 break;
2635 default:
2636 error("Invalid 'srr_pred_fun'");
2637 }
2638 }
2639 // Same floor as R in 6.6.1: the first year's R_hat is reported and read by retrospective().
2640 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R_hat(sp, first_yr) = posfun(R_hat(sp, first_yr), Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
2641
2642 // Year 1+
2643 for(yr = 1; yr < nyrs; yr++){
2644 // - Calculate recruitment (with linkage offsets pre-added).
2645 // Pre-styr spawning year takes R_init, the SAME anchor the realised
2646 // recruitment above uses. Expected and realised then differ only by
2647 // rec_dev, so the stock-recruit penalty at 15.x scores the deviation and
2648 // nothing else -- there is no spawning biomass in these years to carry
2649 // information about the curve's level. Anchoring this side on the curve
2650 // instead (R_hat's own first year) leaves a mean-versus-curve level gap
2651 // that the penalty reads as signal: under the Ianelli configuration
2652 // (srr_fun mean, srr_pred_fun BevertonHolt) that added a fixed 0.83 nats
2653 // per guarded year, pulling rec_pars against alpha and Beta from years
2654 // with no data. Identical for BevertonHolt/BevertonHolt and
2655 // Ricker/Ricker, where R_init is already R_hat's first-year value.
2656 int hat_spawn_yr = yr - minage(sp);
2657 int hat_srr_use = (hat_spawn_yr < 0) ? 0 : srr_pred_fun;
2658 Type ssb_tmp = (hat_spawn_yr < 0) ? Type(0.0) : ssb(sp, hat_spawn_yr);
2659 Type hat_rec_mean = (hat_spawn_yr < 0) ? R_init(sp) : R0(sp, yr);
2660
2661 // Note: Expected recruitment does not include deviations, so we pass Type(0.0)
2662 R_hat(sp, yr) = calculate_recruitment(hat_srr_use, hat_rec_mean, ssb_tmp, alpha(sp, yr), Beta(sp, yr), Type(0.0), SPR0(sp));
2663 // Same floor as R in 6.6.1: log(R_hat) enters the stock-recruit penalty.
2664 if (rec_floor_on) { Type pen_R = 0; R_hat(sp, yr) = posfun(R_hat(sp, yr), Type(1e-3), pen_R); zero_N_pen(sp) += pen_R; }
2665 }
2666 }
2667
2668
2669
2670 // 6.11. ESTIMATE AVERAGE NUMBERS AT AGE
2671 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
2672 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2673 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2674 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
2675 // switch(avgnMode){
2676 // case 0: // MSVPA approach
2677 avgN_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2678 avgN_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr))) / M_at_age_dB0(sp, sex, age, yr);
2679 avgN_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) - Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) / (M_at_age_dBF(sp, sex, age, yr) + Ftarget_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
2680 /*
2681 break;
2682 case 1: // Kinzey and Punt (2009) approximation
2683 avgN_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * exp(- Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) / 2);
2684 break;
2685 case 2: // Van Kirk et al (2010) approximation
2686 avgN_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
2687 break;
2688 default:
2689 error("Invalid 'avgnMode'");
2690 }
2691 */
2692 }
2693 }
2694 }
2695 }
2696

2698 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
2699 // 7. MSVPA PREDATION MORTALITY EQUATIONS //
2700 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
2701
2702 // START PREDATION
2703 if(msmMode > 0) {
2704
2705 // NOTE -- LOOPING INDICES -- sp = species, age = age, ln = length, ksp = prey, k_age = prey age (yr), k_ln = prey length, yr = year, rsp = predator, r_age = predator age (yr), r_ln = predator length
2706
2707 // 7.1. Empirical MSVPA Suitability
2708 calculate_msvpa_suitability(stom_div_bio, suitability, suit_other,
2709 nspp, nyrs, suit_styr, suit_endyr, nyrs_suit, msmMode,
2710 nsex, nages, suitMode, diet_prop, avgN_at_age, weight_hat, other_food_diet_prop);
2711

2713 // 7.2. MSVPA PREDATION MORTALITY
2714 if((msmMode == 1) | (msmMode == 2)) {

2716 M2_at_age, M2_at_age_dB0, M2_at_age_dBF, M2_prop,

2723 } // End population dynamics iterations
2724 // - END LOOP - END LOOP - END LOOP - END LOOP - END LOOP - //

2728 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
2729 // 8. INDEX COMPONENTS EQUATIONS //
2730 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
2731
2732 // -- 8.1. Index of abundance/biomass
2733 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_ctl.rows(); index_ind++){
2734
2735 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary survey index
2736 sp = index_ctl(index_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
2737 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
2738 wt_idx_flt = nspp * 2 + index; // Temporary weight index for fleet
2739 mo = index_n(index_ind, 0); // Temporary index for month
2740
2741 index_hat(index_ind) = 0.0; // Initialize
2742
2743 if(flt_yr > 0){
2744 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2745 }
2746 else if(flt_yr < 0){
2747 flt_yr = -flt_yr - styr;
2748 }
2749
2750 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2751 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
2752
2753 // Index by fleet type.
2754 // Month is not used for a fishery: the year-average has no
2755 // instant to be taken at. SS3 splits the same way on its per-fleet
2756 // survey timing (SS_expval.tpl: timing >= 0 -> exp(-Z * timing);
2757 // timing < 0, required of every fishing fleet -> (1 - exp(-Z))/Z).
2758 //
2759 // A seasonal fishery is covered by the same form. Its exact predictor
2760 // over a window [t1, t1+D] is
2761 // N_a * exp(-Zpre_a * t1) * (1 - exp(-Zwin_a * D)) / (Zwin_a * D)
2762 // Zpre_a = M_a + other fleets' F_a (this fishery has yet to fish)
2763 // Zwin_a = M_a + F_a/D + other fleets' F_a
2764 // Since Zwin*D = M*D + F, the window factor tracks F almost as the
2765 // annual one does; the exp(-M*t1) offset carries no F, so q absorbs it.
2766 // Trend error against the exact form is ~1.5% over F 0.05-0.8, against
2767 // -29% to +33% for the snapshot.
2768 //
2769 // TODO: fit the window form directly when a fleet needs it.
2770 Type n_index;
2771 if(flt_type(index) == 1){
2772 n_index = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * (1.0 - exp( - Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr))) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr);
2773 } else {
2774 n_index = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * exp( - (mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr));
2775 }
2776
2777 // Weight
2778 if(flt_units(index) == 1){
2779 index_hat(index_ind) += n_index * sel_at_age(index, sex, age, flt_yr) * weight_hat(wt_idx_flt, sex, age, flt_yr );
2780 }
2781 // Numbers
2782 if(flt_units(index) == 2){
2783 index_hat(index_ind) += n_index * sel_at_age(index, sex, age, flt_yr);
2784 }
2785 }
2786 }
2787 }
2788
2789
2790 // -- 8.2. Analytical survey q following Ludwig and Martell 1994
2791 index_n_obs.setZero();
2792 index_q_analytical.setZero();
2793 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_ctl.rows(); index_ind++){
2794
2795
2796
2797 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary survey index
2798 sp = index_ctl(index_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
2799 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
2800
2801 if(flt_yr > 0){
2802 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2803
2804
2805 mo = index_n(index_ind, 0); // Temporary index for month
2806 if(flt_yr < nyrs_hind){
2807
2808 // If etimated standard deviation or analytical sigma (non-time-varying)
2809 if(est_sigma_index(index) > 0) {
2810 index_n_obs(index) += 1; // Add one if survey is used
2811 index_q_analytical(index) += log(index_obs(index_ind, 0) / index_hat(index_ind));
2812 }
2813
2814 // If time-varying sigma
2815 if(est_sigma_index(index) == 0 ) {
2816 index_n_obs(index) += 1 / square(index_obs(index_ind, 1));
2817 index_q_analytical(index) += log(index_obs(index_ind, 0) / index_hat(index_ind)) / square(index_obs(index_ind, 1));
2818 }
2819 }
2820 }
2821 }
2822
2823 // Take average
2824 for(index = 0 ; index < n_flt; index ++){
2825 index_q_analytical(index) = exp(index_q_analytical(index) / index_n_obs(index));
2826
2827 // Set index_q to analytical if used
2828 if(est_index_q(index) == 3){
2829 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
2830 index_q(index, yr) = index_q_analytical(index);
2831 }
2832 }
2833 }
2834
2835
2836 // -- 8.2b. Arithmetic-mean analytical q (AMAK/ebswp): q = sum(obs)/sum(pred)
2837 // over the fitted survey years (est_index_q == 7, "AnalyticalArith"). This
2838 // reproduces the AMAK BTS q_bts = mean(ob_bts)/mean(eb_bts) and is the q
2839 // form paired with the MVN covariance survey likelihood (Index_loglike =
2840 // "MVN"). Uses index_hat before it is scaled by q just below.
2841 vector<Type> index_obs_sum(n_flt); index_obs_sum.setZero();
2842 vector<Type> index_hat_sum(n_flt); index_hat_sum.setZero();
2843 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_ctl.rows(); index_ind++){
2844 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1;
2845 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2);
2846 if(flt_yr > 0){
2847 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2848 if(flt_yr < nyrs_hind){
2849 index_obs_sum(index) += index_obs(index_ind, 0);
2850 index_hat_sum(index) += index_hat(index_ind);
2851 }
2852 }
2853 }
2854 for(index = 0; index < n_flt; index++){
2855 if(est_index_q(index) == 7){
2856 Type q_arith = index_obs_sum(index) / index_hat_sum(index);
2857 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
2858 index_q(index, yr) = q_arith;
2859 }
2860 }
2861 }
2862
2863
2864 // -- 8.3. Survey Biomass - multiply by q
2865 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_ctl.rows(); index_ind++){
2866
2867 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary survey index
2868 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
2869
2870 if(flt_yr > 0){
2871 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2872 }
2873 else if(flt_yr < 0){
2874 flt_yr = -flt_yr - styr;
2875 }
2876
2877 // Hindcast or projection indexing for q
2878 int yr_ind = (flt_yr < nyrs_hind) ? flt_yr : (nyrs_hind - 1);
2879
2880 index_hat(index_ind) = index_q(index, yr_ind) * index_hat(index_ind); // pow(index_hat(index_ind), (1 + index_q_pow(index)));
2881 }
2882
2883
2884
2885 // --8.4. Calculate analytical sigma following Ludwig and Walters 1994
2886 //
2887 // The positive-observation guard matches the catch estimator below,
2888 // data_check() already refuses a non-positive index, so somewhat duplicative.
2889 index_n_obs.setZero();
2890 index_analytical_sd.setZero();
2891 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_ctl.rows(); index_ind++){
2892
2893 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary survey index
2894 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
2895
2896 if(flt_yr > 0){
2897 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2898
2899 if((flt_yr < nyrs_hind) && (index_obs(index_ind, 0) > 0)){
2900 index_n_obs(index) += 1; // Add one if survey is used
2901 index_analytical_sd(index) += square( log(index_obs(index_ind, 0)) - log(index_hat(index_ind)));
2902 }
2903 }
2904 }
2905
2906 for(index = 0 ; index < n_flt; index ++){
2907 if(index_n_obs(index) > 0){
2908 index_analytical_sd(index) = concentrated_lognormal_sd(index_analytical_sd(index) / index_n_obs(index), bias_adjust_obs);
2909 }
2910 }
2911
2912
2913 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
2914 // 9. FISHERY COMPONENTS EQUATIONS //
2915 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
2916 // 9.1. ESTIMATE CATCH-AT-AGE and TOTAL YIELD (kg)
2917 for(fsh_ind = 0; fsh_ind < catch_ctl.rows(); fsh_ind++){
2918
2919 flt = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fishery index
2920 sp = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
2921 flt_yr = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
2922 mo = catch_n(fsh_ind, 0); // Temporary index for month
2923 wt_idx_flt = nspp * 2 + flt; // Weight index for fleet
2924
2925 catch_hat(fsh_ind) = 0.0; // Initialize
2926 max_catch_hat(fsh_ind) = 0.0; // Initialize
2927
2928 if(flt_yr > 0){
2929 flt_yr = flt_yr - styr;
2930 }
2931 else if(flt_yr < 0){
2932 flt_yr = -flt_yr - styr;
2933 }
2934
2935 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
2936 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
2937
2938 // By weight
2939 if(flt_units(flt) == 1){
2940 catch_hat(fsh_ind) += F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, flt_yr) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * (1.0 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_flt, sex, age, flt_yr ); // 5.5.
2941 max_catch_hat(fsh_ind) += N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_flt, sex, age, flt_yr ) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, flt_yr) * proj_F_prop(flt); // FIXME using last year of selectivity;
2942 }
2943
2944 // By numbers
2945 if(flt_units(flt) == 2){
2946 catch_hat(fsh_ind) += F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, flt_yr) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * (1.0 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr);
2947 max_catch_hat(fsh_ind) += N_at_age(sp, sex, age, flt_yr) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, flt_yr) * proj_F_prop(flt); // FIXME using last year of selectivity;
2948 }
2949 }
2950 }
2951 }
2952
2953 // -- 9.1a. Initial equilibrium catch, in weight or numbers per the fleet's
2954 // Observation_units, as catch_hat is
2955 //
2956 // C_eq = sum_a Finit * s_a * w_a * N_eq_a * (1 - exp(-Z_a)) / Z_a
2957 // Z_a = M1_a + Finit * s_a
2958 //
2959 // Baranov on the deviation-free equilibrium age structure, at the fleet's own
2960 // selectivity and weight in the first hindcast year; SS3's Equil_catch
2961 // (SS_popdyn.tpl, Do_Equil_Calc). R supplies these rows only under initMode
2962 // 6, the one mode that builds N_eq at this same Finit * selectivity.
2963 vector<Type> equil_catch_hat(equil_catch_ctl.rows()); equil_catch_hat.setZero();
2964 for(int eq_ind = 0; eq_ind < equil_catch_ctl.rows(); eq_ind++){
2965 flt = equil_catch_ctl(eq_ind, 0) - 1;
2966 sp = equil_catch_ctl(eq_ind, 1) - 1;
2967 wt_idx_flt = nspp * 2 + flt;
2968 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
2969 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++){
2970 Type s_a = sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, 0);
2971 Type Z_a = M1_at_age(sp, sex, age, 0) + Finit(sp) * s_a;
2972 Type baranov = Finit(sp) * s_a / Z_a * (1.0 - exp(-Z_a)) * N_eq(sp, sex, age);
2973 if(flt_units(flt) == 1){ // by weight
2974 equil_catch_hat(eq_ind) += baranov * weight_hat( wt_idx_flt, sex, age, 0 );
2975 }
2976 if(flt_units(flt) == 2){ // by numbers
2977 equil_catch_hat(eq_ind) += baranov;
2978 }
2979 }
2980 }
2981 }
2982
2983 // -- 9.1b. Analytical catch sigma, following Ludwig and Walters (1994)
2984 //
2985 // The sd that minimises the catch density, accumulating the squared log
2986 // residuals here and concentrating them in concentrated_lognormal_sd().
2987 // Computed here because catch_hat is complete and the likelihood below reads it.
2988 //
2989 // The row predicate matches the likelihood's own -- a fitted year, a fishery,
2990 // and a positive observation -- so the sd is estimated over exactly the rows
2991 // it is then applied to. The positive-observation guard matters: a zero-catch
2992 // year is legal input, and log(0) is -inf, which would poison the sd for the
2993 // whole fleet.
2994 //
2995 // It reads catch_obs, not obsvec, so oneStepPredict()'s candidate value never
2996 // reaches it: the sd enters an OSA sweep as a fixed full-data number, the way
2997 // an estimated sd held at its MLE would.
2998 catch_n_obs.setZero();
2999 catch_analytical_sd.setZero();
3000 for(fsh_ind = 0; fsh_ind < catch_ctl.rows(); fsh_ind++){
3001
3002 flt = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 0) - 1;
3003 flt_yr = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 2);
3004
3005 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (flt_type(flt) == 1) && (catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0) > 0)){
3006 catch_n_obs(flt) += 1;
3007 catch_analytical_sd(flt) += square( log(catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0)) - log(catch_hat(fsh_ind)) );
3008 }
3009 }
3010
3011 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
3012 if(catch_n_obs(flt) > 0){
3013 catch_analytical_sd(flt) = concentrated_lognormal_sd(catch_analytical_sd(flt) / catch_n_obs(flt), bias_adjust_obs);
3014 }
3015 }
3016
3017
3018 // 9.2 Exploitable biomass ----
3019 exploitable_biomass.setZero();
3020
3021 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++) {
3022
3023 sp = flt_spp(flt);
3024 wt_idx_flt = nspp * 2 + flt;
3025
3026 if(flt_type(flt) == 1){ //Fishery only
3027 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++) {
3028 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3029 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3030 exploitable_biomass(sp, yr) += N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * weight_hat( wt_idx_flt, sex, age, yr ) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * proj_F_prop(flt); // FIXME using last year of selectivity;
3031 }
3032 }
3033 }
3034 }
3035 }
3036
3037
3038 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
3039 * 10. COMPOSITION EQUATIONS //
3040 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
3041
3042 // -- 10.1. Marginal age/length composition
3043 age_hat.setZero(); // Age-composition
3044 age_obs_hat.setZero(); // Age-composition with ageing error
3045 comp_hat.setZero(); // Age- or length-comp following data
3046 for(comp_ind = 0; comp_ind < comp_hat.rows(); comp_ind++){
3047
3048 flt = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fishery index
3049 sp = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
3050 flt_sex = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 2); // Temporary index for comp sex (0 = combined, 1 = female, 2 = male)
3051 comp_type = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 3); // Temporary index for comp type (0 = age, 1 = length, 2 = CAAL)
3052 yr = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 4); // Temporary index for years of data
3053 mo = (growth_model(sp) > 0) ? flt_month(flt) : comp_n(comp_ind, 0); // Temporary index for month (use fleet month if estimating growth, otherwise use from data)
3054 int wtind = nspp * 2 + flt;
3055 n_hat(comp_ind) = 0.0; // Initialize
3056
3057 // Likelihood (yr > 0) vs prediction (yr < 0)
3058 if(yr > 0){
3059 yr = yr - styr;
3060 }
3061 else if(yr < 0){
3062 yr = -yr - styr;
3063 }
3064
3065 // Hindcast
3066 Type Frate = 0.0;
3067 if(yr < nyrs_hind){
3068 yr_ind = yr;
3069 Frate = exp(log_F(flt, yr));
3070 }
3071
3072 // Projection
3073 if(yr >= nyrs_hind){
3074 yr_ind = nyrs_hind - 1;
3075 Frate = proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
3076 }
3077
3078 // 10.1.1. Estimated growth
3079 if(growth_model(sp) > 0){
3080 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3081 for(ln = 0; ln < nlengths(sp); ln++) {
3082 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3083
3084 switch(flt_type(flt)){
3085 case 1: // - Fishery
3086 if(flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1){ // Length based
3087 {
3088 // sel(L) * P(L|age) over this data bin's population bins
3089 // (section 2.3c).
3090 Type ps_ln = 0.0;
3091 for(int lp = pop_bin_lo(sp, ln); lp <= pop_bin_hi(sp, ln); lp++){
3092 ps_ln += sel_at_length(flt, sex, lp, yr) * growth_matrix(wtind, sex, age, lp, yr);
3093 }
3094 pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr) = ps_ln * (Frate / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
3095 }
3096 }
3097 break;
3098
3099
3100 case 2: // - Survey
3101 if(flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1){ // Length based
3102 {
3103 // sel(L) * P(L|age) over this data bin's population bins
3104 // (section 2.3c).
3105 Type ps_ln = 0.0;
3106 for(int lp = pop_bin_lo(sp, ln); lp <= pop_bin_hi(sp, ln); lp++){
3107 ps_ln += sel_at_length(flt, sex, lp, yr) * growth_matrix(wtind, sex, age, lp, yr);
3108 }
3109 pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr) = ps_ln * (N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * index_q(flt, yr_ind) * exp( - Type(mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr)));
3110 }
3111 }
3112 break;
3113 }
3114 }
3115 }
3116 }
3117
3118 // Assign CAAL to marginal age or length composition
3119 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3120 for(ln = 0; ln < nlengths(sp); ln++) {
3121
3122 // Age composition
3123 // - Catch-at-age
3124 if(comp_type == 0){
3125 switch(flt_sex){
3126 case 0: // Sexes combined or 1 sex assessment
3127 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3128 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr);
3129 }
3130 break;
3131
3132 case 1: case 2: // Sex-specific composition data
3133 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3134 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr);
3135 break;
3136
3137 case 3: // Joint composition data
3138 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3139 age_hat(comp_ind, age + nages(sp) * sex ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr);
3140 }
3141 break;
3142 }
3143 }
3144
3145
3146 // Length composition
3147 // - Catch-at-length
3148 if(comp_type == 1){
3149 switch(flt_sex){
3150 case 0: // Sexes combined or 1 sex assessment
3151 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3152 comp_hat(comp_ind, ln ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr);
3153 }
3154 break;
3155
3156 case 1: case 2: // Sex-specific composition data
3157 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3158 comp_hat(comp_ind, ln ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr);
3159 break;
3160
3161 case 3: // Joint composition data
3162 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3163 comp_hat(comp_ind, ln + nlengths(sp) * sex ) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr) ;
3164 }
3165 break;
3166 }
3167 }
3168 }
3169 }
3170
3171 // Adjust for aging error
3172 for(int obs_age = 0; obs_age < nages(sp); obs_age++) {
3173 for(int true_age = 0; true_age < nages(sp); true_age++) {
3174 age_obs_hat(comp_ind, obs_age) += age_hat(comp_ind, true_age ) * age_error(flt_ageing_error_index(flt), true_age, obs_age);
3175 }
3176 }
3177
3178 // Adjust for aging error for joint data
3179 if(flt_sex == 3){
3180 for(int obs_age = nages(sp); obs_age < nages(sp) * 2; obs_age++) {
3181 for(int true_age = nages(sp); true_age < nages(sp) * 2; true_age++) {
3182
3183 // Adjust indexing for joint age/length comp
3184 int true_age_tmp = true_age - nages(sp);
3185 int obs_age_tmp = obs_age - nages(sp);
3186
3187 age_obs_hat(comp_ind, obs_age) += age_hat(comp_ind, true_age ) * age_error(flt_ageing_error_index(flt), true_age_tmp, obs_age_tmp);
3188 }
3189 }
3190 }
3191
3192 // Assign age-comp to estimated comp
3193 if( comp_type == 0) {
3194 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 1;
3195 if(flt_sex == 3){
3196 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 2;
3197 }
3198 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp) * joint_adjust(comp_ind); age++) {
3199 comp_hat(comp_ind, age ) = age_obs_hat(comp_ind, age );
3200 }
3201 }
3202 } // End estimated growth loop
3203
3204
3205 // 10.1.2. Empirical weight-at-age
3206 if(growth_model(sp) == 0){
3207 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3208
3209 switch(flt_type(flt)){
3210 case 1: // - Fishery
3211 switch(flt_sex){
3212 case 0: // Sexes combined or 1 sex assessment
3213 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3214 // Catch-at-age
3215 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) += F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
3216 }
3217 break;
3218
3219 case 1: case 2: // Sex-specific composition data
3220 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3221 // Catch-at-age
3222 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) = F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
3223 break;
3224
3225 case 3: // Joint composition data
3226 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3227 // Catch-at-age
3228 age_hat(comp_ind, age + nages(sp) * sex ) = F_flt_age(flt, sex, age, yr) / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr);
3229 }
3230 break;
3231 }
3232 break;
3233
3234
3235 case 2: // - Survey
3236 switch(flt_sex){
3237 case 0: // Sexes combined or 1 sex assessment
3238 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3239 // Survey catch-at-age
3240 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) += N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * index_q(flt, yr_ind) * exp( - Type(mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
3241 }
3242 break;
3243
3244 case 1: case 2: // Sex-specific composition data
3245 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3246 // Survey catch-at-age
3247 age_hat(comp_ind, age ) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * index_q(flt, yr_ind) * exp( - Type(mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
3248 break;
3249
3250 case 3: // Joint composition data
3251 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
3252 // Survey catch-at-age
3253 age_hat(comp_ind, age + nages(sp) * sex ) = N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr) * index_q(flt, yr_ind) * exp( - Type(mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
3254 }
3255 break;
3256 }
3257 }
3258 }
3259
3260
3261 // Adjust for aging error
3262 for(int obs_age = 0; obs_age < nages(sp); obs_age++) {
3263 for(int true_age = 0; true_age < nages(sp); true_age++) {
3264 age_obs_hat(comp_ind, obs_age) += age_hat(comp_ind, true_age ) * age_error(flt_ageing_error_index(flt), true_age, obs_age);
3265 }
3266 }
3267
3268 // Adjust for aging error for joint data
3269 if(flt_sex == 3){
3270 for(int obs_age = nages(sp); obs_age < nages(sp) * 2; obs_age++) {
3271 for(int true_age = nages(sp); true_age < nages(sp) * 2; true_age++) {
3272
3273 // Adjust indexing for joint age/length comp
3274 int true_age_tmp = true_age - nages(sp);
3275 int obs_age_tmp = obs_age - nages(sp);
3276
3277 age_obs_hat(comp_ind, obs_age) += age_hat(comp_ind, true_age ) * age_error(flt_ageing_error_index(flt), true_age_tmp, obs_age_tmp);
3278 }
3279 }
3280 }
3281
3282 // Assign age-comp to estimated comp
3283 if( comp_type == 0) {
3284 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 1;
3285 if(flt_sex == 3){
3286 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 2;
3287 }
3288 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp) * joint_adjust(comp_ind); age++) {
3289 comp_hat(comp_ind, age ) = age_obs_hat(comp_ind, age );
3290 }
3291 }
3292
3293 // Convert from catch-at-age to catch-at-length.
3294 //
3295 // From age_hat, the TRUE ages -- not age_obs_hat. The age-length key is
3296 // P(length | true age), and a measured length carries no otolith reading,
3297 // so ageing error has no part in a length composition. SS3 likewise
3298 // applies its age_age matrix only to age and CAAL data.
