3299 if( comp_type == 1) {
3300 for(ln = 0; ln < nlengths(sp); ln++) {
3301 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3302
3303 sex = 0;
3304
3305 // Adjust sex for males/females
3306 if((flt_sex > 0) & (flt_sex < 3)){
3307 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3308 }
3309 comp_hat(comp_ind, ln ) += age_hat(comp_ind, age) * age_trans_matrix(flt_age_transition_index(flt), sex, age, ln );
3310 }
3311 }
3312
3313
3314 // Convert from catch-at-age to catch-at-length for joint comp data
3315 if( flt_sex == 3) {
3316 for(ln = nlengths(sp); ln < nlengths(sp) * 2; ln++) {
3317 for(age = nages(sp); age < nages(sp) * 2; age++) {
3318
3319 // Adjust indexing for joint age/length comp
3320 int obs_log_tmp = ln;
3321 int obs_age_tmp = age;
3322
3323 obs_age_tmp = age - nages(sp);
3324 obs_log_tmp = ln - nlengths(sp);
3325 sex = 1;
3326
3327 comp_hat(comp_ind, ln ) += age_hat(comp_ind, age) * age_trans_matrix(flt_age_transition_index(flt), sex, obs_age_tmp, obs_log_tmp );
3328 }
3329 }
3330 }
3331 }
3332 } // End empirical weight-at-age loop
3333
3334 // Standardize to sum to 1
3335 Type penalty = 0.0;
3336 comp_hat.row(comp_ind) /= posfun(comp_hat.row(comp_ind).sum(), Type(0.001), penalty);
3337 (void) penalty;
3338 }
3339
3340
3341 // -- 10.2. CAAL
3342 // -- length-based selectivity was converted above
3343 caal_hat.setZero();
3344 for(int caal_ind = 0; caal_ind < caal_hat.rows(); caal_ind++){
3345
3346 flt = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fishery index
3347 sp = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
3348 flt_sex = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 2); // Temporary index for caal sex (0 = combined, 1 = female, 2 = male)
3349 yr = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 3); // Temporary index for years of data
3350 ln = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 4) - 1; // Temporary index for length-bin
3351 mo = flt_month(flt); // Temporary index for month (use fleet month b/c estimating growth)
3352
3353 if(growth_model(sp) == 0) continue; // Skip empirical weight-at-age species
3354
3355 if(flt_sex > 0){
3356 sex = flt_sex - 1;
3357 } else {
3358 sex = flt_sex;
3359 }
3360
3361 int wtind = nspp * 2 + flt;
3362
3363 // Likelihood (yr > 0) vs prediction (yr < 0)
3364 if(yr > 0){
3365 yr = yr - styr;
3366 }
3367 else if(yr < 0){
3368 yr = -yr - styr;
3369 }
3370 // Hindcast
3371 Type Frate = 0.0;
3372 if(yr < nyrs_hind){
3373 yr_ind = yr;
3374 Frate = exp(log_F(flt, yr));
3375 }
3376
3377 // Projection
3378 if(yr >= nyrs_hind){
3379 yr_ind = nyrs_hind - 1;
3380 Frate = proj_F_prop(flt) * proj_F(sp, yr);
3381 }
3382
3383 // 10.2. Calculate CAAL (predicted conditional age-at-length)
3384 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
3385
3386 switch(flt_type(flt)){
3387 case 1: // - Fishery
3388 if(flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1){
3389 {
3390 // sel(L) * P(L|age) over this data bin's population bins
3391 // (section 2.3c).
3392 Type ps_ln = 0.0;
3393 for(int lp = pop_bin_lo(sp, ln); lp <= pop_bin_hi(sp, ln); lp++){
3394 ps_ln += sel_at_length(flt, sex, lp, yr) * growth_matrix(wtind, sex, age, lp, yr);
3395 }
3396 pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr) = ps_ln * (Frate / Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * (1 - exp(-Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr))) * N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr));
3397 }
3398 }
3399 break;
3400
3401
3402 case 2: // - Survey
3403 if(flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1){
3404 {
3405 // sel(L) * P(L|age) over this data bin's population bins
3406 // (section 2.3c).
3407 Type ps_ln = 0.0;
3408 for(int lp = pop_bin_lo(sp, ln); lp <= pop_bin_hi(sp, ln); lp++){
3409 ps_ln += sel_at_length(flt, sex, lp, yr) * growth_matrix(wtind, sex, age, lp, yr);
3410 }
3411 pred_CAAL(flt, sex, age, ln, yr) = ps_ln * (N_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr) * index_q(flt, yr_ind) * exp( - Type(mo/12.0) * Z_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr)) );
3412 }
3413 }
3414 break;
3415 }
3416 }
3417
3418 // Adjust for aging error
3419 for(int obs_age = 0; obs_age < nages(sp); obs_age++) {
3420 for(int true_age = 0; true_age < nages(sp); true_age++) {
3421 caal_hat(caal_ind, obs_age) += pred_CAAL(flt, sex, true_age, ln, yr) * age_error(flt_ageing_error_index(flt), true_age, obs_age);
3422 }
3423 }
3424
3425 // Observed CAAL standardize to sum to 1
3426 Type penalty = 0.0;
3427 caal_hat.row(caal_ind) /= posfun(caal_hat.row(caal_ind).sum(), Type(0.0001), penalty);
3428 (void) penalty;
3429 }
3430
3431
3432
3433 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
3434 * 11. PREDICTED STOMACH CONTENT //
3435 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
3436
3437 // Predict stomach content
3438 if((msmMode > 2) || (imax(suitMode) > 0)) {
3439 predict_stomach_content(nspp, nyrs_hind, styr, suit_styr, suit_endyr,
3440 minage, nsex, nages, diet_obs, diet_ctl,
3441 avgN_at_age, diet_prop_hat, diet_hat);
3442 }
3443
3444
3445 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
3446 // 12. DERIVED QUANTITIES
3447 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
3448
3449
3450 // 12.1. Depletion
3451 biomass_depletion.setZero();
3452 ssb_depletion.setZero();
3453 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
3454 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs; yr++){
3455
3456 if(DynamicHCR == 0){
3457 biomass_depletion(sp, yr) = biomass(sp, yr)/B0(sp, nyrs-1);
3458 ssb_depletion(sp, yr) = ssb(sp, yr)/SB0(sp, nyrs-1);
3459 }
3460
3461 if(DynamicHCR == 1){
3462 biomass_depletion(sp, yr) = biomass(sp, yr)/DynamicB0(sp, yr);
3463 ssb_depletion(sp, yr) = ssb(sp, yr)/DynamicSB0(sp, yr);
3464 }
3465
3466 // Multi-species, no HCR: the projection runs unfished, so SSB in the last
3467 // projection year is multispecies SB0 once `projyr` is far enough out to
3468 // equilibrate. Excluded under DynamicHCR, where DynamicSB0 is the
3469 // reference and this would overwrite it.
3470 if((HCR == 0) & (msmMode > 0) & (DynamicHCR == 0)){
3471 biomass_depletion(sp, yr) = biomass(sp, yr)/biomass(sp, nyrs-1);
3472 ssb_depletion(sp, yr) = ssb(sp, yr)/ssb(sp, nyrs-1);
3473 }
3474 }
3475 }
3476
3477
3478
3479
3480 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
3481 // 13. LIKELIHOOD EQUATIONS
3482 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
3483
3484 // 13.0. OBJECTIVE FUNCTION
3485 int n_col = std::max(n_flt, nspp);
3486 // Named rows of jnll_comp / unweighted_jnll_comp. These integer codes are
3487 // "magic" -- they MUST stay in sync with the row labels assigned in
3488 // R/6-rename_output.R (rownames of quantities$jnll_comp). Add/reorder a row
3489 // here and there in lockstep.
3490 enum JnllRow {
3491 JNLL_INDEX = 0, // Index data
3492 JNLL_CATCH = 1, // Catch data
3493 JNLL_COMP = 2, // Composition data
3494 JNLL_CAAL = 3, // CAAL data
3495 JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM = 4, // Non-parametric selectivity
3496 JNLL_SEL_DEV = 5, // Selectivity deviates
3497 JNLL_Q_PRIOR = 6, // Catchability prior
3498 JNLL_Q_DEV = 7, // Catchability deviates
3499 JNLL_SRR_PRIOR = 8, // Stock-recruit prior
3500 JNLL_INIT_DEV = 9, // Initial abundance deviates
3501 JNLL_REC_DEV = 10, // Recruitment deviates
3502 JNLL_SRR_PENALTY = 11, // Stock-recruit penalty
3503 JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY = 12, // Reference point penalties
3504 JNLL_ZERO_N_PENALTY = 13, // Zero n-at-age penalty
3505 JNLL_M_PRIOR = 14, // M prior
3506 JNLL_M_RE = 15, // M random effects
3507 JNLL_RATION = 16, // Ration
3508 JNLL_RATION_PENALTY = 17, // Ration penalties
3509 JNLL_STOMACH = 18, // Stomach content data
3510 JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR = 19, // Linkage-table priors (per-row)
3511 JNLL_LINKAGE_RE = 20, // Linkage random effects
3512 JNLL_EQUIL_CATCH = 21, // Initial equilibrium catch
3513 JNLL_N_ROWS = 22 // total row count (for dimensioning)
3514 };
3515 matrix<Type> jnll_comp(JNLL_N_ROWS, n_col); jnll_comp.setZero(); // negative log-likelihood components
3516 matrix<Type> unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_N_ROWS, n_col); unweighted_jnll_comp.setZero(); // same, without likelihood weights
3517
3518 // -- Data likelihood components (Fleet specific)
3519 // Slot 0 -- Survey biomass
3520 // Slot 1 -- Total catch (kg)
3521 // Slot 2 -- Age/length composition
3522 // Slot 3 -- CAAL
3523 // -- Selectivity and catchability components
3524 // Slot 4 -- Non-parametric selectivity
3525 // Slot 5 -- Selectivity annual deviates
3526 // Slot 6 -- Survey catchability prior
3527 // Slot 7 -- Survey catchability annual deviates
3528 // -- Species-specific priors/penalties
3529 // Slot 8 -- Stock recruitment parameter prior
3530 // Slot 9 -- init_dev -- Initial abundance-at-age
3531 // Slot 10 -- Annual recruitment deviation
3532 // Slot 11 -- Stock-recruit penalty
3533 // Slot 12 -- Reference point penalities
3534 // Slot 13 -- N-at-age < 0 penalty
3535 // Slot 14 -- M_at_age prior
3536 // Slot 15 -- M_at_age random effects
3537 // -- Predation components
3538 // Slot 16 -- Ration likelihood
3539 // Slot 17 -- Ration penalties
3540 // Slot 18 -- Diet proportion by weight likelihood
3541
3542
3543 // 13.1. FIT OBJECTIVE FUNCTION
3544 // Slot 0 -- Index of abundance biomass/numbers --
3545 Type index_std_dev = 0;
3546 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_obs.rows(); index_ind++) {
3547
3548 index = index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary survey index
3549 sp = index_ctl(index_ind, 1) - 1; // Species is the 2nd column
3550 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
3551
3552 // Set up variance
3553 switch (est_sigma_index(index)) {
3554 case 0: // Provided standard deviation
3555 index_std_dev = index_obs(index_ind, 1);
3556 break;
3557 case 1: // Estimated standard deviation
3558 index_std_dev = exp(index_log_sd(index));
3559 break;
3560 case 2: // Analytical (Ludwig and Walters 1994); see section 8.4
3561 index_std_dev = index_analytical_sd(index);
3562 break;
3563 default:
3564 error("Invalid 'Estimate_sigma_index'");
3565 }
3566
3567 index_sd(index_ind) = index_std_dev;
3568
3569 // Only include years from hindcast. Lognormal IID branch (index_ll_type == 0);
3570 // MVN covariance fleets (index_ll_type == 1) are handled in the per-fleet loop
3571 // below and contribute nothing here.
3572 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (flt_type(index) > 0) && (index_ll_type(index) == 0)){
3573 if(index_obs(index_ind) > 0){
3574 // Read the (log) observation from obsvec and gate it with keep so that
3575 // oneStepPredict() can compute OSA residuals. With keep == 1 (normal
3576 // fitting) and obsvec(pos) == log(index_obs) this equals the original
3577 // lognormal likelihood exactly. The `pos >= 0` guard matches comp/caal/
3578 // diet and the MVN/Normal OSA branches: safe today because the R
3579 // build_osa_data() inclusion set is identical to this predicate, and
3580 // defensive against a future divergence making obsvec(pos) out of bounds.
3581 int pos = index_obsvec_idx(index_ind);
3582 if(pos >= 0){
3583 Type index_mu = log(index_hat(index_ind)) - bias_adjust_obs*square(index_std_dev)/2.0;
3584 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), index_mu, index_std_dev, true);
3585 // method = "cdf": the same lognormal read as a CDF on the log scale.
3586 if(osa_mode == 2){
3587 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= osa_norm_cdf_terms(
3588 obsvec(pos), index_mu, index_std_dev, keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
3589 }
3590 }
3591 }
3592 }
3593
3594 // Natural-scale normal: the residual (obs - q*pred) is normal with an
3595 // ABSOLUTE sd (index_std_dev is the observation sd on the natural scale, not
3596 // a log-scale CV). No lognormal bias term. Two families share this branch and
3597 // differ only in whether the density is renormalized over the positive half
3598 // line:
3599 //
3600 // 3 "Normal" plain normal on (-inf, inf). Matches the AMAK
3601 // avo_like/cpue_like = 0.5*(obs - q*pred)^2 / sd^2
3602 // term for term, which is what the ADMB bridges
3603 // compare against, so it is kept exactly as-is.
3604 // 4 "TruncatedNormal" normal left-truncated at zero. An index cannot be
3605 // negative and data_check() will not accept one, so
3606 // over the values the data can actually take the
3607 // support is (0, inf) and the density has to be
3608 // renormalized: log f = log phi(x; mu, sd)
3609 // - log(1 - Phi(-mu/sd)), and 1 - Phi(-mu/sd)
3610 // = Phi(mu/sd).
3611 //
3612 // The distinction is a modelling choice, not a correction: only family 4 has
3613 // a simulator that draws from the same distribution the likelihood scores
3614 // (see the draw below). Family 3's draw is exact for the untruncated normal
3615 // it is fitted under, but has to reject the non-positive draws data_check()
3616 // would refuse, so draw and density differ where the absolute sd is large
3617 // relative to the index. Family 4 has no such gap.
3618 //
3619 // mu = q * (selected biomass) >= 0 and sd > 0, so mu/sd >= 0 and the
3620 // truncation constant lies in [log(0.5), 0]: bounded, and no underflow is
3621 // reachable.
3622 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (flt_type(index) > 0) &&
3623 ((index_ll_type(index) == 3) || (index_ll_type(index) == 4))){
3624 if(index_obs(index_ind, 0) > 0){
3625 Type log_Z = (index_ll_type(index) == 4) ? log(pnorm(index_hat(index_ind) / index_std_dev)) : Type(0.0);
3626 if(osa_mode == 0){
3627 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= dnorm(index_obs(index_ind, 0), index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev, true);
3628 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) += log_Z;
3629 } else {
3630 // OSA: read the natural-scale observation from obsvec (build_osa_data()
3631 // stores the untransformed obs for both families), keep-gated, so
3632 // oneStepPredict() residualizes it against the same density that was fit.
3633 int pos = index_obsvec_idx(index_ind);
3634 if(pos >= 0){
3635 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev, true);
3636 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) += keep(pos) * log_Z;
3637 // method = "cdf". "TruncatedNormal" gets its own CDF, renormalized
3638 // over (0, inf), which is exactly the correction the Gaussian methods
3639 // cannot see -- so under this method the family needs no separate
3640 // oneStepGeneric call and none of that call's integration failures.
3641 if(osa_mode == 2){
3642 if(index_ll_type(index) == 4){
3643 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= osa_trunc_norm_cdf_terms(
3644 obsvec(pos), index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev,
3645 keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
3646 } else {
3647 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= osa_norm_cdf_terms(
3648 obsvec(pos), index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev,
3649 keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
3650 }
3651 }
3652 }
3653 }
3654 }
3655 }
3656
3657 // -- Simulate the survey observation, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
3658 // Families 0 (lognormal), 3 (normal) and 4 (truncated normal); the correlated
3659 // families are drawn per fleet below, where their covariance lives. Each
3660 // draws what its own density assumes.
3661 //
3662 // Outside the hindcast gate, deliberately: run_mse() splices the
3663 // negative-Year rows in sign-flipped as the next assessment's data, so
3664 // gating the draw would leave the projection carrying observations that were
3665 // never simulated.
3666 SIMULATE {
3667 if((flt_type(index) > 0) && (index_ll_type(index) == 0)){
3668 index_obs(index_ind, 0) = exp(rnorm(log(index_hat(index_ind)) - bias_adjust_obs*square(index_std_dev)/2.0, index_std_dev));
3669 // The density reads obsvec for this family; keep the two in step.
3670 int sim_pos = index_obsvec_idx(index_ind);
3671 if(sim_pos >= 0){
3672 obsvec(sim_pos) = log(index_obs(index_ind, 0));
3673 }
3674 }
3675 if((flt_type(index) > 0) && (index_ll_type(index) == 3)){
3676 // "Normal": the density is untruncated, so the exact draw is a plain
3677 // normal -- which can come back non-positive, and data_check() rejects
3678 // that. Redraw, and count the rejections: the redrawn row follows the
3679 // normal truncated at zero, not the untruncated one the likelihood
3680 // scores, and sim_mod() warns when that is doing enough of the work to
3681 // matter. Use "TruncatedNormal" to remove the gap rather than measure it.
3682 Type sim_draw = rnorm(index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev);
3683 int tn_tries = 0;
3684 while((sim_draw <= Type(0)) && (tn_tries < index_trunc_max_tries)){
3685 index_trunc_rejects_sim(index_ind) += 1;
3686 sim_draw = rnorm(index_hat(index_ind), index_std_dev);
3687 tn_tries++;
3688 }
3689 index_trunc_tries_sim(index_ind) += tn_tries + 1;
3690 index_trunc_sd_sim(index_ind) = index_std_dev;
3691 index_trunc_budget_sim(index_ind) = index_trunc_max_tries;
3692 index_obs(index_ind, 0) = sim_draw;
3693 }
3694 if((flt_type(index) > 0) && (index_ll_type(index) == 4)){
3695 // "TruncatedNormal": left-truncated at zero, by inverse CDF, matching the
3696 // density above. With a = Phi(-mu/sd), drawing u uniformly on (a, 1) and
3697 // returning mu + sd*Phi^-1(u) is an exact draw from the normal restricted
3698 // to (0, inf) -- no rejection loop, no retry budget, and no draw that can
3699 // come back non-positive for data_check() to reject.
3700 Type a = pnorm(-index_hat(index_ind) / index_std_dev);
3701 Type u = a + (Type(1.0) - a) * runif(Type(0.0), Type(1.0));
3702 index_obs(index_ind, 0) = index_hat(index_ind) + index_std_dev * qnorm(u);
3703 }
3704 // Keep obsvec in step for both natural-scale families, in whichever layout
3705 // it is currently carrying. build_osa_data() stores the UNTRANSFORMED
3706 // observation for these families when the OSA data are built, which is
3707 // what the OSA branch of the density above reads; on the ordinary fitting
3708 // path it keeps the log(obs) layout it uses for every fleet. Writing the
3709 // wrong one would leave obsvec_sim describing different data from
3710 // index_obs_sim. Same reasoning as the MVN block below.
3711 if((flt_type(index) > 0) && ((index_ll_type(index) == 3) || (index_ll_type(index) == 4))){
3712 int sim_pos = index_obsvec_idx(index_ind);
3713 if(sim_pos >= 0){
3714 if(osa_mode == 0){
3715 if(index_obs(index_ind, 0) > Type(0)) obsvec(sim_pos) = log(index_obs(index_ind, 0));
3716 } else {
3717 obsvec(sim_pos) = index_obs(index_ind, 0);
3718 }
3719 }
3720 }
3721 }
3722 }
3723
3724 // MVN survey biomass likelihood (Index_loglike == "MVN"): the AMAK/ebswp
3725 // DoCovBTS covariance survey likelihood 0.5 * r' Sigma^-1 r applied to each MVN
3726 // fleet's fitted residual vector r = obs - q*pred (arithmetic, natural scale;
3727 // pair with est_index_q == 7 for the AMAK arithmetic-mean q). Sigma is the
3728 // per-fleet covariance index_cov_mat(index). The residual vector is assembled in
3729 // index_obs row order to match the rows/cols of Sigma. Reuses jnll_comp row 0.
3730 //
3731 // OSA (osa_mode == 1): the correlated block is whitened into independent standard
3732 // normals so oneStepPredict() can residualize each survey observation. With the
3733 // lower Cholesky Sigma = L L', build_osa_data() stores the whitened observation
3734 // z = L^-1 obs in obsvec, and here the whitened predicted mean m = L^-1 mu (mu =
3735 // index_hat) is formed with the SAME L; z_k ~ N(m_k, 1) are independent and the
3736 // innovation z_k - m_k = (L^-1(obs - mu))_k is the multivariate-Gaussian
3737 // one-step-ahead residual (Thygesen et al. 2017, the SAM/TMB OSA construction).
3738 // Sigma is fixed data, so L is a constant factorization; the whitened negative
3739 // log-density differs from the fitting density only by the constant
3740 // 0.5*logdet(Sigma) (family 1 also drops n/2*log(2*pi)), which does not affect
3741 // oneStepPredict's residuals.
3742 for(index = 0; index < n_flt; index++){
3743 if((flt_type(index) > 0) && (index_ll_type(index) == 1 || index_ll_type(index) == 2)){ // 1 = MVN (bare quadratic form), 2 = MVNORM (full density) ONLY -- other families (0 lognormal, 3 normal) carry a 1x1 dummy Sigma and must not enter here
3744 int n_mvn = 0;
3745 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_obs.rows(); index_ind++){
3746 if((index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1) == index){
3747 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2);
3748 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (index_obs(index_ind, 0) > 0)) n_mvn++;
3749 }
3750 }
3751 if(n_mvn > 0){
3752 vector<Type> resid(n_mvn);
3753 vector<Type> mu(n_mvn);
3754 vector<int> posv(n_mvn);
3755 vector<int> rowv(n_mvn); // index_obs row per Sigma position, for SIMULATE
3756 int k = 0;
3757 for(index_ind = 0; index_ind < index_obs.rows(); index_ind++){
3758 if((index_ctl(index_ind, 0) - 1) == index){
3759 flt_yr = index_ctl(index_ind, 2);
3760 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (index_obs(index_ind, 0) > 0)){
3761 resid(k) = index_obs(index_ind, 0) - index_hat(index_ind); // arithmetic residual (obs - q*pred)
3762 mu(k) = index_hat(index_ind);
3763 posv(k) = index_obsvec_idx(index_ind);
3764 rowv(k) = index_ind;
3765 k++;
3766 }
3767 }
3768 }
3769 if(osa_mode == 0){
3770 // TMB-native multivariate normal: density::MVNORM(Sigma) factorizes Sigma
3771 // internally (robust; no explicit inverse). MVNORM(Sigma)(r) returns the full
3772 // negative log-density 0.5*(r' Sigma^-1 r + logdet(Sigma) + n*log(2*pi)).
3773 Type dens = MVNORM(index_cov_mat(index))(resid);
3774 // "MVN" (1) reports the bare quadratic form 0.5 r' Sigma^-1 r (the AMAK/ebswp
3775 // value) by removing the fixed normalizing constant; "MVNORM" (2) keeps the
3776 // full density. Both give an identical fit (the constant has zero gradient).
3777 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) += (index_ll_type(index) == 2) ? dens : (dens - index_cov_const(index));
3778 } else {
3779 // OSA: whiten with the lower Cholesky of Sigma (same unique factor
3780 // build_osa_data() uses to whiten the observations), then score each
3781 // whitened observation as an independent standard normal.
3782 Eigen::LLT<Eigen::Matrix<Type, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic> > llt(index_cov_mat(index));
3783 matrix<Type> Lmat = llt.matrixL();
3784 matrix<Type> muc(n_mvn, 1);
3785 for(k = 0; k < n_mvn; k++) muc(k, 0) = mu(k);
3786 matrix<Type> mwhite = Lmat.template triangularView<Eigen::Lower>().solve(muc); // m = L^-1 mu
3787 for(k = 0; k < n_mvn; k++){
3788 int pos = posv(k);
3789 if(pos >= 0){
3790 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), mwhite(k, 0), Type(1.0), true);
3791 // method = "cdf": the whitened block is independent standard
3792 // normals, so each row's CDF is pnorm of its own innovation.
3793 if(osa_mode == 2){
3794 jnll_comp(JNLL_INDEX, index) -= osa_norm_cdf_terms(
3795 obsvec(pos), mwhite(k, 0), Type(1.0),
3796 keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
3797 }
3798 }
3799 }
3800 }
3801
3802 // -- Simulate the correlated survey block --
3803 // MVN and MVNORM differ only by a constant in the density, so they
3804 // simulate identically; MVNORM_t draws mean-zero, hence adding mu back.
3805 // Only the FITTED rows are drawn -- Sigma is dimensioned to exactly those,
3806 // in the assembly order above -- so unlike the independent families, rows
3807 // outside the fitted set keep the values they came in with.
3808 SIMULATE {
3809 // Redraw while any row is non-positive. The target is the joint normal
3810 // truncated to the positive orthant, which has no closed-form inverse
3811 // CDF, so rejection is the exact sampler here rather than a fallback;
3812 // truncating each margin separately would be a different distribution
3813 // and would break the correlation this likelihood models. There is no
3814 // truncated family to switch to, so the draw/density gap stays.
3815 //
3816 // The budget scales with the row count (index_trunc_max_tries * n_mvn)
3817 // because a vector is rejected if ANY row is non-positive.
3818 //
3819 // The acceptance test is at the TOP of the loop, so the draw written
3820 // out has always been checked: an exhausted budget writes a
3821 // non-positive index rather than an unexamined one, and sim_mod()
3822 // reports it as any other non-positive draw.
3823 vector<Type> sim_dev = MVNORM(index_cov_mat(index)).simulate();
3824 int mvn_tries = 0;
3825 while(true){
3826 bool any_nonpos = false;
3827 for(k = 0; k < n_mvn; k++){
3828 if(mu(k) + sim_dev(k) <= Type(0)) any_nonpos = true;
3829 }
3830 if(!any_nonpos) break;
3831 if(mvn_tries >= index_trunc_max_tries * n_mvn) break; // budget spent; the non-positive draw stands and is reported
3832 for(k = 0; k < n_mvn; k++){
3833 if(mu(k) + sim_dev(k) <= Type(0)) index_trunc_rejects_sim(rowv(k)) += 1;
3834 }
3835 sim_dev = MVNORM(index_cov_mat(index)).simulate();
3836 mvn_tries++;
3837 }
3838 for(k = 0; k < n_mvn; k++){
3839 index_trunc_tries_sim(rowv(k)) += mvn_tries + 1;
3840 index_trunc_sd_sim(rowv(k)) = sqrt(index_cov_mat(index)(k, k));
3841 index_trunc_budget_sim(rowv(k)) = index_trunc_max_tries * n_mvn;
3842 index_obs(rowv(k), 0) = mu(k) + sim_dev(k);
3843 // obsvec holds log(obs) for this family on the ordinary fitting path
3844 // (build_osa_data() only whitens it when the OSA data are built), so
3845 // keep it in step on that path and leave the whitened layout alone.
3846 int sim_pos = posv(k);
3847 if((sim_pos >= 0) && (osa_mode == 0) && (index_obs(rowv(k), 0) > Type(0))){
3848 obsvec(sim_pos) = log(index_obs(rowv(k), 0));
3849 }
3850 }
3851 }
3852 }
3853 }
3854 }
3855
3856 // Reported under a _sim name -- see the naming rule in section 5.12b.
3857 SIMULATE {
3858 matrix<Type> index_obs_sim = index_obs;
3859 REPORT(index_obs_sim);
3860 REPORT(index_trunc_tries_sim);
3861 REPORT(index_trunc_rejects_sim);
3862 REPORT(index_trunc_sd_sim);
3863 REPORT(index_trunc_budget_sim);
3864 }
3865
3866
3867 // Slot 1 -- Total catch --
3868 Type fsh_std_dev = 0;
3869 for(fsh_ind = 0; fsh_ind < catch_obs.rows(); fsh_ind++) {
3870
3871 flt = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fishery index
3872 sp = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 1) - 1; // Species is the column 3
3873 flt_yr = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 2); // Temporary index for years of data
3874 yr = flt_yr - styr; // Temporary index of years. Start at 0.
3875
3876 // Set up variance
3877 switch (est_sigma_fsh(flt)) {
3878 case 0: // Provided standard deviation
3879 fsh_std_dev = catch_obs(fsh_ind, 1);
3880 break;
3881 case 1: // Estimated standard deviation
3882 fsh_std_dev = exp(catch_log_sd(flt));
3883 break;
3884 case 2: // Analytical (Ludwig and Walters 1994); see section 9.1b
3885 fsh_std_dev = catch_analytical_sd(flt);
3886 break;
3887 default:
3888 error("Invalid 'Estimate_sigma_catch'");
3889 }
3890
3891 catch_sd(fsh_ind) = fsh_std_dev; // the sd this row was actually fitted with
3892
3893 // Add only years from hindcast
3894 if((flt_yr > 0) && (flt_yr <= endyr) && (flt_type(flt) == 1)){
3895 if(catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0) > 0){
3896 // Read the (log) observation from obsvec and gate it with keep for OSA
3897 // residuals (see the index slot above). With keep == 1 and
3898 // obsvec(pos) == log(catch_obs) this equals the original likelihood. The
3899 // `pos >= 0` guard matches the index/comp/caal/diet reads (defensive
3900 // parity; the R inclusion set makes pos valid for every fitted row today).
3901 int pos = catch_obsvec_idx(fsh_ind);
3902 if(pos >= 0){
3903 Type catch_mu = log(catch_hat(fsh_ind)) - bias_adjust_obs*square(fsh_std_dev)/2.0;
3904 jnll_comp(JNLL_CATCH, flt) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), catch_mu, fsh_std_dev, true) ;
3905 // method = "cdf": the same lognormal read as a CDF on the log scale.
3906 if(osa_mode == 2){
3907 jnll_comp(JNLL_CATCH, flt) -= osa_norm_cdf_terms(
3908 obsvec(pos), catch_mu, fsh_std_dev, keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
3909 }
3910 }
3911 // Martin's
3912 // jnll_comp(JNLL_CATCH, flt)+= 0.5*square((log(catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0))-log(catch_hat(fsh_ind)))/fsh_std_dev);
3913 }
3914 }
3915
3916 // -- Simulate the catch observation, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
3917 // Same mean as the dnorm above, bias term included: the estimator fits to
3918 // that mean, so a draw centred elsewhere biases every self-test.
3919 //
3920 // Outside the hindcast gate, deliberately. clean_data() appends a catch row
3921 // per fishery per projection year with Catch = NA (99 of BS2017SS's 216)
3922 // that sim_mod() has always filled; gating the draw leaves them NA and
3923 // data_check() rejects the refit.
3924 //
3925 // catch_hat is 0 there, so the mean is log(0) = -inf and rnorm() returns it
3926 // without drawing, giving exp(-inf) = 0. Safe only because SIMULATE runs on
3927 // doubles -- do not share this mean with the dnorm above, where log(0) puts
3928 // a NaN adjoint on the tape, and do not add a catch_hat > 0 guard, which
3929 // would change how many random numbers the draw consumes.
3930 SIMULATE {
3931 catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0) = exp(rnorm(log(catch_hat(fsh_ind)) - bias_adjust_obs*square(fsh_std_dev)/2.0, fsh_std_dev));
3932 // The density reads obsvec (log scale), the write-back reads catch_obs
3933 // (natural scale); keep both in step. -1 outside the fitted window.
3934 // Both writes last only for this evaluation -- DATA_ objects are re-read
3935 // each call -- so the jnll a simulate call returns is still the original
3936 // data's. Fit simulated data by building a new model on them.
3937 int sim_pos = catch_obsvec_idx(fsh_ind);
3938 if(sim_pos >= 0){
3939 obsvec(sim_pos) = log(catch_obs(fsh_ind, 0));
3940 }
3941 }
3942 }
3943
3944 // -- Initial equilibrium catch likelihood
3945 //
3946 // The lognormal the hindcast catch uses, on the row's own Log_sd, booked to
3947 // its own jnll row as SS3 does (equ_catch_like). Its own loop, so it still
3948 // runs for a fleet with no hindcast catch rows. No OSA slot: one observation
3949 // has no residual sequence to condition on.
3950 for(int eq_ind = 0; eq_ind < equil_catch_ctl.rows(); eq_ind++){
3951 int eq_flt = equil_catch_ctl(eq_ind, 0) - 1;
3952 if((equil_catch_obs(eq_ind, 0) > 0) && (flt_type(eq_flt) == 1)){
3953 Type eq_sd = equil_catch_obs(eq_ind, 1);
3954 Type eq_mu = log(equil_catch_hat(eq_ind)) - bias_adjust_obs*square(eq_sd)/2.0;
3955 jnll_comp(JNLL_EQUIL_CATCH, eq_flt) -=
3956 dnorm(log(equil_catch_obs(eq_ind, 0)), eq_mu, eq_sd, true);
3957
3958 // -- Simulate the equilibrium catch, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
3959 // Same mean as the dnorm above, bias term included. This observation is
3960 // the ONLY one informing Finit, and therefore the initial age-structure
3961 // and the SSB scale under initMode 6, so leaving it at its real value
3962 // conditioned every self_test() replicate on data its own operating model
3963 // had not generated, and reported the resulting Finit bias as real.
3964 //
3965 // Inside the gate, unlike the hindcast catch: every equilibrium row is a
3966 // real observation that data_check() requires to be positive, so there is
3967 // no projection row to fill.
3968 SIMULATE {
3969 equil_catch_obs(eq_ind, 0) = exp(rnorm(eq_mu, eq_sd));
3970 }
3971 }
3972 }
3973
3974 // Reported under _sim names -- see the naming rule in section 5.12b.
3975 //
3976 // obsvec_sim holds the catch and survey-index entries redrawn and every other
3977 // entry as observed, and that is all it will ever hold: the composition, CAAL
3978 // and diet draws below write their own matrices and do not touch obsvec, since
3979 // their densities read it only in OSA mode and sim_mod() never simulates from
3980 // an OSA object. It is reported for inspection, not as a simulated data set --
3981 // sim_mod() assembles the data_list from the per-type *_obs_sim matrices.
3982 SIMULATE {
3983 matrix<Type> catch_obs_sim = catch_obs;
3984 matrix<Type> equil_catch_obs_sim = equil_catch_obs;
3985 vector<Type> obsvec_sim = obsvec;
3986 REPORT(catch_obs_sim);
3987 REPORT(equil_catch_obs_sim);
3988 REPORT(obsvec_sim);
3989 }
3990
3991
3992 // Slot 2 -- Age/length composition
3993 // Small proportion offset added to obs/pred comps before the multinomial to avoid log(0).
3994 // Supplied as data (DATA_SCALAR comp_offset) so it is set from R via
3995 // rearrange_data()/fit_control(); default 1e-5. The OSA obsvec is built with the same
3996 // offset, so fitting and OSA residuals stay consistent.
3997 Type comp_prop_offset = comp_offset;
3998 // FIXME: case 0 fitting routes through dmultinom_osa(), which renormalizes p;
3999 // the previous dmultinom() did not, so the *reported* case-0 multinomial NLL
4000 // shifts by a per-row constant Neff*log(1 + n_comp*offset). The gradient and MLE
4001 // are unchanged (additive constant) -- only the reported value moves. Left as-is
4002 // for now: either reword the "changes the decomposition, not the value" note to
4003 // admit the constant, or subtract it so the reported NLL is comparable across
4004 // versions.
4005 //
4006 // Simulated compositions go to this copy, not into the REPORTed comp_obs --
4007 // see the _sim naming rule in section 5.12b. Rows the draw does not touch keep
4008 // the observed values they were copied with.
4009 matrix<Type> comp_sim = comp_obs;
4010
4011 for(comp_ind = 0; comp_ind < comp_obs.rows(); comp_ind++) {
4012
4013 flt = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fleet index
4014 sp = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
4015 flt_sex = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 2); // Temporary index for comp sex (0 = combined, 1 = female, 2 = male, 3 = joint)
4016 comp_type = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 3); // Temporary index for comp type (0 = age, 1 = length)
4017 yr = comp_ctl(comp_ind, 4); // Temporary index for years of data
4018
4019 // Adjustment for joint sex composition data
4020 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 1;
4021 if(flt_sex == 3){
4022 joint_adjust(comp_ind) = 2;
4023 }
4024
4025 // Number of ages
4026 int n_comp = 0;
4027 if(comp_type == 0){
4028 n_comp = nages(sp) * joint_adjust(comp_ind); // For sex = 3 (joint sex comp data)
4029
4030 }
4031 if(comp_type == 1){
4032 n_comp = nlengths(sp) * joint_adjust(comp_ind);
4033 }
4034
4035 // Select sections
4036 vector<Type> comp_obs_tmp = comp_obs.row(comp_ind).segment(0, n_comp); // Observed proportion
4037 vector<Type> comp_hat_tmp = comp_hat.row(comp_ind).segment(0, n_comp); // Expected proportion
4038
4039 // Composition young/old accumulation (AFSC ac_yng / ac_old): fold the bins
4040 // below `yng` into the `yng` bin and above `old` into the `old` bin, then
4041 // restrict the likelihood to [yng, old]. Done PER SEX BLOCK for joint-sex
4042 // comps (joint_adjust == 2) so a fold never crosses the sex boundary. yng/old
4043 // are 1-based bin ordinals on the fleet's comp dimension (age or length); the
4044 // default (yng = 1, old >= nbins) is a no-op, so models without accumulation
4045 // stay bit-identical. Applied on BOTH the ordinary-fitting path and the OSA
4046 // path (osa_mode == 1): OSA residuals must correspond to the folded model that
4047 // was fit, so the OSA branch below reads a folded obsvec (built identically in
4048 // build_osa_data()) against this folded comp_hat_tmp / n_comp.
4049 {
4050 int nbins_blk = (comp_type == 0) ? nages(sp) : nlengths(sp);
4051 int yng = comp_accum_young(flt);
4052 int old = comp_accum_old(flt);
4053 if (yng < 1) yng = 1;
4054 if (old < 1 || old > nbins_blk) old = nbins_blk;
4055 if (yng > old) yng = old; // defensive: keep 1 <= yng <= old (data_check() validates)
4056 if (yng > 1 || old < nbins_blk) {
4057 int nkeep = old - yng + 1;
4058 int nblk = joint_adjust(comp_ind);
4059 vector<Type> obs_acc(nblk * nkeep); obs_acc.setZero();
4060 vector<Type> hat_acc(nblk * nkeep); hat_acc.setZero();
4061 for (int b = 0; b < nblk; b++) {
4062 for (int j = 0; j < nbins_blk; j++) {
4063 int tgt = j;
4064 if (j < yng - 1) tgt = yng - 1; // fold young tail into the yng bin
4065 if (j > old - 1) tgt = old - 1; // fold old tail into the old bin
4066 obs_acc(b * nkeep + tgt - (yng - 1)) += comp_obs_tmp(b * nbins_blk + j);
4067 hat_acc(b * nkeep + tgt - (yng - 1)) += comp_hat_tmp(b * nbins_blk + j);
4068 }
4069 }
4070 comp_obs_tmp = obs_acc;
4071 comp_hat_tmp = hat_acc;
4072 n_comp = nblk * nkeep;
4073 }
4074 }
4075
4076 // Folded proportions (pre-offset, pre-numbers) for the AFSC pseudo-likelihood
4077 // (comp_ll_type == -1), which reads proportions directly rather than the
4078 // numbers vector built below. Copying here -- after the fold -- keeps case -1
4079 // consistent with cases 0/1 (which use comp_obs_tmp/comp_hat_tmp). With no
4080 // accumulation these equal comp_obs.row(comp_ind)/comp_hat.row(comp_ind), so
4081 // the no-op path stays bit-identical.
4082 vector<Type> comp_obs_prop = comp_obs_tmp;
4083 vector<Type> comp_hat_prop = comp_hat_tmp;
4084
4085 // Add offset (for some reason can't do above in single line....)
4086 comp_obs_tmp += comp_prop_offset;
4087 comp_hat_tmp += comp_prop_offset;
4088
4089 // Convert observed prop to observed numbers
4090 comp_obs_tmp *= comp_n(comp_ind, 1);
4091 // Dirichlet-multinomial concentration. Use the observed-count total
4092 // comp_obs_tmp.sum() = N*(1 + offset*nbins) as the effective sample size,
4093 // matching the N that ddirmultinom() reads from obs.sum() (so the alpha and
4094 // the density use a consistent N), the CAAL DM (which uses sum(caal_obs_tmp)),
4095 // and the AFSC linear-DM parameterization. Previously used the raw comp_n.
4096 vector<Type> alphas = comp_obs_tmp.sum() * comp_hat_tmp * DM_pars_comp(flt); // DM alpha
4097 vector<Type> unweighted_alphas = comp_obs_tmp.sum() * comp_hat_tmp; // DM alpha
4098
4099 // Only use years wanted
4100 if((yr <= endyr) && (yr > 0) && (flt_type(flt) > 0) && (comp_n(comp_ind, 1) > 0)){
4101
4102 if(osa_mode == 0){
4103 // ---- Normal fitting: weighted density read from comp_obs (unchanged) ----
4104 switch(comp_ll_type(flt)){
4105
4106 case -1:
4107 for(ln = 0; ln < n_comp; ln++) {
4108 // Martin's -- read the folded proportions (comp_*_prop), so an active
4109 // Comp_accum_young/old actually accumulates the tails here too.
4110 jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= comp_weights(flt) * Type(comp_n(comp_ind, 1)) * (comp_obs_prop(ln) + comp_prop_offset) * log((comp_hat_prop(ln)+comp_prop_offset) / (comp_obs_prop(ln) + comp_prop_offset)) ;
4111 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= Type(comp_n(comp_ind, 1)) * (comp_obs_prop(ln) + comp_prop_offset) * log((comp_hat_prop(ln)+comp_prop_offset) / (comp_obs_prop(ln) + comp_prop_offset));
4112 }
4113 break;
4114
4115 case 0: { // Full multinomial -- via the OSA conditional-binomial decomposition (keep == 1)
4116 data_indicator<vector<Type>, Type> keep_ones(comp_obs_tmp, true);
4117 jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= comp_weights(flt) * dmultinom_osa(comp_obs_tmp, comp_hat_tmp, keep_ones, 1, 1);
4118 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= dmultinom_osa(comp_obs_tmp, comp_hat_tmp, keep_ones, 1, 1);
4119 break;
4120 }
4121
4122 case 1: // Dirichlet-multinomial
4123 jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= ddirmultinom(comp_obs_tmp, alphas, true);
4124 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= ddirmultinom(comp_obs_tmp, unweighted_alphas, true);
4125 break;
4126 default:
4127 error("Invalid 'comp_ll_type'");
4128 }
4129 } else {
4130 // ---- OSA build: unweighted, keep-gated conditional density read from
4131 // obsvec so oneStepPredict() can residualize each bin. The AFSC
4132 // pseudo-likelihood (-1) has no proper density, so it is residualized
4133 // under the full multinomial. ----
4134 int start = comp_obsvec_idx(comp_ind);
4135 if(start >= 0){
4136 vector<Type> osa_x = obsvec.segment(start, n_comp);
4137 if(comp_ll_type(flt) == 1){ // Dirichlet-multinomial (uses fitted DM par)
4138 // No CDF term: the beta-binomial has no elementary one (comp_osa.hpp).
4139 jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= ddirmultinom_osa(osa_x, alphas, keep.segment(start, n_comp), 1, 1);
4140 } else { // multinomial (cases 0 and -1)
4141 jnll_comp(JNLL_COMP, flt) -= dmultinom_osa(osa_x, comp_hat_tmp, keep.segment(start, n_comp), 1, 1, osa_mode == 2);
4142 }
4143 }
4144 }
4145 }
4146
4147 // -- Simulate the composition, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
4148 // Drawn in RAW bin space, from comp_hat before the transforms above.
4149 // Tail accumulation folds bins many-to-one before the density, so a draw
4150 // taken there has no way back; drawing raw and letting the refit fold is
4151 // exact, both families being closed under merging categories. And
4152 // comp_prop_offset is affine on obs and prediction alike, so drawing from
4153 // the un-offset prediction is what keeps the round trip unbiased.
4154 //
4155 // Outside the year gate, deliberately: run_mse() reveals the negative-Year
4156 // rows to the estimation model as new composition data.
4157 SIMULATE {
4158 int nbin_raw = ((comp_type == 0) ? nages(sp) : nlengths(sp)) * joint_adjust(comp_ind);
4159 vector<Type> sim_p = comp_hat.row(comp_ind).segment(0, nbin_raw);
4160 Type sim_tot = sim_p.sum();
4161 Type n_nom = comp_n(comp_ind, 1);
4162 // A row the draw cannot be taken for comes back EMPTY, not carried over and
4163 // not filled in from the prediction. Two ways to get there, and they mean
4164 // the same thing:
4165 // sim_tot == 0 nothing is predicted -- a fleet with no catch that year,
4166 // or one switched off.
4167 // n_nom == 0 nothing was sampled -- no sample size to draw at.
4168 // comp_hat rows are normalized to sum to one, so falling back to the
4169 // prediction would hand back noise-free proportions summing to one: a row
4170 // that was never sampled, indistinguishable from a real full-weight
4171 // composition. run_mse() decides "no catch, so no composition" by testing
4172 // whether the row sums above zero (R/10-run_mse.R), and it zeroes
4173 // Sample_size for empty rows and feeds them back in -- so the second case
4174 // is reachable on the next assessment. sim_mod() warns on
4175 // an empty row by the same test.
4176 vector<Type> sim_out(nbin_raw); sim_out.setZero();
4177
4178 if((sim_tot > Type(0)) && (n_nom > Type(0))){
4179 vector<Type> p = sim_p / sim_tot;
4180 if(comp_ll_type(flt) == 1){
4181 // Dirichlet-multinomial: the concentration already carries the weight
4182 // (DM_pars_comp = exp(comp_weights)), so the draw is at the nominal N.
4183 vector<Type> sim_alphas = p * n_nom * DM_pars_comp(flt);
4184 sim_out = rdirmultinom_rce(n_nom, sim_alphas);
4185 } else {
4186 // Multinomial (and the AFSC pseudo-likelihood, which has no proper
4187 // density of its own): comp_weights multiplies the log-likelihood, so
4188 // it is an effective sample size and the draw has to match it, or the
4189 // data are more informative than the estimator treats them as being.
4190 sim_out = rmultinom_rce(n_nom * comp_weights(flt), p);
4191 }
4192 }
4193 for(int b = 0; b < nbin_raw; b++){
4194 comp_sim(comp_ind, b) = sim_out(b);
4195 }
4196 // Clear the ragged tail. comp_obs is sized to the widest row, so a row
4197 // with fewer bins has padding columns that belong to no bin. The R draw
4198 // overwrote the whole row; writing only the real bins would leave whatever
4199 // was there, and rearrange_data() normalizes across ALL columns on the
4200 // next fit -- diluting every real bin by the padding's share.
4201 for(int b = nbin_raw; b < comp_sim.cols(); b++){
4202 comp_sim(comp_ind, b) = Type(0);
4203 }
4204 }
4205 }
4206
4207 SIMULATE {
4208 matrix<Type> comp_obs_sim = comp_sim;
4209 REPORT(comp_obs_sim);
4210 }
4211
4212
4213 // Slot 3 -- Conditional age at length (CAAL)
4214 // Simulated CAAL goes to this copy, not into caal_obs, for the reason comp_sim
4215 // and diet_sim exist: caal_obs is REPORTed further down.
4216 matrix<Type> caal_sim = caal_obs;
4217
4218 for(int caal_ind = 0; caal_ind < caal_hat.rows(); caal_ind++){
4219
4220 flt = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 0) - 1; // Temporary fishery index
4221 sp = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 1) - 1; // Temporary index of species
4222 flt_sex = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 2); // Temporary index for caal sex (0 = combined, 1 = female, 2 = male, 3 = joint)
4223 yr = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 3); // Temporary index for years of data
4224 ln = caal_ctl(caal_ind, 4) - 1; // Temporary index for length-bin
4225
4226 // // Adjustment for joint sex CAAL data
4227 // joint_adjust(caal_ind) = 1;
4228 // if(flt_sex == 3){
4229 // joint_adjust(caal_ind) = 2;
4230 // }
4231
4232 // Number of ages
4233 int n_caal = nages(sp); // * joint_adjust(caal_ind); // For sex = 3 (joint sex caal data)
4234
4235 // Select sections
4236 vector<Type> caal_obs_tmp = caal_obs.row(caal_ind).segment(0, n_caal); // Observed proportion
4237 vector<Type> caal_hat_tmp = caal_hat.row(caal_ind).segment(0, n_caal); // Expected proportion
4238
4239 // Proportions kept pre-offset and pre-numbers for the AFSC pseudo-likelihood
4240 // (caal_ll_type == -1), which reads proportions directly. Mirrors the
4241 // comp_obs_prop / comp_hat_prop copies in the age-composition slot above.
4242 vector<Type> caal_obs_prop = caal_obs_tmp;
4243 vector<Type> caal_hat_prop = caal_hat_tmp;
4244
4245 // Add offset (for some reason can't do above in single line....)
4246 caal_obs_tmp += comp_prop_offset;
4247 caal_hat_tmp += comp_prop_offset;
4248
4249 // Convert observed prop to observed numbers
4250 caal_obs_tmp *= caal_n(caal_ind, 0);
4251 vector<Type> alphas = sum(caal_obs_tmp) * caal_hat_tmp * DM_pars_caal(flt); // DM alpha
4252 vector<Type> unweighted_alphas = sum(caal_obs_tmp) * caal_hat_tmp; // DM alpha
4253
4254 // Only use years wanted
4255 if((yr <= endyr) && (yr > 0) && (flt_type(flt) > 0) && (caal_n(caal_ind, 0) > 0)){
4256
4257 if(osa_mode == 0){
4258 // ---- Normal fitting ----
4259 // Two parallel accumulators per CAAL fleet:
4260 // jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) weighted by caal_weights(flt); enters the objective.
4261 // unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) unweighted; reported so Francis and
4262 // McAllister-Ianelli reweighting can read the raw likelihood.
4263 // Both address JNLL_CAAL, not JNLL_COMP: age composition and conditional
4264 // age-at-length are separate likelihood rows (see the JnllRow enum).
4265 switch(caal_ll_type(flt)){
4266
4267 case -1: // AFSC/AMAK multinomial pseudo-likelihood, as for age comps
4268 // Same form as comp_ll_type == -1 (see the age-composition slot):
4269 // sum_a N * (obs_a + off) * log((hat_a + off) / (obs_a + off)), read
4270 // off the proportions rather than the numbers vector. It drops the
4271 // multinomial normalizing constant, so it is a pseudo-likelihood
4272 // rather than a density -- which is why the OSA branch below
4273 // residualizes it under the full multinomial, as comps do.
4274 for(int age_ind = 0; age_ind < n_caal; age_ind++){
4275 jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= caal_weights(flt) * Type(caal_n(caal_ind, 0)) * (caal_obs_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset) * log((caal_hat_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset) / (caal_obs_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset));
4276 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= Type(caal_n(caal_ind, 0)) * (caal_obs_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset) * log((caal_hat_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset) / (caal_obs_prop(age_ind) + comp_prop_offset));
4277 }
4278 break;
4279
4280 case 0: { // Full multinomial -- via the OSA conditional-binomial decomposition (keep == 1)
4281 data_indicator<vector<Type>, Type> keep_ones(caal_obs_tmp, true);
4282 jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= caal_weights(flt) * dmultinom_osa(caal_obs_tmp, caal_hat_tmp, keep_ones, 1, 1);
4283 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= dmultinom_osa(caal_obs_tmp, caal_hat_tmp, keep_ones, 1, 1);
4284 break;
4285 }
4286
4287 case 1: // Dirichlet-multinomial
4288 jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= ddirmultinom(caal_obs_tmp, alphas, true);
4289 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= ddirmultinom(caal_obs_tmp, unweighted_alphas, true);
4290 break;
4291 default:
4292 error("Invalid 'caal_ll_type'");
4293 }
4294 } else {
4295 // ---- OSA build: unweighted, keep-gated conditional density read from
4296 // obsvec (alpha total uses the fixed caal_obs counts, not obsvec). ----
4297 int start = caal_obsvec_idx(caal_ind);
4298 if(start >= 0){
4299 vector<Type> osa_x = obsvec.segment(start, n_caal);
4300 if(caal_ll_type(flt) == 1){ // Dirichlet-multinomial
4301 // No CDF term: the beta-binomial has no elementary one (comp_osa.hpp).
4302 jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= ddirmultinom_osa(osa_x, alphas, keep.segment(start, n_caal), 1, 1);
4303 } else { // multinomial
4304 jnll_comp(JNLL_CAAL, flt) -= dmultinom_osa(osa_x, caal_hat_tmp, keep.segment(start, n_caal), 1, 1, osa_mode == 2);
4305 }
4306 }
4307 }
4308 }
4309
4310 // -- Simulate the conditional age-at-length, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
4311 // Same construction as the marginal composition above, and for the same
4312 // reasons: drawn from caal_hat before comp_prop_offset is added, so the round
4313 // trip through a refit is unbiased, and outside the year gate so the rows
4314 // run_mse() reveals to the estimation model are drawn too. CAAL has no tail
4315 // accumulation, so there is no fold to undo here.
4316 SIMULATE {
4317 vector<Type> sim_p = caal_hat.row(caal_ind).segment(0, n_caal);
4318 Type sim_tot = sim_p.sum();
4319 Type n_nom = caal_n(caal_ind, 0);
4320 vector<Type> sim_out(n_caal); sim_out.setZero();
4321
4322 if((sim_tot > Type(0)) && (n_nom > Type(0))){
4323 vector<Type> p = sim_p / sim_tot;
4324 if(caal_ll_type(flt) == 1){
4325 vector<Type> sim_alphas = p * n_nom * DM_pars_caal(flt);
4326 sim_out = rdirmultinom_rce(n_nom, sim_alphas);
4327 } else {
4328 sim_out = rmultinom_rce(n_nom * caal_weights(flt), p);
4329 }
4330 }
4331 // As for the marginal composition: a row with nothing predicted or nothing
4332 // sampled comes back empty rather than filled in from the prediction, and
4333 // the ragged tail is cleared so a later normalization cannot dilute the
4334 // real bins.
4335 for(int b = 0; b < n_caal; b++){
4336 caal_sim(caal_ind, b) = sim_out(b);
4337 }
4338 for(int b = n_caal; b < caal_sim.cols(); b++){
4339 caal_sim(caal_ind, b) = Type(0);
4340 }
4341 }
4342 }
4343
4344 SIMULATE {
4345 matrix<Type> caal_obs_sim = caal_sim;
4346 REPORT(caal_obs_sim);
4347 }
4348
4349
4350 // Slot 4-5 -- Selectivity
4351 //
4352 // FIXME: penalize every selectivity deviation rather than a sub-range. The
4353 // range controls (Sel_pen_first_bin, Sel_pen_last_bin, Sel_cap_bin,
4354 // Sel_start_year, and the matching build_map masking) exist only because these
4355 // penalties cover a sub-range; penalizing all deviations would pin the
4356 // unidentified directions and remove the need to index by bin and year.
4357 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){ // Loop around surveys
4358 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) = 0;
4359 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) = 0;
4360 sp = flt_spp(flt);
4361
4362 // Non-parametric penalties act over the fleet's selectivity dimension:
4363 // nbins = nages for age-based, nlengths for length-based selectivity.
4364 bool sel_is_length = (flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1);
4365 // sel_at_length is indexed on the POPULATION bins, so the penalty's bin
4366 // range is counted there. Identical to the data bins with one grid, and
4367 // data_check() refuses a time-varying length-based selectivity on a coarser
4368 // data grid, where Sel_pen_first_bin / Sel_pen_last_bin would be ambiguous.
4369 int nbins = sel_is_length ? nlengths_pop(sp) : nages(sp);
4370
4371 // If estimating survey or fishery (and not a selectivity mirror of an earlier
4372 // fleet - the shared penalty is accumulated once, on the lead fleet).
4373 if(flt_type(flt) > 0 && flt_sel_lead(flt) == 1){
4374
4375 // 1a) Ianelli/AMAK non-parametic selectivity penalties
4376 // - using non-normalized selectivities following the arrowtooth ADMB model
4377 // - updated to make differentiable using abs to only penalize when sel_ratio_tmp > 0 (decreasing sel_at_age)
4378 // - Added time-varying component following Atka mackerel
4379 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 2) {
4380
4381 // Time-invariant selectivity has one curve, so the shape penalties are
4382 // charged once. Both time-varying modes give every year its own curve,
4383 // so they are charged every year.
4384 //
4385 // PROPOSED, to make IID integrable under random_sel = TRUE: drop the
4386 // `== 1` here so IID charges terms 1, 2 and 4 once on the base curve
4387 // sel_coff. Those three are priors on the SHAPE, and under IID the
4388 // shape is the base curve; only term 3 belongs to the deviates.
4389 int nyrs_tmp = 1;
4390 if((flt_varying_sel(flt) == 1) || (flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4)){
4391 nyrs_tmp = nyrs_hind;
4392 }
4393
4394 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_tmp; yr++){
4395
4396 // 1. Decreasing selectivity penalty (over the fleet's own bins)
4397 // FIXME: AMAK starts at nbins/2
4398 //
4399 // PROPOSED (IID only): read the base curve, sel_coff(flt, sex, age),
4400 // in place of log_non_par_sel. max(d, 0)^2 has a STEP second
4401 // derivative, so charging it on the deviates steps the Laplace
4402 // log-determinant. Bound the loop at flt_n_sel_bins(flt) - 1: past
4403 // that, sel_coff holds 0 rather than the copy of the last estimated
4404 // bin the realized curve repeats, so d would be a cliff that the
4405 // fitted selectivity does not have.
4406 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4407 for(age = 0; age < (nbins - 1); age++) {
4408 Type sel_ratio_tmp = log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr) - log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age + 1, yr); // Positive if decreasing
4409 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * square( (CppAD::abs(sel_ratio_tmp) + sel_ratio_tmp)/2.0);
4410 }
4411 }
4412
4413 // 2. Curvature penalty
4414 //
4415 // PROPOSED (IID only): fill sel_tmp from sel_coff(flt, sex, age).
4416 // This term is already smooth, so it adds no kink -- it is here for
4417 // the second defect: it does not scale with sel_dev_sd, so charging
4418 // it on the deviates integrates an unnormalized prior and biases the
4419 // sd. Same for term 4.
4420 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4421 // Extract only the selectivities we want
4422 vector<Type> sel_tmp(nbins); sel_tmp.setZero();
4423
4424 for(age = 0; age < nbins; age++) {
4425 sel_tmp(age) = log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr);
4426 }
4427
4428 // Second difference computed once (matches the type-9 branch).
4429 vector<Type> sel_d2 = first_difference( first_difference( sel_tmp ) );
4430 for(int a2 = 0; a2 < sel_d2.size(); a2++) {
4431 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 1) * sel_d2(a2) * sel_d2(a2);
4432 }
4433 }
4434
4435 // 3. Time-varying penalty
4436 //
4437 // RandomWalk (4) scores the year-to-year change in the realized
4438 // log-selectivity (Atka mackerel ADMB model), which is renormalized to
4439 // mean 1 each year; the level is held by the avgsel penalty at (4).
4440 // IID (1) scores each deviation itself, over exactly the coefficient
4441 // bins build_map() estimates. Bins outside that range are fixed at 0
4442 // and left unscored: each would add log(sel_dev_sd) + 0.5*log(2*pi),
4443 // constant in the deviates but rising with the sd, so scoring them
4444 // would drag the estimate toward zero.
4445 if(flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4){
4446 if(yr > 0){
4447 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4448 for(age = 0; age < (nbins - 1); age++) {
4449 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr), log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr - 1), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4450 }
4451 }
4452 }
4453 } else if(flt_varying_sel(flt) == 1){
4454 // PROPOSED: this term is already correct and stays as it is -- it
4455 // is the only one that belongs to the random effects. If nyrs_tmp
4456 // becomes 1 for IID, it needs its own `for(int y = 0; y <
4457 // nyrs_hind; y++)` here so every hindcast year is still scored.
4458 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4459 for(int bin = bin_first_selected(flt); bin < flt_n_sel_bins(flt); bin++) {
4460 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4461 }
4462 }
4463 }
4464
4465 // 4. Survey selectivity normalization (non-parametric)
4466 //
4467 // PROPOSED (IID only): compute the level from sel_coff over
4468 // [bin_first_selected, flt_n_sel_bins) with log_mean_exp(), as the
4469 // type-9 branch already does, rather than reading the per-year
4470 // avg_sel, which includes the deviates.
4471 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4472 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += 2.0 * square(avg_sel(flt, sex, yr));
4473 }
4474 }
4475 }
4476
4477 // 1b) Non-parametric with the ADMB ("pm"/AMAK) selectivity penalty
4478 // (NonParametricPM, type 9). Construction is identical to type 2; only
4479 // the penalty differs to match ADMB's Selectivity_Likelihood:
4480 // jnll_comp(4) = ADMB sel_like(1): decreasing-only penalty,
4481 // weight sel_curve_pen(flt,0) (= ctrl_flag(13)).
4482 // jnll_comp(5) = ADMB sel_like_dev(1):
4483 // - curvature: weight sel_curve_pen(flt,1) (= ctrl_flag(11)/nch) on
4484 // the 2nd difference of log-selectivity, every year;
4485 // - random walk: bare Gaussian SSQ of the year-to-year change in
4486 // log-selectivity / (2*sd^2) (NO dnorm normalizing constant), all ages;
4487 // - dev magnitude: weight sel_curve_pen(flt,2) (= ctrl_flag(10)/group_num)
4488 // on norm2 of the year-to-year coefficient increments.
4489 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 9) {
4490
4491 int nyrs_tmp = 1;
4492 if(flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4){
4493 nyrs_tmp = nyrs_hind;
4494 }
4495
4496 // Per-fleet selectivity start year (0-based). Penalties over realized
4497 // selectivity skip pre-survey years (and the survey base-year curvature,
4498 // matching ADMB's styr-anchored base term which is 0 for a survey that
4499 // starts after styr). For a fleet starting at styr (e.g. the fishery,
4500 // start_yr = 0) this is the original behaviour.
4501 int start_yr = flt_sel_start_yr(flt);
4502 int shape_a0 = flt_sel_pen_first_bin(flt); // first (left) bin of the shape-penalty pairs
4503 if(shape_a0 < 0) shape_a0 = bin_first_selected(flt); // default: first selected bin
4504 int shape_a1 = flt_sel_pen_last_bin(flt); // last (left) bin of the shape-penalty pairs
4505 if(shape_a1 < 0) shape_a1 = nbins - 2; // default: whole range (pairs up to (nbins-2, nbins-1))
4506 // The pair is (age, age + 1), so the left bin stops one short of the
4507 // last. data_check() bounds Sel_pen_last_bin by the number of bins, so
4508 // without this a final-bin setting reads bin `nbins` -- allocated to the
4509 // widest species, never written, scoring as a phantom selected bin.
4510 if(shape_a1 > nbins - 2) shape_a1 = nbins - 2;
4511 int shape_mode = flt_sel_shape_mode(flt); // 0 = directional (sign of pen), 1 = smooth (two-sided d^2)
4512 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4513 for(yr = start_yr; yr < nyrs_tmp; yr++){
4514
4515 // (1) Shape penalty over adjacent ages [shape_a0 .. shape_a1], all active years.
4516 // mode 0 (directional, ADMB/AMAK): SIGN of sel_curve_pen(flt,0) sets
4517 // direction (>=0 penalize DECREASING, <0 penalize INCREASING), one-sided,
4518 // differentiable via (|d|+d)/2 = max(d,0) and (|d|-d)/2 = max(-d,0).
4519 // mode 1 (smooth, RTMB "rpm"): two-sided weight * d^2 smoothness.
4520 for(age = shape_a0; age <= shape_a1; age++) {
4521 Type d = log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr) - log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age + 1, yr); // > 0 if decreasing
4522 if(shape_mode == 1)
4523 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * d * d; // two-sided smoothness
4524 else if(sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) >= 0)
4525 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * square( (CppAD::abs(d) + d)/2.0 ); // penalize decreasing
4526 else
4527 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += -sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * square( (CppAD::abs(d) - d)/2.0 ); // penalize increasing
4528 }
4529
4530 // (2) Curvature (2nd-difference) penalty [ADMB term 2/3]. Includes the
4531 // base year only when the fleet starts at styr (start_yr == 0);
4532 // otherwise the survey base-year curvature is excluded (ADMB anchors
4533 // the base curvature term at styr, which is 0 pre-survey).
4534 if((yr > start_yr) || (start_yr == 0)){
4535 vector<Type> ls(nbins); ls.setZero();
4536 for(age = 0; age < nbins; age++) ls(age) = log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr);
4537 vector<Type> d2 = first_difference( first_difference( ls ) );
4538 for(int a2 = 0; a2 < d2.size(); a2++) jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 1) * d2(a2) * d2(a2);
4539 }
4540
4541 // (3) Random-walk penalty (bare SSQ, no normalizing constant) [ADMB term 4]
4542 if(yr > start_yr){
4543 for(age = 0; age < nbins; age++) {
4544 Type dd = log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr) - log_non_par_sel(flt, sex, age, yr - 1);
4545 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += dd * dd / (2.0 * sel_dev_sd(flt) * sel_dev_sd(flt));
4546 }
4547 }
4548 }
4549
4550 // (4) Dev-magnitude penalty: norm2 of the RAW per-year increments
4551 // (sel_coff_dev IS the random-walk increment for NonParametricPM;
4552 // = RTMB norm2(sel_devs)). Increments are 0 at non-change years.
4553 for(int bin = 0; bin < flt_n_sel_bins(flt); bin++){
4554 for(yr = start_yr; yr < nyrs_tmp; yr++){
4555 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 2) * sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr) * sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr);
4556 }
4557 }
4558
4559 // (5) AMAK "avgsel" base-level penalty:
4560 // weight * (log(mean(exp(base coffs))))^2 over the estimated coefficient
4561 // bins [bin_first_selected, n_sel_bins-1]. A mild regulariser that pins
4562 // the overall level of the base coefficients, which the per-year
4563 // mean-centering leaves unconstrained; equivalent to AMAK's
4564 // 10*square(avgsel_*). The weight flt_sel_avgsel_pen defaults to 0 (off);
4565 // a model opts in via Sel_avgsel_pen (e.g. 10 to match AMAK).
4566 // The range holds at least one bin: data_check() requires
4567 // Bin_first_selected <= N_sel_bins.
4568 if(flt_sel_avgsel_pen(flt) > 0){
4569 int n_base = flt_n_sel_bins(flt) - bin_first_selected(flt);
4570 vector<Type> base(n_base);
4571 for(int bin = 0; bin < n_base; bin++){
4572 base(bin) = sel_coff(flt, sex, bin + bin_first_selected(flt));
4573 }
4574 Type avgsel = log_mean_exp(base);
4575 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += flt_sel_avgsel_pen(flt) * avgsel * avgsel;
4576 }
4577 }
4578 }
4579
4580
4581 // 1c) NonParametricIntegrable (13): the Ianelli shape
4582 // priors (decreasing, curvature, average selectivity) are charged ONCE
4583 // on the base curve sel_coff, and the deviates carry a proper Gaussian
4584 // density with sel_dev_sd, so under random_sel = TRUE the Laplace
4585 // approximation integrates a density whose normalizing constant is
4586 // complete. With no deviates the objective equals NonParametric's.
4587 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 13) {
4588 int n_sel_bins = flt_n_sel_bins(flt);
4589 int start_yr = flt_sel_start_yr(flt);
4590 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4591
4592 // The base curve as selectivity.hpp builds a year without deviates:
4593 // the estimated bins, the tail held at the last estimated bin, the
4594 // whole vector centred to mean exp() of 1. Bins below the first
4595 // selected bin read the 0 that build_map() leaves in sel_coff there,
4596 // exactly as the realized curve does before the normalizer zeroes them.
4597 vector<Type> base(nbins);
4598 for(int bin = 0; bin < nbins; bin++){
4599 base(bin) = sel_coff(flt, sex, (bin < n_sel_bins ? bin : n_sel_bins - 1));
4600 }
4601 vector<Type> est(n_sel_bins);
4602 for(int bin = 0; bin < n_sel_bins; bin++) est(bin) = base(bin);
4603 Type avg_base = log_mean_exp(est);
4604 Type ctr = log_mean_exp(base);
4605 for(int bin = 0; bin < nbins; bin++) base(bin) -= ctr;
4606
4607 // 1. Decreasing-selectivity penalty on the base.
4608 for(int bin = 0; bin < (nbins - 1); bin++) {
4609 Type d = base(bin) - base(bin + 1);
4610 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * square( (CppAD::abs(d) + d)/2.0 );
4611 }
4612 // 2. Curvature penalty on the base.
4613 vector<Type> d2 = first_difference( first_difference( base ) );
4614 for(int a2 = 0; a2 < d2.size(); a2++) {
4615 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 1) * d2(a2) * d2(a2);
4616 }
4617 // 4. Average-selectivity level of the base coefficients.
4618 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_NONPARAM, flt) += 2.0 * square(avg_base);
4619
4620 // 3. The deviates: iid about the base over every hindcast year,
4621 // or random-walk increments from the year after the fleet's
4622 // start year (the start-year increment is fixed at 0). Only the
4623 // estimated coefficient bins are scored; a bin held at 0 would add
4624 // a constant rising with the sd and pull it toward zero.
4625 // With Time_varying_sel = "Off" there are no deviates and no density.
4626 bool scored = (flt_varying_sel(flt) == 1) || (flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4);
4627 int yr_lo = (flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4) ? start_yr + 1 : 0;
4628 if(scored){
4629 for(yr = yr_lo; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4630 for(int bin = bin_first_selected(flt); bin < n_sel_bins; bin++) {
4631 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4632 }
4633 }
4634 }
4635 }
4636 }
4637
4638
4639 // 2) Logistic selectivity penalties
4640 // Penalized/random effect likelihood time-varying logistic/double-logistic selectivity deviates
4641 if(((flt_varying_sel(flt) == 1)||(flt_varying_sel(flt) == 2)) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 2) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 5) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 11) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 13)){
4642 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
4643 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4644
4645 // Logistic / ascending-limb deviates (types 1, 3, 8)
4646 // For DoubleNormal (8): sel_inf_dev(0) = peak deviate, log_sel_slp_dev(0) = ascending-SD deviate
4647 if((flt_sel_type(flt) == 1) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 3) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 8)){
4648 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_inf_dev(0, flt, sex, yr), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4649 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(log_sel_slp_dev(0, flt, sex, yr), Type(0.0), 4 * sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4650 }
4651
4652 // Double logistic / descending-limb deviates (types 3, 4, 8)
4653 // For DoubleNormal (8): sel_inf_dev(1) = right-floor logit deviate; log_sel_slp_dev(1) = descending-SD deviate
4654 if((flt_sel_type(flt) == 3) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 4) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 8)){
4655 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_inf_dev(1, flt, sex, yr), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4656 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(log_sel_slp_dev(1, flt, sex, yr), Type(0.0), 4 * sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4657 }
4658 }
4659 }
4660 }
4661
4662 // Random walk:
4663 // - Type 4 = random walk on ascending and descending for double logistic
4664 // - Type 5 = ascending only for double logistics
4665 if(((flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4)||(flt_varying_sel(flt) == 5)) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 2) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 5) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 11) && (flt_sel_type(flt) != 13)){
4666 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
4667 for(yr = 1; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){ // Start at second year
4668
4669 // Logistic / ascending-limb random walk (types 1, 3, 8)
4670 if((flt_sel_type(flt) == 1) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 3) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 8)){
4671 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(log_sel_slp_dev(0, flt, sex, yr) - log_sel_slp_dev(0, flt, sex, yr-1), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4672 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_inf_dev(0, flt, sex, yr) - sel_inf_dev(0, flt, sex, yr-1), Type(0.0), 4 * sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4673 }
4674
4675 // Double logistic / descending-limb random walk (types 3, 4, 8).
4676 // Gated on mode 4 as well as the type: mode 5 (RandomWalkAscending)
4677 // varies the ascending limb ONLY, and build_map() estimates no
4678 // descending deviate under mode 5 for any selectivity type -- type 3
4679 // restricts to j = 1, and types 4 and 8 exclude mode 5 outright. Those
4680 // deviates therefore sit at their init of 0. With random_sel = FALSE
4681 // that makes the penalty a pure constant -- it shifts the reported
4682 // objective and leaves every gradient untouched. With random_sel =
4683 // TRUE, sel_dev_log_sd is estimated, so the term is 2n log(sigma) +
4684 // const and biases that SD downward.
4685 if((flt_varying_sel(flt) == 4) &&
4686 ((flt_sel_type(flt) == 3) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 4) || (flt_sel_type(flt) == 8))){
4687 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_inf_dev(1, flt, sex, yr) - sel_inf_dev(1, flt, sex, yr-1), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4688 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(log_sel_slp_dev(1, flt, sex, yr) - log_sel_slp_dev(1, flt, sex, yr-1), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt) * 4, true);
4689 }
4690 }
4691 }
4692 }
4693
4694 // 2b) LogisticPM (type 11): ADMB AMAK ("pm") bottom-trawl-survey penalties,
4695 // ctrl_flag(19) > 0 branch. Two random-walk (norm2 of first-difference)
4696 // terms, BOTH starting the year AFTER the fleet's selectivity start year
4697 // (flt_sel_start_yr) so pre-survey years and the start-year boundary jump
4698 // are excluded (ADMB's dev_vector / flat pre-survey selectivity contribute
4699 // ~0 there):
4700 // (1) RW on the REALIZED log-selectivity-at-age over the penalty
4701 // age-range [sel_norm_bin1, sel_norm_bin2] (= ADMB ctrl_flag(26) *
4702 // sum_{q_amin..q_amax-1} norm2(first_difference(log_sel_bts))),
4703 // weight sel_curve_pen(flt,0);
4704 // (2) RW on the free age-1 parameter deviates (= ADMB
4705 // 8 * norm2(first_difference(sel_age_one_bts_dev))),
4706 // weight sel_curve_pen(flt,2).
4707 // (sel_curve_pen(flt,1) is unused in this branch.)
4708 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 11){
4709 int start_yr = flt_sel_start_yr(flt); // 0-based; first first-difference is start_yr+1
4710 int alo = sel_norm_bin1(flt); int ahi = sel_norm_bin2(flt);
4711 if(alo < 0) alo = bin_first_selected(flt); // default: whole selected range
4712 if(ahi < 0) ahi = nbins - 1;
4713 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
4714 for(yr = start_yr + 1; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4715 // (1) realized log-selectivity random walk over the penalty bin-range
4716 for(age = alo; age <= ahi; age++){
4717 Type s_now = sel_is_length ? sel_at_length(flt, sex, age, yr) : sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr);
4718 Type s_prev = sel_is_length ? sel_at_length(flt, sex, age, yr - 1) : sel_at_age(flt, sex, age, yr - 1);
4719 Type d = log(s_now) - log(s_prev);
4720 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 0) * d * d;
4721 }
4722 // (2) free age-1 parameter-deviate random walk
4723 Type da1 = sel_inf_dev(1, flt, sex, yr) - sel_inf_dev(1, flt, sex, yr - 1);
4724 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += sel_curve_pen(flt, 2) * da1 * da1;
4725 }
4726 }
4727 }
4728
4729 // 3) Hake style non-parametric
4730 // Penalized/random effect likelihood time-varying non-parametric (Taylor et al 2014) selectivity deviates
4731 if(((flt_varying_sel(flt) == 1) || (flt_varying_sel(flt) == 2)) && (flt_sel_type(flt) == 5)){
4732 for(int bin = 0; bin < flt_n_sel_bins(flt); bin++){ //NOTE: extends beyond selectivity age range, but should be mapped to 0 in map function
4733 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++){
4734 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4735 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr), Type(0.0), sel_dev_sd(flt), true);
4736 }
4737 }
4738 }
4739 }
4740
4741
4742 // 4) 2D AR1
4743 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 6){
4744 int n_sel_bins = flt_n_sel_bins(flt);
4745 array<Type> tmp_AR2(n_sel_bins, nyrs_hind);
4746
4747
4748 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
4749 for (int bin = 0; bin < n_sel_bins; bin++) {
4750 for (int yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
4751 tmp_AR2(bin, yr) = sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr);
4752 }
4753 }
4754
4755 Type rho_a = rho_trans(sel_curve_pen(flt, 0)); // Scale from -1 to 1
4756 Type rho_y = rho_trans(sel_curve_pen(flt, 1));
4757
4758 Type Sigma_sig_sel = pow(pow(sel_dev_sd(flt),2) / ((1-pow(rho_y,2))*(1-pow(rho_a,2))),0.5);
4759 // As in the M 2D-AR1 above: SEPARABLE(f, g) puts f on the outermost
4760 // dimension. tmp_AR2 is (bin, year), so year leads and bin follows.
4761 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += SCALE(SEPARABLE(AR1(rho_y),AR1(rho_a)), Sigma_sig_sel)(tmp_AR2);
4762 } // end sex loop
4763 }
4764
4765 // 5) 3D AR1
4766 if(flt_sel_type(flt) == 7){
4767 // Build bin-year index
4768 int n_sel_bins = flt_n_sel_bins(flt);
4769 int num_rows = n_sel_bins * nyrs_hind;
4770 matrix<Type> ay_index(num_rows, 2);
4771
4772 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
4773
4774 int row = 0;
4775 for (int year = 1; year <= nyrs_hind; ++year) {
4776 for (int bin = 1; bin <= n_sel_bins; ++bin) {
4777 ay_index(row, 0) = bin;
4778 ay_index(row, 1) = year;
4779 row++;
4780 }
4781 }
4782
4783 // -- Define precision matrix for GMRF
4784 Eigen::SparseMatrix<Type> Q_sparse(num_rows, num_rows); // Precision matrix
4785
4786 // -- Construct precision matrix
4787 // Argument order is bin, year, cohort. construct_Q()'s own parameter
4788 // names read the other way round, but its `age > 1` branch (previous
4789 // bin, same year) multiplies the FIRST argument, and this ay_index is
4790 // filled (bin, year) -- the mirror of WHAM's -- so the two inversions
4791 // cancel. Do not "correct" this call to match those names.
4792 Q_sparse = construct_Q(nyrs_hind, n_sel_bins, ay_index,
4793 sel_curve_pen(flt, 0), sel_curve_pen(flt, 1), sel_curve_pen(flt, 2), // natural scale
4794 log(square(sel_dev_sd(flt))), 0); // Conditional variance
4795
4796
4797 // --- Derive likelihood
4798 array<Type> tmp_AR2(n_sel_bins, nyrs_hind);
4799 for (int bin = 0; bin < n_sel_bins; bin++) {
4800 for (int yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
4801 tmp_AR2(bin, yr) = sel_coff_dev(flt, sex, bin, yr);
4802 }
4803 }
4804 jnll_comp(JNLL_SEL_DEV, flt) += GMRF(Q_sparse)(tmp_AR2);
4805 }
4806 }
4807 }
4808 } // End selectivity loop
4809
4810
4811 // Slot 6-7 -- Catchability
4812 // Fleets sharing a Q_index estimate one catchability and one deviate vector,
4813 // so only the lead fleet accumulates the prior and deviate penalties.
4814 for(flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
4815 if(flt_q_lead(flt) == 1){
4816
4817 // Lognormal prior on catchability: Catchability_init is the mean of q when
4818 // bias_adjust_proc = 1, the median when 0.
4819 if( est_index_q(flt) == 2){
4820 jnll_comp(JNLL_Q_PRIOR, flt) -= dnorm(index_log_q(flt), index_log_q_prior(flt) - bias_adjust_proc*square(index_q_sd(flt))/2.0, index_q_sd(flt), true);
4821 }
4822
4823 // Penalized/random deviate likelihood
4824 if(((index_varying_q(flt) == 1) || (index_varying_q(flt) == 2)) // - Time_varying_q = 1 (IID) or 2 (AR1, retired -- scored as IID)
4825 && (flt_type(flt) > 0) && // - If survey or fishery CPUE
4826 ((est_index_q(flt) == 1) || (est_index_q(flt) == 2))){ // - Catchability = 1 (Estimated) or 2 (Estimated-with-prior)
4827 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4828 jnll_comp(JNLL_Q_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(index_q_dev(flt, yr), Type(0.0), index_q_dev_sd(flt), true );
4829 }
4830 }
4831
4832 // Random walk
4833 if((index_varying_q(flt) == 4) && // - Time_varying_q = 4 (RandomWalk)
4834 (flt_type(flt) > 0) && // - If survey or fishery CPUE
4835 ((est_index_q(flt) == 1) || (est_index_q(flt) == 2))) // - Catchability = 1 (Estimated) or 2 (Estimated-with-prior)
4836 {
4837 for(yr = 1; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++){
4838 jnll_comp(JNLL_Q_DEV, flt) -= dnorm(index_q_dev(flt, yr) - index_q_dev(flt, yr-1), Type(0.0), index_q_dev_sd(flt), true );
4839 }
4840 }
4841 } // End q lead gate
4842 } // End q loop
4843
4844
4845 // Slots 8-11 -- Recruitment
4846 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
4847 penalty = 0.0;
4848 // Input numbers-at-age (estDynamics > 0) leave R a placeholder, so no SRR
4849 // prior, Bmsy penalty or curve penalty.
4850 int srr_terms_on = (estDynamics(sp) == 0);
4851
4852 // Slot 9 -- stock-recruit prior for Beverton
4853 // -- Lognormal on steepness. srr_prior is its mean when bias_adjust_proc = 1
4854 // (centred at -sigma^2/2, as rec_dev), its median when 0.
4855 if(srr_terms_on && (srr_est_mode == 2) & ((srr_pred_fun == 2) | (srr_pred_fun == 3))){
4856 jnll_comp(JNLL_SRR_PRIOR, sp) -= dnorm(log(steepness(sp, 0)), log(srr_prior(sp)) - bias_adjust_proc*square(srr_prior_sd(sp))/2.0, srr_prior_sd(sp), true);
4857 }
4858
4859 // -- Beta
4860 if(srr_terms_on && (srr_est_mode == 3) & ((srr_pred_fun == 2) | (srr_pred_fun == 3))){
4861 // Convert mean and SD to beta params
4862 Type beta_alpha = ((1 - srr_prior(sp))/ square(srr_prior_sd(sp)) - 1/srr_prior(sp)) * square(srr_prior(sp));
4863 Type beta_beta = beta_alpha * (1/srr_prior(sp) - 1);
4864 jnll_comp(JNLL_SRR_PRIOR, sp) -= dbeta(steepness(sp, 0), beta_alpha, beta_beta, true);
4865 }
4866
4867 // Slot 9 -- stock-recruit prior for Ricker, lognormal on alpha. srr_prior is alpha's
4868 // mean when bias_adjust_proc = 1, its median when 0.
4869 if(srr_terms_on && (srr_est_mode == 2) & ((srr_pred_fun == 4) | (srr_pred_fun == 5))){
4870 jnll_comp(JNLL_SRR_PRIOR, sp) -= dnorm(rec_pars(sp, 1), log(srr_prior(sp)) - bias_adjust_proc*square(srr_prior_sd(sp))/2.0, srr_prior_sd(sp), true);
4871 }
4872
4873 // Slot 9 -- penalty for Bmsy > Bmsy_lim for Ricker
4874 if(srr_terms_on && (!isNA(Bmsy_lim(sp))) && ((srr_pred_fun == 4) || (srr_pred_fun == 5))){ // Using pred_fun in case ianelli method is used
4875 Type bmsy = 1.0/exp(rec_pars(sp, 2));
4876 bmsy = posfun(Bmsy_lim(sp)/Type(1000000.0) - bmsy, Type(0.001), penalty);
4877 jnll_comp(JNLL_SRR_PRIOR, sp) += 100 * penalty;
4878 }
4879
4880
4881 // Slot 9 -- init_dev -- Initial abundance-at-age
4882 // Lognormal bias correction: dev ~ N(-sigma^2/2, sigma) so E[N_init] = deterministic equilibrium.
4883 // initMode 5 (OffsetEquilibrium) fixes init_dev at 0 (off), like the
4884 // equilibrium modes, so it carries no init_dev penalty.
4885 if(initMode > 1 && initMode != 5){
4886 for(age = 1; age < nages(sp); age++) {
4887 jnll_comp(JNLL_INIT_DEV, sp) -= dnorm( init_dev(sp, age - 1), -bias_adjust_proc*square(R_sd(sp))/2.0, R_sd(sp), true);
4888 }
4889 }
4890
4891 // Slot 10 -- Tau -- Annual recruitment deviation
4892 // Lognormal bias correction: dev ~ N(-sigma^2/2, sigma) so E[R] = R0 (mean-unbiased).
4893 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
4894 jnll_comp(JNLL_REC_DEV, sp) -= dnorm( rec_dev(sp, yr), -bias_adjust_proc*square(R_sd(sp))/2.0, R_sd(sp), true); // Recruitment deviation using random effects.
4895 }
4896
4897 // Slot 11 -- Additional penalty for SRR curve (sensu AMAK/Ianelli). R_hat is the mean of R
4898 // when bias_adjust_proc = 1 (Ianelli's pm.tpl, Dorn 2002), the median (AMAK) when 0.
4899 if(srr_terms_on && (srr_fun == 0) & (srr_pred_fun > 0)){
4900 for(yr = srr_hat_styr; yr <= srr_hat_endyr; yr++) {
4901 jnll_comp(JNLL_SRR_PENALTY, sp) -= dnorm( log(R(sp, yr)), log(R_hat(sp,yr)) - bias_adjust_proc*square(R_sd(sp))/2.0, R_sd(sp), true);
4902 }
4903 }
4904 }
4905
4906
4907 // Slot 12 -- Reference point penalties
4908 // -- CMSY
4909 Type CMSY = 0;
4910
4911 // --- Sum terminal catch across species
4912 if(HCR == 1){
4913
4914 // -- Loop through catch data
4915 for(fsh_ind = 0; fsh_ind < catch_ctl.rows(); fsh_ind++){
4916
4917 flt = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 0) - 1;
4918 sp = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 1) - 1;
4919 flt_yr = catch_ctl(fsh_ind, 2);
4920
4921 // Add fishery data from terminal year
4922 if((flt_type(flt) == 1) && (forecast(sp) == 1) && (estDynamics(sp) == 0)){
4923 if(flt_yr == projyr){
4924 CMSY += catch_hat(fsh_ind);
4925 }
4926 }
4927 }
4928
4929 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, 0) = - square(CMSY/1000000.0); // CMSY is ll
4930
4931
4932 // --- Add biomass_depletion constraint
4933 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
4934 if((forecast(sp) == 1) && (estDynamics(sp) == 0)){
4935 penalty = 0.0;
4936 Type nothing_useful = posfun( (ssb_depletion(sp, nyrs-1) - Plimit(sp)), Type(0.0001), penalty); (void) nothing_useful;
4937 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 500.0 * square(CMSY/1000.0) * penalty; // CMSY
4938 }
4939 }
4940 }
4941
4942
4943 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
4944 // -- Single-species static reference points
4945 if((DynamicHCR == 0) && (forecast(sp) == 1) && (msmMode == 0) && (estDynamics(sp) == 0)){
4946
4947 // -- Avg F (have F limit)
4948 if(HCR == 2){
4949 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRlimit(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Flimit_percent(sp));
4950 }
4951
4952 // F that acheives \code{Ftarget}% of SSB0 in the end of the projection
4953 if(HCR == 3){
4954 // Depletion target: realized SSB in the final projection year against SB0.
4955 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((ssb(sp, nyrs-1)/SB0(sp, nyrs-1))-Ftarget_percent(sp));
4956 }
4957
4958 // -- SPR
4959 if(HCR > 3){
4960 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRlimit(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Flimit_percent(sp));
4961 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRtarget(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Ftarget_percent(sp));
4962 }
4963 }
4964
4965 // -- Single-species dynamic reference points
