4966 if((DynamicHCR == 1) && (forecast(sp) == 1) && (msmMode == 0) && (estDynamics(sp) == 0)){
4967
4968 // -- Avg F (have F limit)
4969 if(HCR == 2){
4970 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRlimit(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Flimit_percent(sp));
4971 }
4972
4973 for(yr = 1; yr < nyrs; yr++){ // No initial abundance
4974 // F that acheives Ftarget% of SSB0y
4975 if(HCR == 3){
4976 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((DynamicSBF(sp, yr)/DynamicSB0(sp, yr))-Ftarget_percent(sp));
4977 }
4978 }
4979
4980 // -- SPR
4981 if(HCR > 3){
4982 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRlimit(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Flimit_percent(sp));
4983 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((SPRtarget(sp)/SPR0(sp))-Ftarget_percent(sp));
4984 }
4985 }
4986
4987
4988 // -- Multi-species static reference points (all biomass_depletion based)
4989 if((forecast(sp) == 1) && (msmMode > 0) && (estDynamics(sp) == 0)){
4990
4991 // -- Avg F (have F limit)
4992 if(HCR == 2){
4993 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((ssb(sp, nyrs-1)/SB0(sp, nyrs-1))-Flimit_percent(sp));
4994 }
4995
4996 // F that achieves \code{Ftarget}% of SSB0 in the end of the projection
4997 if(HCR == 3){
4998 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((ssb(sp, nyrs-1)/SB0(sp, nyrs-1))-Ftarget_percent(sp));
4999 }
5000
5001 // Tiered HCRs with Limit and Targets
5002 if(HCR == 6){
5003 jnll_comp(JNLL_REFPT_PENALTY, sp) += 200*square((ssb(sp, nyrs-1)/SB0(sp, nyrs-1))-Flimit_percent(sp));
5004 }
5005 }
5006 }
5007
5008
5009 // Slot 13 -- N-at-age < 0 penalty. See "posfun"
5010 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++){
5011 if(estDynamics(sp) == 0){
5012 jnll_comp(JNLL_ZERO_N_PENALTY, sp) += zero_N_pen(sp);
5013 }
5014 }
5015
5016
5017 // Slots 14-15 -- M PRIORS AND RANDOM EFFECTS
5018 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
5019
5020 // -------------------------------------------------------------
5021 // PRIORS (Slot 14)
5022 // -------------------------------------------------------------
5023 // M1_model 0 = use fixed natural mortality from M1_base
5024 // 1 = estimate sex- and age-invariant M1_at_age,
5025 // 2 = sex-specific (two-sex model), age-invariant M1_at_age
5026 // 3 = estimate sex- and age-specific M1_at_age.
5027
5028 // Lognormal prior on M: M_prior is its mean when bias_adjust_proc = 1, its median
5029 // when 0. The log-scale centre is computed once per species, outside the age loop.
5030 Type M_prior_mean = log(M_prior(sp)) - bias_adjust_proc*square(M_prior_sd(sp)) / 2.0;
5031
5032 // Prior on M1_at_age only
5033 if( (M1_use_prior(sp) == 1) && (M2_use_prior(sp) == 0) ) {
5034 // Determine loop bounds dynamically based on M1_model
5035 int nsex_tmp = (M1_model(sp) > 1) ? nsex(sp) : 1;
5036 int nage_tmp = (M1_model(sp) == 3) ? nages(sp) : 1;
5037
5038 for(int sex = 0; sex < nsex_tmp; sex++) {
5039 for(int age = 0; age < nage_tmp; age++) {
5040 jnll_comp(JNLL_M_PRIOR, sp) -= dnorm(log_M1(sp, sex, age), M_prior_mean, M_prior_sd(sp), true);
5041 }
5042 }
5043 }
5044
5045 // Prior on total M_at_age (M1_at_age and M2_at_age)
5046 // FIXME: sex-specific prior?
5047 if( M2_use_prior(sp) == 1 ) {
5048 for(int sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex++) {
5049 for(int age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
5050 for(int yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
5051 jnll_comp(JNLL_M_PRIOR, sp) -= dnorm(log(M_at_age(sp, sex, age, yr)), M_prior_mean, M_prior_sd(sp), true);
5052 }
5053 }
5054 }
5055 }
5056
5057
5058 // -------------------------------------------------------------
5059 // RANDOM EFFECTS LIKELIHOOD (Slot 15)
5060 // -------------------------------------------------------------
5061 // M1 random effects are applied to each species if M1_model = 1 or each species AND sex if M1_model = 2.
5062 // Variance and correlation coefficients are species-specific, but sex-invariant.
5063 // - M1_re = 0: No random effects (default).
5064 // - M1_re = 1: Random effects varies by age, but uncorrelated (IID) and constant over years.
5065 // - M1_re = 2: Random effects varies by year, but uncorrelated (IID) and constant over ages.
5066 // - M1_re = 3: Random effects varies by year and age, but uncorrelated (IID).
5067 // - M1_re = 4: Correlated AR1 random effects varies by age, but constant over years.
5068 // - M1_re = 5: Correlated AR1 random effects varies by year, but constant over ages.
5069 // - M1_re = 6: Correlated 2D-AR1 random effects varies by year and age.
5070
5071 // Determine how many sexes to run REs for (only add 2nd sex if M1_model == 2)
5072 int num_re_sexes = (M1_model(sp) == 2 && nsex(sp) > 1) ? 2 : 1;
5073
5074 // M1_re = 1/4: Random effects varies by age (IID or AR1) and constant over years.
5075 if( (M1_re(sp) == 1) || (M1_re(sp) == 4) ) {
5076 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
5077 Type rho_M_a = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 0));
5078 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / (1.0 - pow(rho_M_a, 2)), 0.5);
5079 vector<Type> M_re_age(nages(sp));
5080
5081 for(int sex = 0; sex < num_re_sexes; sex++) {
5082 for(int age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
5083 M_re_age(age) = log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, 0);
5084 }
5085 jnll_comp(JNLL_M_RE, sp) += SCALE(AR1(rho_M_a), Sigma_M)(M_re_age);
5086 }
5087 }
5088
5089 // M1_re = 2/5: Random effects varies by year (IID or AR1) and constant over ages.
5090 if( (M1_re(sp) == 2) || (M1_re(sp) == 5) ) {
5091 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
5092 Type rho_M_y = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 1));
5093 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / (1.0 - pow(rho_M_y, 2)), 0.5);
5094 vector<Type> M_re_yr(nyrs_hind);
5095
5096 for(int sex = 0; sex < num_re_sexes; sex++) {
5097 for(int yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
5098 M_re_yr(yr) = log_M1_dev(sp, sex, 0, yr);
5099 }
5100 jnll_comp(JNLL_M_RE, sp) += SCALE(AR1(rho_M_y), Sigma_M)(M_re_yr);
5101 }
5102 }
5103
5104 // M1_re = 3/6: Random effects varies by age and year (IID or 2D-AR1)
5105 if( (M1_re(sp) == 3) || (M1_re(sp) == 6) ) {
5106 Type sigma_M = exp(M1_dev_log_sd(sp, 0));
5107 Type rho_M_a = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 0));
5108 Type rho_M_y = rho_trans(M1_rho(sp, 0, 1));
5109 Type Sigma_M = pow(pow(sigma_M, 2) / ((1.0 - pow(rho_M_y, 2)) * (1.0 - pow(rho_M_a, 2))), 0.5);
5110 array<Type> M_re_a_yr(nages(sp), nyrs_hind);
5111
5112 for(int sex = 0; sex < num_re_sexes; sex++) {
5113 for(int age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
5114 for(int yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
5115 M_re_a_yr(age, yr) = log_M1_dev(sp, sex, age, yr);
5116 }
5117 }
5118 // SEPARABLE(f, g) applies f to the OUTERMOST array dimension and g to
5119 // the fastest-running one (TMB density.hpp). The array is
5120 // (age, year), so the year correlation goes first and the age
5121 // correlation second -- written the other way round, rho_M_a would
5122 // correlate over years and rho_M_y over ages.
5123 jnll_comp(JNLL_M_RE, sp) += SCALE(SEPARABLE(AR1(rho_M_y), AR1(rho_M_a)), Sigma_M)(M_re_a_yr);
5124 }
5125 }
5126 }
5127
5128
5129 // Slot 19 -- Linkage-table priors on the natural scale.
5130 // Priors are specified using natural-scale parameter names (R0,
5131 // alpha, M1, K, ...). For (Intercept) rows, so transform before
5132 // evaluating the prior. For all slope
5133 // rows, b_nat == b (the coefficient IS on the natural / linear scale).
5134 //
5135 // Families:
5136 // 0 = none -- no contribution
5137 // 1 = normal -- dnorm(b_nat, p1, p2) prior on natural-scale value
5138 // 2 = lognormal -- dnorm(log(b_nat), p1 - bias_adjust_proc*p2^2/2, p2); exp(p1) = mean if bias_adjust_proc = 1, median if 0
5139 // 3 = gamma -- dgamma(b_nat, p1, 1/p2) prior on natural-scale value
5140 // 4 = beta -- dbeta(b_nat, p1, p2) prior on natural-scale value
5141 //
5142 // Most (Intercept) rows are mapped out (beta_linkage(i) stays at 0); for
5143 // those rows the prior is evaluated against the *base parameter*
5144 // (`rec_pars`, `log_M1`, `log_growth_pars`) instead of beta_linkage. The
5145 // recruitment `R_init` intercept has no base parameter and stays estimable,
5146 // so its prior is read on beta_linkage(i) like a slope.
5147 for (int i = 0; i < beta_linkage.size(); ++i) {
5148 int fam = linkage_prior_family(i);
5149 if (fam == 0) continue;
5150 Type p1 = linkage_prior_p1(i);
5151 Type p2 = linkage_prior_p2(i);
5152 int slot_col = linkage_species(i) - 1;
5153 if (slot_col < 0) slot_col = 0; // shared/all => column 0
5154 if (slot_col >= n_col) slot_col = 0;
5155
5156 Type b = beta_linkage(i);
5157 // Whether the intercept's base parameter lives on the log scale (so
5158 // b_nat = exp(b)). True for every log-scale base (rec_pars, log_M1,
5159 // log_growth_pars, index_log_q, comp_weights); set false for a
5160 // natural-scale base (the selectivity inflection sel_inf), whose prior is
5161 // read on the natural scale directly.
5162 bool base_is_log = true;
5163 if (linkage_is_intercept(i) == 1) {
5164 // Re-target the prior to the base parameter that this intercept
5165 // row stands in for. Sentinel 0 in species/sex/age_bin means
5166 // "all levels"; pick the first concrete cell as the prior target
5167 // (in practice intercepts are stratified per species/sex/age and
5168 // there is a single base-parameter scalar per row).
5169 int sp_in = linkage_species(i);
5170 int sx_in = linkage_sex(i);
5171 int ab_in = linkage_age_bin(i);
5172 int sp_idx = (sp_in == 0) ? 0 : (sp_in - 1);
5173 int sx_idx = (sx_in == 0) ? 0 : (sx_in - 1);
5174 int ab_idx = (ab_in == 0) ? 0 : (ab_in - 1);
5175
5176 int proc = linkage_process(i);
5177 int param = linkage_param(i);
5178 if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_RECRUIT) {
5179 // recruitment params: R0=0, alpha=1, beta=2 -> rec_pars cols 0..2
5180 // (stored as log_R0, log_alpha, log_beta on the log scale). R_init (3)
5181 // has NO rec_pars column -- its intercept IS the level, so the prior
5182 // stays on beta_linkage(i) and reading rec_pars here would run off the
5183 // end of the matrix.
5184 if (param != RCEATTLE_REC_R_INIT) {
5185 b = rec_pars(sp_idx, param);
5186 }
5187 } else if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_M) {
5188 b = log_M1(sp_idx, sx_idx, ab_idx);
5189 } else if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_GROWTH) {
5190 // growth params: K=0, L1=1, Linf=2, m=3 -> log_growth_pars(sp, sx, param)
5191 // SD endpoints: sd_L1=4, sd_Linf=5 -> growth_log_sd(sp, sx, param - N_GROWTH)
5192 if (param < RCEATTLE_N_GROWTH_PARAMS) {
5193 b = log_growth_pars(sp_idx, sx_idx, param);
5194 } else {
5195 b = growth_log_sd(sp_idx, sx_idx, param - RCEATTLE_N_GROWTH_PARAMS);
5196 }
5197 } else if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_Q) {
5198 // Catchability is fleet- not species-indexed. The intercept
5199 // stands in for the base log-catchability index_log_q(fleet).
5200 int fl_in = linkage_fleet(i);
5201 int fl_idx = (fl_in == 0) ? 0 : (fl_in - 1);
5202 b = index_log_q(fl_idx);
5203 } else if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_COMP) {
5204 // Dirichlet-multinomial overdispersion. comp/caal weights are
5205 // fleet-indexed, diet weights predator(species)-indexed; all stored on
5206 // the log scale (theta = exp(weight)), so b_nat = exp(b) is the natural
5207 // DM scalar the prior targets. param: theta_comp=0, theta_caal=1,
5208 // theta_diet=2.
5209 int fl_in = linkage_fleet(i);
5210 int fl_idx = (fl_in == 0) ? 0 : (fl_in - 1);
5211 if (param == 0) b = comp_weights(fl_idx);
5212 else if (param == 1) b = caal_weights(fl_idx);
5213 else if (param == 2) b = diet_comp_weights(sp_idx);
5214 } else if (proc == RCEATTLE_PROC_SEL) {
5215 // Parametric selectivity base parameters are (slot, fleet, sex).
5216 // param: slp_asc=0 / slp_desc=1 -> log_sel_slp (log scale, exp -> slope);
5217 // inf_asc=2 / inf_desc=3 -> sel_inf (natural scale, the
5218 // inflection age / peak). asc -> slot 0, desc -> slot 1. The
5219 // (Intercept) beta_linkage row is pinned at 0, so it adds no
5220 // offset to selectivity -- the base parameter carries the mean
5221 // and this prior regularizes it (Cole Monnahan's GOA pollock
5222 // selectivity priors: lognormal on the log-slope, normal on the
5223 // natural inflection). coff (param 4) has no scalar base
5224 // parameter and cannot carry a linkage (see
5225 // .check_sel_linkage_support), so it is not reachable here.
5226 int fl_in = linkage_fleet(i);
5227 int fl_idx = (fl_in == 0) ? 0 : (fl_in - 1);
5228 int slot = param % 2; // asc -> 0, desc -> 1
5229 if (param == 0 || param == 1) {
5230 b = log_sel_slp(slot, fl_idx, sx_idx);
5231 } else if (param == 2 || param == 3) {
5232 b = sel_inf(slot, fl_idx, sx_idx);
5233 base_is_log = false; // inflection is natural-scale, not log
5234 } else if (param == 5) {
5235 // apical: the per-sex multiplier, stored logged, so the prior reads
5236 // on the multiplier itself (lognormal centred on 1 = no offset).
5237 b = log_sel_apical(fl_idx, sx_idx);
5238 } else if (param >= 6 && param <= 11) {
5239 // DoubleNormalSS3: the prior reads the parameter as stored, on SS3's
5240 // own scale (peak in cm, P3/P4 log widths, P2/P5/P6 logits), which
5241 // is where an SS3 control file puts its priors.
5242 b = sel_dn6(param - 6, fl_idx, sx_idx);
5243 base_is_log = false;
5244 }
5245 }
5246 }
5247
5248 // Back-transform to natural scale when this is
5249 // an intercept row on a log-scale base parameter (b holds the log-scale
5250 // parameter). For all slope rows, and for a natural-scale intercept base
5251 // (sel_inf), b_nat == b already.
5252 Type b_nat = (linkage_is_intercept(i) == 1 && base_is_log) ? exp(b) : b;
5253
5254 if (fam == 1) { // normal(p1, p2) on natural scale
5255 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dnorm(b_nat, p1, p2, true);
5256 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dnorm(b_nat, p1, p2, true);
5257 } else if (fam == 2) { // lognormal on log(b_nat); exp(p1) = mean when bias_adjust_proc = 1, median when 0
5258 // For a log-scale intercept base: log(b_nat) = b (efficient form avoids
5259 // log(exp(b))). A natural-scale intercept base (sel_inf) takes log(b_nat).
5260 Type log_b_nat = (linkage_is_intercept(i) == 1 && base_is_log) ? b : log(b_nat);
5261 Type mu_log = p1 - bias_adjust_proc * square(p2) / 2.0;
5262 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dnorm(log_b_nat, mu_log, p2, true);
5263 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dnorm(log_b_nat, mu_log, p2, true);
5264 } else if (fam == 3) { // gamma(p1=shape, p2=rate) on natural scale
5265 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dgamma(b_nat, p1, Type(1.0)/p2, true);
5266 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dgamma(b_nat, p1, Type(1.0)/p2, true);
5267 } else if (fam == 4) { // beta(p1=shape1, p2=shape2) on natural scale
5268 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dbeta(b_nat, p1, p2, true);
5269 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, slot_col) -= dbeta(b_nat, p1, p2, true);
5270 }
5271 }
5272
5273
5274 // 13.2. Diet likelihood components
5275 // Simulated stomach contents go to this copy, not into the REPORTed diet_obs
5276 // -- see the _sim naming rule in section 5.12b. Stomachs the model does not fit
5277 // keep the observed values they were copied with.
5278 matrix<Type> diet_sim = diet_obs;
5279
5280 if((msmMode > 2) || (imax(suitMode) > 0)) {
5281
5282 int current_j = 0; // Track position in diet_ctl
5283
5284 for (int i = 0; i < n_stomach_obs; ++i) {
5285
5286 // Take this stomach's prey as the run of diet_ctl rows with stomach_id ==
5287 // i. The cursor only moves forward, so the ids must be sorted 0, 1, 2, ...
5288 // with no gaps. clean_data() guarantees that -- it rebuilds stomach_id
5289 // from the pred/sex/age/year stratum and sorts by it on every pass, so a
5290 // fit never sees anything else -- and data_check() rejects a table that
5291 // breaks it for anyone validating one directly. Out of that order the
5292 // cursor runs past whole stomachs, which then drop out of the likelihood
5293 // silently, and build_osa_data(), which matches on which(stomach_id == i),
5294 // would disagree with this scan.
5295 int start_j = current_j;
5296 while((current_j < diet_ctl.rows()) && (stomach_id(current_j) == i)) {
5297 current_j++;
5298 }
5299
5300 // --- Process the predator if suitability is estimated and data are available
5301 // Test the empty run first: start_j can sit one past the last row, where
5302 // reading diet_ctl / diet_obs would be out of bounds.
5303 int n_prey = current_j - start_j;
5304 if (n_prey == 0) continue;
5305
5306 int rsp = diet_ctl(start_j, 0) - 1;
5307 Type N_s = diet_obs(start_j, 0);
5308
5309 if (suitMode(rsp) <= 0) continue;
5310
5311 // -- Pre-allocate TMB vectors with space for "Other prey" (+1)
5312 vector<Type> obs_diet_prop(n_prey + 1); obs_diet_prop.setZero();
5313 vector<Type> pred_diet_prop(n_prey + 1); pred_diet_prop.setZero();
5314
5315 for (int k = 0; k < n_prey; ++k) {
5316 obs_diet_prop(k) = diet_obs(start_j + k, 1);
5317 pred_diet_prop(k) = diet_hat(start_j + k, 1);
5318 }
5319
5320 // --- Add in "Other prey" ---
5321 Type sum_obs_p = obs_diet_prop.head(n_prey).sum();
5322 if (sum_obs_p > 1.0) sum_obs_p = 1.0;
5323 obs_diet_prop(n_prey) = 1.0 - sum_obs_p;
5324
5325 Type sum_est_p = pred_diet_prop.head(n_prey).sum();
5326 pred_diet_prop(n_prey) = posfun(1.0 - sum_est_p, Type(0.00001), penalty); // Making it differentiable (cant do if statement)
5327
5328 // Vectorized Offset & Normalization. Uses the same configurable proportion
5329 // offset (DATA_SCALAR comp_offset, default 1e-5) as the age/length comps,
5330 // so fitting and the diet OSA obsvec stay consistent.
5331 obs_diet_prop += comp_offset;
5332 pred_diet_prop += comp_offset;
5333
5334 obs_diet_prop /= obs_diet_prop.sum();
5335 pred_diet_prop /= pred_diet_prop.sum();
5336
5337 // Convert observed prop to observed numbers
5338 vector<Type> obs_diet_content = obs_diet_prop * N_s;
5339
5340 Type stomach_log_likelihood = 0;
5341 Type unweighted_stomach_log_likelihood = 0;
5342 Type DM_diet_par = DM_diet_pars(rsp);
5343
5344 // Calculate alpha parameters.
5345 vector<Type> diet_alphas = pred_diet_prop * N_s * DM_diet_par;
5346 vector<Type> unweighted_diet_alphas = pred_diet_prop * N_s; // For "unweighted" likelihood (DM_diet_par = 1)
5347
5348 // Likelihood
5349 if(osa_mode == 0){
5350 // ---- Normal fitting: weighted density read from diet_obs (unchanged) ----
5351 switch(diet_ll_type(rsp)){
5352
5353 case 0: // Full multinomial
5354 stomach_log_likelihood = dmultinom(obs_diet_content, pred_diet_prop, true);
5355
5356 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= stomach_log_likelihood;
5357 jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= diet_comp_weights(rsp) * stomach_log_likelihood;
5358 break;
5359 case 1: // Dirichlet-multinomial
5360 // Calculate the log-likelihood
5361 stomach_log_likelihood = ddirmultinom(obs_diet_content, diet_alphas, true);
5362 unweighted_stomach_log_likelihood = ddirmultinom(obs_diet_content, unweighted_diet_alphas, true);
5363
5364 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= unweighted_stomach_log_likelihood;
5365 jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= stomach_log_likelihood;
5366 break;
5367
5368 default:
5369 error("Invalid 'diet_ll_type'");
5370 }
5371 } else {
5372 // ---- OSA build: unweighted, keep-gated conditional density read from
5373 // obsvec. The diet composition for a stomach is its prey items plus an
5374 // "other prey" category (the last bin, fixed by sum-to-1 and dropped).
5375 // diet_obsvec_idx gives the obsvec start for this stomach. ----
5376 int start = diet_obsvec_idx(i);
5377 if(start >= 0){
5378 vector<Type> osa_x = obsvec.segment(start, n_prey + 1);
5379 if(diet_ll_type(rsp) == 1){ // Dirichlet-multinomial (fitted DM par)
5380 // No CDF term: the beta-binomial has no elementary one (comp_osa.hpp).
5381 jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= ddirmultinom_osa(osa_x, diet_alphas, keep.segment(start, n_prey + 1), 1, 1);
5382 } else { // multinomial
5383 jnll_comp(JNLL_STOMACH, rsp) -= dmultinom_osa(osa_x, pred_diet_prop, keep.segment(start, n_prey + 1), 1, 1, osa_mode == 2);
5384 }
5385 }
5386 }
5387
5388 // -- Simulate the stomach contents, for sim_mod(simulate = TRUE) --
5389 // Drawn under the same family and from the same predicted proportions and
5390 // concentration the density above uses.
5391 //
5392 // The composition is this stomach's prey plus the "other prey" balance, so
5393 // the draw covers n_prey + 1 bins. Only the prey bins are written back:
5394 // "other prey" is defined as whatever is left over and is recomputed from
5395 // the prey proportions on the next fit, so storing it would double-count.
5396 SIMULATE {
5397 // Draw from the composition BEFORE the offset, rebuilt here from
5398 // diet_hat so ordinary fitting pays nothing for it. The offset keeps
5399 // log(0) out of the density rather than describing the stomachs, and the
5400 // density's transform is affine, so drawing from the un-offset
5401 // prediction is what keeps a simulate-then-refit round trip unbiased.
5402 vector<Type> sim_p(n_prey + 1);
5403 Type prey_sum = 0.0;
5404 for(int k = 0; k < n_prey; k++){
5405 sim_p(k) = diet_hat(start_j + k, 1);
5406 prey_sum += sim_p(k);
5407 }
5408 sim_p(n_prey) = (prey_sum < Type(1.0)) ? Type(1.0) - prey_sum : Type(0.0);
5409 Type sim_tot = sim_p.sum();
5410 if(sim_tot > Type(0)) sim_p /= sim_tot;
5411
5412 if((N_s > Type(0)) && (sim_tot > Type(0))){
5413 vector<Type> sim_counts(n_prey + 1);
5414 switch(diet_ll_type(rsp)){
5415 case 0: {
5416 // The multinomial density is multiplied by diet_comp_weights, which
5417 // makes it an effective sample size: weighting a multinomial
5418 // log-likelihood by w is (up to a constant) a multinomial at w*N.
5419 // Draw at that size, or a down-weighted fleet gets stomachs the
5420 // likelihood treats as w times less informative than they are.
5421 // (For the Dirichlet-multinomial the same parameter is log theta and
5422 // already enters through the concentration below.)
5423 Type n_eff = N_s * diet_comp_weights(rsp);
5424 sim_counts = rmultinom_rce(n_eff, sim_p);
5425 break;
5426 }
5427 case 1: {
5428 vector<Type> sim_alphas = sim_p * N_s * DM_diet_par;
5429 sim_counts = rdirmultinom_rce(N_s, sim_alphas);
5430 break;
5431 }
5432 default:
5433 error("Invalid 'diet_ll_type'");
5434 }
5435 // Divide by the number of observations actually PLACED, not by N_s.
5436 // rmultinom_rce rounds N_s to a whole number, so with a fractional
5437 // sample size the prey proportions would otherwise sum to
5438 // round(N_s)/N_s > 1 -- and data_check() rejects a stomach summing
5439 // above 1, which self_test() then reports as a failed replicate rather
5440 // than as bad data.
5441 //
5442 // A stomach whose weighted sample size rounds to zero places nothing,
5443 // and comes back EMPTY rather than carrying its observed proportions
5444 // over -- the same rule the composition draw follows (section 5.9).
5445 // Keeping the observed values would hand the refit the real diet under
5446 // a weight that says the stomach is worth less than one observation,
5447 // and a self_test() would then score suitability recovery against data
5448 // it was never asked to simulate.
5449 Type n_drawn = sim_counts.sum();
5450 for(int k = 0; k < n_prey; k++){
5451 diet_sim(start_j + k, 1) = (n_drawn > Type(0))
5452 ? sim_counts(k) / n_drawn
5453 : Type(0);
5454 }
5455 }
5456 }
5457 }
5458 }
5459
5460 // Reported under a _sim name -- see the naming rule in section 5.12b. Equal to
5461 // diet_obs for a model with no diet likelihood, where nothing above is drawn.
5462 SIMULATE {
5463 matrix<Type> diet_obs_sim = diet_sim;
5464 REPORT(diet_obs_sim);
5465 }
5466
5467
5468 // Diet likelihood components for Kinzey and Punt predation
5469 /*
5470 if(msmMode > 2){
5471 // Slot 15 -- Ration likelihood
5472 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
5473 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
5474 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
5475 for(age = 1; age < nages(sp); age++) { // don't include age zero in likelihood
5476 if(ration(sp, sex, age, yr) > 0){
5477 if(ration_hat(sp, sex, age, yr) > 0){
5478 jnll_comp(JNLL_RATION, sp) -= dnorm(log(ration(sp, sex, age, yr)) - square(sd_ration) / 2, log( ration_hat(sp, sex, age, yr)), sd_ration, true);
5479 }
5480 }
5481 }
5482 }
5483 }
5484 }
5485
5486
5487 // Slot 16 -- Ration penalalties FIXME: not sure if necessary: talk to Andre
5488 for(sp = 0; sp < nspp; sp++) {
5489 for(sex = 0; sex < nsex(sp); sex ++){
5490 for(age = 0; age < nages(sp); age++) {
5491 for(yr = 0; yr < nyrs_hind; yr++) {
5492 if(ration_hat(sp, sex, age, yr) > 0){
5493 //jnll_comp(JNLL_RATION_PENALTY, sp) += 20 * pow(ration_hat(sp, sex, age, yr) - ration_hat_ave(sp, sex, age), 2);
5494 }
5495 }
5496 }
5497 }
5498 }
5499 } // End if statement for Kinzey diet likelihood
5500 */
5501
5502

5504 // - Only comp and diet comp use data weights!
5505 for(flt = 0; flt < n_col; flt++){
5506 for(int ind = 0; ind < 19; ind++){
5507 if((ind!= 2) & (ind != 18)){
5508 unweighted_jnll_comp(ind, flt) = jnll_comp(ind, flt);
5509 }

5550 // -- Secondary display series, so add_ci = TRUE can draw an interval at all.
5551 // Natural scale ONLY: exploitable_biomass sums over fisheries alone, so it is
5552 // exactly 0 for a survey-only species or proj_F_prop = 0, and the depletions
5553 // divide by B0 / SB0. log() of either puts -Inf on the tape and NaNs the whole
5554 // sdreport. The plotters recover sd(log x) = sd(x)/x instead.
5555 ADREPORT( exploitable_biomass );

5559 // -- Log-scale derived series.
5560 // sdreport linearizes once about the MLE, so its SD is exact only for a linear
5561 // function of the parameters. These are built multiplicatively (R = R0 *
5562 // exp(rec_dev); n-at-age is a product of survivals), so log(x) is near-linear
5563 // where x is exponential, and exp(log(x) +/- z * sd) is right-skewed and cannot
5564 // cross zero. The log SD is also the CV, the form the ABC / OFL buffer wants.
5565 // The natural-scale ADREPORTs are kept so existing sdrep$value callers work.
5566 matrix<Type> log_biomass = biomass; log_biomass = log(biomass.array());
5567 matrix<Type> log_ssb = ssb; log_ssb = log(ssb.array());
5568 matrix<Type> log_R = R; log_R = log(R.array());
5569 REPORT( log_biomass );
5570 REPORT( log_ssb );
5571 REPORT( log_R );
5572 ADREPORT( log_biomass );
5573 ADREPORT( log_ssb );
5574 ADREPORT( log_R );
5575 ADREPORT( R_sd );
5576 ADREPORT( R );
5577
5578 // -- Log selectivity-at-age, for a delta-method interval on the curve. Log and
5579 // not logit, because the non-parametric forms normalize to a MEAN of one, so
5580 // sel_at_age routinely exceeds one. Gated because the delta method costs every
5581 // reported value against every parameter; see ?fit_control.
5582 //
5583 // Only estimated, age-based lead fleets, from their first selected bin: those
5584 // are the cells that cannot be a structural zero, and one log(0) = -Inf on the
5585 // tape turns EVERY quantity in the sdreport to NaN, biomass and SSB included.
5586 // The four routes to a structural zero are enumerated in ?fit_control; all are
5587 // read from the data, so the reported SET never depends on a parameter value.
5588 // A reported VALUE still can underflow -- a narrow dome puts exp(-x^2/2) below
5589 // 1e-308 many bins from its peak -- so the log is floored. max2() is exact
5590 // above the floor, so nothing a fleet would report is altered.
5591 //
5592 // log_sel_at_age_index carries the fleet, sex, absolute age and calendar year
5593 // of each row, since which cells are reported depends on the model.
5594 if(adreport_sel == 1){
5595 // First bin and bin count per fleet. data_check() bounds Bin_first_selected
5596 // by nages, but a 0 in the workbook still arrives here as -1, and the model
5597 // builds safebounds = FALSE, so both ends are clamped before indexing.
5598 vector<int> sel_first_bin(n_flt); sel_first_bin.setZero();
5599 vector<int> sel_rep_bins(n_flt); sel_rep_bins.setZero();
5600 for(int flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
5601 if((flt_type(flt) <= 0) || (flt_sel_lead(flt) != 1) ||
5602 (flt_sel_type(flt) == 0) || (flt_sel_dim(flt) == 1)) continue;
5603 int n_age = nages(flt_spp(flt));
5604 int first = bin_first_selected(flt);
5605 if(first < 0) first = 0;
5606 if(first > n_age) first = n_age;
5607 sel_first_bin(flt) = first;
5608 sel_rep_bins(flt) = n_age - first;
5609 }
5610
5611 int n_sel = 0;
5612 for(int flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
5613 n_sel += nsex(flt_spp(flt)) * sel_rep_bins(flt) * nyrs_hind;
5614 }
5615
5616 vector<Type> log_sel_at_age(n_sel); log_sel_at_age.setZero();
5617 matrix<Type> log_sel_at_age_index(n_sel, 4); log_sel_at_age_index.setZero();
5618
5619 int i_sel = 0;
5620 for(int flt = 0; flt < n_flt; flt++){
5621 if(sel_rep_bins(flt) == 0) continue;
5622 int sel_sp = flt_spp(flt);
5623 for(int sel_sex = 0; sel_sex < nsex(sel_sp); sel_sex++){
5624 for(int sel_age = sel_first_bin(flt); sel_age < nages(sel_sp); sel_age++){
5625 for(int sel_yr = 0; sel_yr < nyrs_hind; sel_yr++){
5626 log_sel_at_age(i_sel) = log(max2(sel_at_age(flt, sel_sex, sel_age, sel_yr),
5627 Type(1e-300)));
5628 log_sel_at_age_index(i_sel, 0) = Type(flt + 1);
5629 log_sel_at_age_index(i_sel, 1) = Type(sel_sex + 1);
5630 log_sel_at_age_index(i_sel, 2) = Type(minage(sel_sp) + sel_age);
5631 log_sel_at_age_index(i_sel, 3) = Type(styr + sel_yr);
5632 i_sel++;
5633 }
5634 }
5635 }
5636 }
5637
5638 REPORT( log_sel_at_age );
5639 REPORT( log_sel_at_age_index );
5640 ADREPORT( log_sel_at_age );
5641 }

5735
5736 // -- 14.6a. Random-effect SD priors (jnll_comp row 19). A prior on a group's
5737 // deviation SD, routed from linkage_spec(priors = list(sigma = ...)). Applied
5738 // once per group (not per level -- the loop is over groups, so the "once"
5739 // property is structural). Shares the linkage-prior row and the same families
5740 // as the fixed-beta prior loop above, on the natural-scale SD exp(log_sigma).
5741 // FIXME(jacobian): the normal/gamma/beta families place the prior on the
5742 // natural-scale SD while the free parameter is log_sigma, WITHOUT the change-
5743 // of-variables Jacobian d(sd)/d(log_sigma) = sd. This is a penalized-likelihood
5744 // prior, not a proper Bayesian prior on the SD (it matches the existing
5745 // fixed-beta prior loop's convention). `lognormal` is exempt: dnorm(log(sd),..)
5746 // has a constant Jacobian w.r.t. log_sigma. Add `+ log_sigma` to the log-prior
5747 // for the natural-scale families if a proper density is wanted.
5748 if (log_sigma_linkage.size() > 0) {
5749 for (int g = 0; g < log_sigma_linkage.size(); ++g) {
5750 int fam = linkage_re_sigma_prior_family(g);
5751 if (fam == 0) continue;
5752 Type sd = exp(log_sigma_linkage(g));
5753 Type p1 = linkage_re_sigma_prior_p1(g);
5754 Type p2 = linkage_re_sigma_prior_p2(g);
5755 if (fam == 1) { // normal(p1, p2) on the SD
5756 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(sd, p1, p2, true);
5757 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(sd, p1, p2, true);
5758 } else if (fam == 2) { // lognormal on the SD; exp(p1) = mean when bias_adjust_proc = 1, median when 0
5759 Type mu_log = p1 - bias_adjust_proc * square(p2) / 2.0;
5760 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(log(sd), mu_log, p2, true);
5761 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(log(sd), mu_log, p2, true);
5762 } else if (fam == 3) { // gamma(shape, rate)
5763 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dgamma(sd, p1, Type(1.0)/p2, true);
5764 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dgamma(sd, p1, Type(1.0)/p2, true);
5765 } else if (fam == 4) { // beta(shape1, shape2)
5766 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dbeta(sd, p1, p2, true);
5767 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dbeta(sd, p1, p2, true);
5768 }
5769 }
5770 }
5771
5772 // -- 14.6a'. Random-effect AR1 correlation priors (jnll_comp row 19), routed
5773 // from linkage_spec(priors = list(rho = ...)) on an ar1 group. On the natural
5774 // (-1, 1) correlation rho = rho_trans(trans_rho_linkage): normal(p1, p2)
5775 // directly, or beta(p1, p2) on (rho + 1) / 2. Once per group.
5776 // FIXME(jacobian): as with the sigma priors above, the prior is on the natural
5777 // rho while the free parameter is trans_rho_linkage, without the rho_trans
5778 // Jacobian -- a penalized-likelihood prior, not a proper density on rho.
5779 if (trans_rho_linkage.size() > 0) {
5780 for (int g = 0; g < linkage_re_rho.size(); ++g) {
5781 int fam = linkage_re_rho_prior_family(g);
5782 if (fam == 0) continue;
5783 Type rho = rho_trans(trans_rho_linkage(linkage_re_rho(g)));
5784 Type p1 = linkage_re_rho_prior_p1(g);
5785 Type p2 = linkage_re_rho_prior_p2(g);
5786 if (fam == 1) { // normal(p1, p2) on rho
5787 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(rho, p1, p2, true);
5788 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dnorm(rho, p1, p2, true);
5789 } else if (fam == 4) { // beta(p1, p2) on (rho + 1) / 2
5790 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dbeta((rho + Type(1)) / Type(2), p1, p2, true);
5791 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_PRIOR, 0) -= dbeta((rho + Type(1)) / Type(2), p1, p2, true);
5792 }
5793 }
5794 }
5795
5796 // -- 14.6b. Random-effect linkage density (jnll_comp row 20)
5797 // Group-oriented so each covariance structure couples its deviations
5798 // correctly. For each RE group, gather its slot-space deviations in ascending
5799 // slot order -- which the registry assigns in real elapsed-time order -- then
5800 // dispatch on the group's structure:
5801 // us (IID) : sum of N(0, sigma) densities (the index_q_dev idiom);
5802 // rw (RandomWalk) : N(0, sigma) on successive first differences, the first
5803 // deviate pinned at 0 by the map (as legacy index_q_dev);
5804 // ar1 (AR1) : stationary AR1 with MARGINAL SD sigma and correlation
5805 // rho = rho_trans(trans_rho_linkage), the glmmTMB /
5806 // Rogers-QAR1 convention SCALE(AR1(rho), sigma).
5807 // Guarded on size so row 20 stays exactly 0 for every model without a random
5808 // linkage. Placed before REPORT(jnll_comp) so the reported matrix reflects
5809 // the density that jnll_comp.sum() also carries.
5810 if (log_sigma_linkage.size() > 0) {
5811 int n_re = beta_linkage_re_all.size();
5812 for (int grp = 0; grp < log_sigma_linkage.size(); ++grp) {
5813 Type sigma = exp(log_sigma_linkage(grp));
5814 // Collect this group's slots in slot (= time) order.
5815 int len = 0;
5816 for (int g = 0; g < n_re; ++g) if (linkage_re_sigma(g) == grp) len++;
5817 if (len == 0) continue;
5818 vector<Type> re(len), obs(len);
5819 vector<int> obs_mask(len), obs_slot(len);
5820 int j = 0;
5821 for (int g = 0; g < n_re; ++g) if (linkage_re_sigma(g) == grp) {
5822 obs(j) = linkage_re_obs_value(g); re(j) = beta_linkage_re_all(g);
5823 obs_mask(j) = linkage_re_obs_mask(g); obs_slot(j) = g; j++;
5824 }
5825
5826 int st = linkage_re_struct(grp);
5827 if (st == 1) { // rw / RandomWalk
5828 for (int t = 1; t < len; ++t) {
5829 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= dnorm(re(t) - re(t - 1), Type(0), sigma, true);
5830 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= dnorm(re(t) - re(t - 1), Type(0), sigma, true);
5831 }
5832 } else if (st == 2) { // ar1 / first-order AR
5833 // Stationary AR1 with marginal SD sigma and correlation rho. SCALE(...)
5834 // returns the negative log density, so it is ADDED (unlike the -= dnorm
5835 // forms). Reduces to the IID sum at rho = 0.
5836 Type rho = rho_trans(trans_rho_linkage(linkage_re_rho(grp)));
5837 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) += SCALE(AR1(rho), sigma)(re);
5838 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) += SCALE(AR1(rho), sigma)(re);
5839 } else { // us / IID (default)
5840 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= sum(dnorm(re, Type(0), sigma, true));
5841 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= sum(dnorm(re, Type(0), sigma, true));
5842 }
5843
5844 // Rogers QAR1 observation: the ar1 latent re(t) is measured as
5845 // linkage_re_obs_value(t) with SD exp(log_obs_sd_linkage(obs_slot)). The
5846 // observation SD is ESTIMATED (one per observed group, matching the
5847 // reference Estimate_q = 6 / GOApollock), started from the spec's obs_sd.
5848 // This term pins the latent to the observed env series and, with the beta
5849 // scaling in beta_linkage_eff, identifies the effect size.
5850 if (linkage_re_obs(grp) >= 0) {
5851 Type osd = exp(log_obs_sd_linkage(linkage_re_obs(grp)));
5852 for (int t = 0; t < len; ++t) {
5853 if (obs_mask(t) == 0) continue; // year absent from env_data: latent exists, but no observation
5854 if (osa_mode == 0) {
5855 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= dnorm(obs(t), re(t), osd, true);
5856 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= dnorm(obs(t), re(t), osd, true);
5857 } else {
5858 // OSA: read the covariate observation from obsvec, keep-gated, so
5859 // oneStepPredict() residualizes it against the latent AR1 state re(t)
5860 // (WHAM's Ecov OSA). build_osa_data() lays each observed slot in.
5861 int pos = linkage_re_obsvec_idx(obs_slot(t));
5862 if (pos >= 0) {
5863 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), re(t), osd, true);
5864 unweighted_jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= keep(pos) * dnorm(obsvec(pos), re(t), osd, true);
5865 // method = "cdf": the covariate measurement is normal about the
5866 // latent state, so its CDF is pnorm of the standardized residual.
5867 // Only jnll_comp, as at every other CDF site: unweighted_jnll_comp
5868 // is reported as an unweighted LIKELIHOOD (Francis and
5869 // McAllister-Ianelli read it), and a CDF term is not one. This row
5870 // is one of the few that keeps its own value -- the wholesale copy
5871 // in section 13.4 runs `ind < 19`, so rows 19 and 20 are never
5872 // overwritten, and it executes before this block in any case.
5873 if (osa_mode == 2) {
5874 jnll_comp(JNLL_LINKAGE_RE, 0) -= osa_norm_cdf_terms(
5875 obsvec(pos), re(t), osd, keep.cdf_lower(pos), keep.cdf_upper(pos));
5876 }
5877 }
5878 }
5879 }
5880 }
5881 }
5882 }

5943 /** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
5944 // 15. END MODEL //
5945 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
5946
5947 Type jnll = 0;
5948
5949 // Modes 0-3 return the real objective. Mode 3 builds the TMB object without
5950 // running the optimizer, so obj$fn()/obj$gr() are usable for diagnostics.
5951 if(estimateMode < 4) {
5952 jnll = jnll_comp.sum();
5953 }
5954
5955 // Mode 4: build_map() maps out every hindcast parameter, leaving `dummy` as
5956 // the only free parameter. Placeholder objective so nlminb has something
5957 // valid to minimize -- a plumbing smoke test, not a likelihood.
5958 if(estimateMode > 3) {
5959 jnll = dummy * dummy;
5960 }
5961
5962
5963 REPORT( jnll );
5964 return jnll;
5965}

5967/** ------------------------------------------------------------------------ //
5968 // 16. CHANGE LOG //
5969 // ------------------------------------------------------------------------- //
5970 // Changes from 2017 assessment
5971 // 1. Normalize age-transition matrix prior to use (PCod rows did not sum to 1)
